units.la: ON immerito Græ- cum illum Poëtā laudauit Nazianzenus, qui recta, commodáque rerum initia columnas aureas appellabat. Vt enim nisi firma fundamenta iaciantur, superuacanea est, & inutilis ædificatio: ita vix vllus laborum nostrorum fructus sperari potest, nisi conuenientibus & aptis initiis nitantur: nec fœlix progressus expectandus est, nisi fausta initia præcesserint. Cùm igitur ea fidei dogmata, quæ sunt inter nos & Pontificios controuersa, Theologicè simul, & Scholastice tractanda existimarem: vt ita Monachorum effrænatas declamationes tanquam in gyrum accuratæ & Theologicæ disputationis ducerentur (si modò ab illis id obtineri queat) initium fecimus à loco de Verbo Dei scripto aduersus humanas tra-
units.tr: Not undeservedly did Gregory of Nazianzus praise that Greek poet who called right and fitting beginnings of things golden pillars. For just as no building is worth anything unless firm foundations are laid, so scarcely any fruit of our labours can be hoped for unless they rest on suitable and apt beginnings, and no happy progress can be expected unless favourable beginnings have gone before. Since I judged that the doctrines of faith which are in dispute between us and the Papists should be treated both theologically and scholastically, so that the unbridled declamations of the monks might be brought, as it were, into the round of an accurate and theological disputation (if indeed they can be brought to this), I began with the topic of the written Word of God against human tradi-

units.la: * ƨ ditiones: eamque nos disputationem anno superiore propositum, vt esset firmissimum reliquarum omnium disputationum fundamentum. Nam hoc pacto nobis visi sumus sequentibus tractationibus columnas aureas suffulcire, si quum de fidei capitibus agitur, primum omnium, ipsi Dei verbo, quo vno fides nostra fundanda & constituenda est, sua constaret authoritas. Nunc autem vt super hoc præstantissimum fundamentum (liceat enim nobis hæc Apostolica verba vsurpare) aurum, argentum, & lapides pretiosos ædificemus: hoc est, dogmata cum verbo Dei consentanea proferamus: ecce, proponimus locum de Vnico Christi sacerdotio & sacrificio, inter alios Theologiæ locos celeberrimum, & quo præcipuum salutis nostræ caput continetur. Huc enim redit summa totius huiusce disputationis, vt intelligamus, quænam & quanta sit efficacitas, qui fructus, & quæ merita mortis ac passionis Iesu Christi Ecclesiæ Redemptoris, & æterni, ac solius Sacerdotis noui Testamenti: qui semetipsum in cruce semel tradidit, & obtulit Deo pro peccatis nostris: & qui (vt aliquando scite ac vere dixit Augustinus) orat pro nobis, vt sacerdos noster: orat in nobis, vt caput nostrum: oratur à nobis, vt Deus noster. Quæ omnia si, vt par est, ex verbo Dei definiantur: facile cognoscemus, quid sit tum sacerdotium Christi, tum ipsius sacrificium: ne nobis Pontificij suorum sophismatum captionibus fucum faciant. Enimuero, vt mirum maximè, ita quoque maximè doledum est, eousque dolos & fallacias Satanæ procedere potuisse, vt omnes prope veterum Ethnicorum ritus ab Apostolis damnatos, explososque, mutatis tantum nominibus in vsum reuocauerit: & retento Christi nomine, veram Christi cognitionem, adeóque Christum ipsum, quoad eius fieri potuit, ex animis hominum delerit. Sic enim Romanus Pontifex, dum Christi vicarius salutatur, reipsa ille est ἀντικείμενος, de quo locutus est Apostolus: sic Episcopi nomine tenus Apostolorum successores, reipsa doctrinam Apostolorum totis viribus oppugnant: sic illi ipsi Pontificij splendido & augusto nomine Ecclesiæ Catholicæ gloriantes, veram & verè Catholicam Ecclesiam, & pios quoslibet Diuini verbi puritatem amplexos, totos iam annos septuaginta crudeliter insectantur. Longum esset iter ad omnia, quæ, & aliud tempus, & longiorem orationem desiderant. Sed, vt in rem præsentem veniamus: nónne ipsâ Missæ sacrificium (aduersus quod instituta hæc nostra est disputatio) ipsius Christi sacrificio tantas offudit tenebras, vt præcipuum hoc fidei caput pro pè in obliuionem abierit? Nónne istud hominum commentum (quæ est humanæ superstitionis fœcunditas) in tot & tam multiplices cæremonias, tot gestus, tot signa: tot denique, tantaque, scilicet, mysteria penitus abstrusa, ac ne ipsis quidem Pontificiis sacerdotibus cognita, tandem excreuit: vt tibi videaris in Numæ schola & in veterum Pontificum Romanorum collegio, potius quàm in Apostolorum doctrina, & in Ecclesia Christiana versari? Nam quid commemorem variam Missalis sacerdotis actione, variósque gestus ac motus corporis in suo illo sacrificio ctificio crificio peragendo ? Nunc enim rectū, nunc incuruum, nunc se in orbem versantem, quandoque in medio orbe subsistentem, sæpe stantem, nonnunquam tardè inambulantem videas: brachiis modò patsis, modò contractis, nunc sublatis, nunc depresis: digitis verò in designandis crucibus perpetuò occupatis: sæpe apud se tacitè loquentem, nūc alios (quos tamen ne conspectu quidē dignatur) alta voce compellantem: aliquoties pani & calici insusurrantem, aliquando etiam dormitantem, tum autem excitatum, alta deinde suspiria ducentem, & continuò in cantum clarissimum erumpentem. Hæc & sexcenta eiusmodi (quæ libens prætermisi, ac ne hæc quidem dicturus, nisi me res ipsa coëgisset) quid, obsecro, commune habent, vel cum sanctissimo sacrificio, quod Christus semel fecit, pro nobis moriens: vel, cum sacro Cœnæ Dominicæ mysterio? Atqui hoc esse Christi sacrificium, & hanc esse Cœnam Domini, Pontificij nobis, scilicet, affirmant: similiterque faciunt, ut siquis tabulam exesam & vetustate consumptā situque squalidam, pro re ad viuum suis coloribus exprefla nobis obtruderet. Nec vero in hanc errorum voraginem Maiores nostri statim præcipites ruerunt: Sed ea fuit astutia Satanæ, vt pedetentim homines in errorem pellexerit: donec tandem eos in istud cæremoniarum ac superstitionum pelagus demerserit. Quinetiam, quod magis mirum videri debeat, ipsorum quoque proborum hominum studio & diligentia abusus est, & sanctum eorum propositum, piósque conatus in contraria partem omnino conuertit. Etenim cûm sacrificij nomen priscis illis temporibus sanctissimum, tam apud Gentiles, quàm apud Iudæos haberetur, nec crederetur vlla fine sacrificio religio esse posse: atque etiam plerisque inuisi essent Christiani, quòd externa sacrificia sustulissent: huic rei vt remedium adhiberent, operæpretium sibi visi sunt facturi Maiores nostri, fi testarentur, Christianam Ecclesiam non esse fine sacrificio: quippe quæ vnico, eodémque perfectissimo Christi sacrificio in cruce facto, cuius sacrificij virtus est perpeperpetua, frueretur. Iam quia sanctissi-mi illius sacrificij memoria in sacrę Coenæ Dominicæ mysterio celebratur: vulgò obtinuit, vt Coena Domini, sacrificium vocaretur: vt ita Veteres significarent, nullam esse causam quamobrem Iudæi & Gentiles abhorrerent ab Ecclesia Christiana, tanquam omnibus sacrificiis destituta: cũ potius illa longè præstantissimo sacrificij genere freta esset. Cum enim vnici sacrificij semel pro nobis in cruce facti memoriam identidem celebraret, & spirituale sacrificium laudis & gratiarum actionis, adeóque se totam Deo per Christum offerret: iniquissimum erat obiicere: nulla esse sacrificia in Ecclesia Christiana; quæ solet per Christum offerre Deo sacrificia, vt spiritualia, ita maximè noui Testamenti temporibus accommodata. Atque hoc quidè fuisse Maiorum nostrorum consilium, si velimus replicare memoriam temporum, cum ex aliis Veterum scriptis, tum ex apologiis nomine Christianorum editis, perspicuum esse poterit. Verùm enimuero, vt ingenium est hominum, ab rebus spiritualibus procliue ad res ex- ternas & crassiores: glisc​ente in dies superstitione, coaceruatis erroribus, & puriore doctrina sensim obsolescente: res tandem eò deuenit, vt post multa annorum secula, sacra Domini Cœna fuerit in crassum externúmque sacrificium commutata: Pastores qui Ecclesiam docebant in sacrificulos conuersi: prædicatio Verbi Dei, in sacerdotum mussitantium susurrationes: mensæ, in altaria: communio, in vnius sacerdotis actionem, qui, cæteris omnibus à tergo relictis, ad se vnum pascendū maximopere intentus est. Ac nequid forte ad transformationem deesse videretur, ipsa etiā elementa, ipsas rerum substantias in hoc Missę sacrificio commutari, &, vt illi quidem loqui solent, transsubstantiari, posterioribus seculis Pontificij tradiderunt. Itaque quum Ecclesiæ Apostolicæ facies esset adeò immutata, deformatáq; & sanctissima Apostolorū instituta, (quoad eius fieri potuit) versa, euersaque omnia: quid mirum, si in crassissimis errorū & ignorantiæ tenebris homines iampridē versati sint? units.tr: tions: and I set out this disputation last year, so that it might be the firmest foundation for all the remaining disputations. In this way we thought we were propping up the golden pillars for the treatises that follow, if, when the articles of faith are handled, the authority of God's own Word, on which alone our faith is to be grounded and established, stood firm first of all. Now, that we may build gold, silver and precious stones upon this most excellent foundation (for we may use these words of the Apostle), that is, that we may put forward doctrines consistent with the Word of God, behold, we propose the topic of the one priesthood and sacrifice of Christ, the most celebrated of the theological topics and the one in which the chief head of our salvation is contained. For the sum of this whole disputation comes back to this: that we may understand what and how great is the efficacy, what the fruit and what the merits of the death and passion of Jesus Christ, the Redeemer of the Church and the eternal and sole priest of the New Testament, who once offered himself on the cross and gave himself up to God for our sins, and who (as Augustine once aptly and truly said) prays for us as our priest, prays in us as our head, and is prayed to by us as our God. If all these things are defined from the Word of God, as is fitting, we shall easily recognise both what the priesthood of Christ is and what his sacrifice is, lest the Papists deceive us with the snares of their sophisms. Indeed, as it is most wonderful, so it is most to be lamented, that the deceits and frauds of Satan have been able to advance so far that he has revived for use almost all the rites of the ancient heathens which the Apostles condemned and rejected, merely under changed names; and, while the name of Christ is retained, he has blotted out from men's minds the true knowledge of Christ, and Christ himself so far as that was possible. For thus the Roman Pontiff, while he is hailed as Christ's vicar, is in fact that adversary [ἀντικείμενος] of whom the Apostle spoke; thus bishops, successors of the Apostles in name only, in fact assail the doctrine of the Apostles with all their might; thus those same Papists, glorying in the splendid and majestic name of the Catholic Church, have for seventy years now cruelly harried the true and truly Catholic Church, and any pious persons who have embraced the purity of the divine Word. It would be a long road to cover all these things, which need another time and a longer discourse. But, to come to the matter at hand: has not the sacrifice of the Mass itself (against which this our disputation is set up) cast such darkness over the sacrifice of Christ himself that this chief article of faith has almost passed into oblivion? Has not that human invention (such is the fecundity of human superstition) grown at last into so many and such manifold ceremonies, so many gestures, so many signs, and finally so many and so great mysteries, deeply hidden and not even known to the Papist priests themselves, that you would seem to be living in the school of Numa and in the college of the ancient Roman Pontiffs, rather than in the teaching of the Apostles and in the Christian Church? For why should I mention the varied actions of the priest at Mass and the various gestures and movements of his body in performing that sacrifice? For now you may see him standing upright, now bowed, now turning himself round, now standing in the middle of the circle, often standing still, sometimes walking slowly to and fro; with his arms now outstretched, now folded, now raised, now lowered; with his fingers constantly busy in making crosses; often speaking softly to himself, now addressing others in a loud voice (whom, however, he does not even deign to look at); at times murmuring over the bread and the cup, at times even dozing, then waking, then drawing deep sighs, and at once breaking out into a very loud chant. These things, and six hundred others of the same kind (which I gladly pass over, and would not mention even these, had the matter itself not compelled me), what, I ask you, do they have in common either with that most holy sacrifice which Christ made once for all, dying for us, or with the sacred mystery of the Lord's Supper? And yet the Papists assert to us that this is the sacrifice of Christ and this is the Lord's Supper; and they do just as if someone were to thrust upon us a panel eaten away and consumed by age, filthy with grime, in place of a thing painted to the life in its own colours. Nor did our forefathers at once rush headlong into this whirlpool of errors; but it was Satan's cunning to draw men into error little by little, until at last he had plunged them into that sea of ceremonies and superstitions. Moreover, what ought to seem more wonderful still, he abused even the zeal and diligence of good men themselves, and turned their holy purpose and pious endeavours wholly to the opposite side. For when in those early times the name of sacrifice was held most sacred, both among the Gentiles and among the Jews, and it was believed that no religion could exist without sacrifice; and when moreover Christians were hated by most people because they had abolished external sacrifices: our forefathers thought it would be worth their while, in order to apply a remedy to this matter, to bear witness that the Christian Church is not without sacrifice, since she enjoys the one and the same most perfect sacrifice of Christ, made on the cross, whose virtue is perpetual. Now, because the memory of that most holy sacrifice is celebrated in the mystery of the sacred Lord's Supper, it became common usage that the Lord's Supper should be called a sacrifice; so that the ancients might signify that there was no cause why Jews and Gentiles should shrink from the Christian Church as if it were destitute of all sacrifices, when rather it was endowed with a far more excellent kind of sacrifice. For since it repeatedly celebrated the memory of the one sacrifice made once for us on the cross, and offered up the spiritual sacrifice of praise and thanksgiving, and so offered itself wholly to God through Christ, it was most unjust to object that there were no sacrifices in the Christian Church; for the Church does offer to God through Christ sacrifices which are spiritual, and which are therefore especially suited to the times of the New Testament. And that this was indeed the counsel of our forefathers may be clear, if we wish to recall the memory of those times, both from other writings of the ancients and from the apologies published in the name of Christians. But truly, as is the nature of men, they moved readily from spiritual things to external and grosser ones; superstition grew day by day, errors piled up, and purer doctrine gradually fell into disuse; and so at last things came to the point where, after many centuries, the holy Lord's Supper had been changed into a gross and external sacrifice; the ministers who taught the Church had been turned into little sacrificers; the preaching of the Word of God had become the muttering whispers of priests; the table had become an altar; the communion had become the action of a single priest, who, with all the others left behind him, is intent above all on feeding himself alone. And lest anything should seem to be missing from this transformation, the Papists in later centuries taught that the very elements, the very substances of things, are changed in this sacrifice of the Mass, and, as they are wont to say, transubstantiated. Therefore, since the face of the Apostolic Church was so greatly changed and deformed, and the most holy institutions of the Apostles were (so far as that could be done) turned upside down, and everything overthrown: what wonder is it if men have long since been immersed in the thickest darkness of error and ignorance? units.la: Postquam enim animæ salus huic vni cōmētitio sacrificio fuit alligata: & infausta illa dogmata, De fide implicita, &, De opere operato simul recepta sunt: adeò creuit hominum tum stupiditas, tum insciţia, vt iam etiā nescirēt, se nescire: quū res sacras ignorare magnæ virtutis, & imprimis Catholicæ fidei esse ducerent. Placuit igitur, & nimis placuit hominibus, hæc Religionis exercendæ facillima ratio, vt huic tam affabre fabricato sacrificio, hoc est, pōpæ deliciis refertissimæ frequentes interessent: videntes quidem mirificas cęremonias, & peregrinorū verborum strepitum audientes: sed nihil eorū quę fiebant, & quę dicebantur, intelligetes. Scilicet, hoc satis supérq. fuit, præsentes adesse, mirari, audire & murmurantibus sacerdotibus, alio vicissim strepitu admurmurare: quum persuasum haberent, se illo opere operato (vt loquūtur) seruari, & otiosos, ac propemodum nihil tale cogitantes, in cœlestem hæreditatem, quasi huiusce sacrificij quadrigis suauissimè vectos, commigrare. Tanta fuit Satanæ, patris mendacij, hominibus illudentis efficacitas:nimirum Deo contemptum sui verbi, & hominum ingratitudinem pœnis,vt iustissimis, ita grauissimis vlcíscente. Nunc autem,quum tam crassi ac fœdi errores, illucente Dei veritate, redarguuntur, exclamant Pontificij: indignum facinus! omnia miscéri, Ecclesiam ruere, pietatem extingui: maximam porrò fieri rebus diuinis,ipsíq.religioni Christianæ iniuriam, quum aliquid Missæ detrahitur: solé denique é mūdo tolli, si Missæ sacrificium tollatur. Sed cūm agnoscamus vnicum Christi sacrificiū factum in cruce pro peccatis nostris, & in illo spem salutis nostræ collocemus:cūm illius sacrificij memoriam ex ipsius Christi instituto in sacra Domini Cœna,summa cum reuerentia,celebremus: deniq. cūm corpus & sanguiné Christi vera fide nos recipere profiteamur,in remissionem peccatorum & vitam æternam: obsecro vos Pontificij,cur nos tanquam hæreticos, & sacrificij Christi inimicos damnatis?eam scilicet ob causam,quòd vestræ Missæ additamenta,vestrásque cæremonias, tum ridiculas,tum absurdas,tum etiam verbo Dei contrarias repudiemus.Vos autē: cur apertę veritati resistitis, nec veremini planos expressosque Scriptu rę locos de vnico Christi sacerdotio & sacrificio, toties à nostris inculcatos, frigidis & insulsis cauillationibus eludere? Nimirū egregie cōfirmatis quod Augustinus de errore disserens, his pene verbis: Duo sunt (ait) quæ in errore hominum difficillimè tolerantur : præsumptio, priusquàm veritas pateat: &, quum iam patuerit, præsumptæ defensio falsitatis. Quo minus ferenda est Monachorum Pseudonymorum audacia: qui Romanę Ecclesię corruptelas omnes, quanquam absurdissimas, præfractè tamē defendere statuerunt: quùmque ex ipsis Pontificiis Doctoribus plerique Sacrificij vocabulum,in hac quęstione,de applicatione vnici illius sacrificij, quod semel in cruce factum est,intelligant : isti nihilominus cōtendunt,in sua Missa fieri verum,externum & proprie dictum sacrificium: atque ad eam rem efficiendam adhibent sua sophismata,quorum scilicet,præstigiis nobis imponant.Nec
units.tr: For once the salvation of the soul had been tied to this single fictitious sacrifice, and those ill-omened doctrines of implicit faith and of the work done (ex opere operato) had been accepted together, people's stupidity and ignorance grew to such a degree that they no longer even knew that they did not know. They thought that being ignorant of sacred things was a mark of great virtue, and above all of the Catholic faith. So this most convenient way of practising religion pleased people, and pleased them too much: they attended this sacrifice so skilfully manufactured, that is, this Mass crammed with pageantry. They saw the marvellous ceremonies and heard the din of foreign words, yet understood nothing of what was being done or said. Indeed, it seemed enough and more than enough to be present, to marvel, to listen, and in turn to murmur along with the noise of the priests' mumbling, since they were persuaded that they were saved by that work done (as they put it), and that, idle and hardly thinking of such things, they would be carried off to the heavenly inheritance as if drawn in the chariot of this sacrifice. So great was the power of Satan, the father of lies, in deceiving men; and God, avenging contempt of his Word and human ingratitude, punished them with penalties as just as they were severe. But now, when such gross and foul errors are being refuted by the light of God's truth, the Papists cry out: "What an outrageous deed! Everything is being thrown into confusion, the Church is collapsing, piety is being extinguished! Moreover, a very great injury is done to divine things and to the Christian religion itself when anything is taken away from the Mass; in short, the sun itself will be removed from the world if the sacrifice of the Mass is removed." But since we acknowledge that the one sacrifice of Christ was made once on the cross for our sins, and place our hope of salvation in it; since we celebrate the memory of that sacrifice in the holy Supper of the Lord, with the greatest reverence, as Christ himself instituted it; and finally since we profess that we receive the body and blood of Christ by true faith, for the forgiveness of sins and eternal life: I beg you, Papists, why do you condemn us as heretics and enemies of Christ's sacrifice? Evidently for this reason: that we reject your additions to the Mass and your ceremonies, which are ridiculous, absurd, and even contrary to the Word of God. But you, why do you resist the plain truth, and not fear to evade with cold and silly quibbles the clear and express passages of Scripture about the one priesthood and sacrifice of Christ, so often urged by us? Surely you are thereby excellently confirming what Augustine says in discussing error, in nearly these words: There are two things (he says) that are least tolerable in the error of men: presumption, before the truth is revealed; and, once it has been revealed, the defence of the presumed falsehood. All the more intolerable is the audacity of the pseudo-monks, who have resolved to defend stubbornly all the corruptions of the Roman Church, however absurd. And although most of the Papist teachers themselves understand the word sacrifice, in this question, of the application of that one sacrifice which was made once on the cross, these men nonetheless contend that in their Mass a true, external and properly so-called sacrifice is performed, and to accomplish this they employ their sophisms, by whose tricks they wish to impose upon us. units.la: Audacia Pseudomonachorum. vero sum nescius hoc Pontificiorum commentum, & quaslibet eiusmodi Monachales ineptias à viris doctissimis fuisse grauissimè refutatas: nec ipse in medium prodeo, quasi nouum, & hactenus inauditum aliquid dicturus: sed speraui non omnino futurum inutile, si Sophistæ, veris Ἱρότης παιδείας armis, & ab illa ipsa arte, quam immeritò quidè, sed tamen fidenter, sibi prope solis vendicant, profligentur. Quamobrè, vt nos copiosam aliorum, fusamque latius orationem & vberrima scripta laudamus, & ex iis legendis maximum nos fructu percipere fatemur: ita nobis concedi petimus, vt hoc etiā contracto & scholastico scribendi genere vti nobis liceat: & quæ huius ætatis Doctores, cùm doctrina, tum etiam summa dicendi facultate præstantissimi fusè, & latiore stylo conscripserunt: ea ex præceptis Ἱρότης παιδείας ita proponere, vt ipsa tela, quæ nobis alij explicant & porrigunt: nos, quasi ipsius artis differendi lacertis, in communes hostes vibrare videamur. Atque vt id sperem me facile impetraturum, facit Augustinus: qui censuit
units.tr: The audacity of the pseudo-monks. Yet I am not unaware that this Papist fiction, and all such monkish trifles of this kind, have been most gravely refuted by the most learned men; nor do I come forward as if about to say something new and hitherto unheard of. But I hoped it would not be wholly useless if the sophists were overthrown with the true weapons of dialectic, and by that very art which they unjustly, yet confidently, claim almost for themselves alone. Therefore, just as we praise the copious discourse of others, and their fuller and more abundant writings, and confess that we gain the greatest profit from reading them, so we ask that we be permitted to use this also, a condensed and scholastic manner of writing; and to set out, according to the precepts of dialectic, what the teachers of this age, eminent both in learning and in the highest power of expression, have written at length and in a fuller style, so that we seem to hurl, as it were from the arms of the art of disputation itself, the very weapons which others explain and hand to us against our common enemies. units.la: Utile esse de iisdem quæstionibus plures a pluribus fieri libros, diuerso stylo, non diuersa fide: quandoquidem (inquit idem aliquanto post) tanto fortius conuincuntur hæretici, quanto plures exitus patent ad eorum laqueos euitandos. Hæc ille. Vt enim qui ad vnū, eundemque portum contendunt, non possunt omnes in vno eodemque nauigio contineri (nam, vt inquit ille, ναῦς μὴ μία πάντας ἄγει.) Ita in iis quibus propositum est, eandem doctrinæ veritatem, aduersus hominum mendacia propugnare: ipsarum tractationum varietas non debet, nec styli dissimilitudo reprehendi. Sed quia in præfatione primæ nostræ disputationis de Verbo Dei scripto, plura de hac re diximus: nō erimus hoc loco longiores. Tantum peto a fratribus ac Symmystis meis plurimum obseruandis, quibus hasce tractationes dicaui: atque adeo a piis omnibus Theologiæ candidatis, quorum studia pro nostro modulo cupimus adiuuare, vt tātulum hunc laborem boni consulant, nostrisque argumentis noua etiamnum adiungant argumenta, & ea quæ a nobis propositä sunt, ipsi, pro ingenij sui doctrinæque facultate locu- pletent.Pontificios autem hortor,atq. etiam obtestor per Iesum Christum, qui dilexit nos, inquit Apostolus, & fe-metipfum tradidit pro nobis, oblationem & victimam Deo,in odorem bonæ fragrantiæ: vt humanis commentis, quæ Deus a-uersatur,procul abiectis: relicto contendendi studio: discussaque errorum caligine,fe ad veram nobiscum de vnico Christi sacrificio doctrinam recipiant: atque ita iisdem animis, summa cum reuerentia, Christum pro nobis crucifixum adoremus:vt eo solo sacerdote freti, illiusque sacrosancti sacrificij, quod semel in cruce factu est, memoriam, non ex hominum institutis, sed ex puro Dei verbo pure celebrantes,virtutem eius perpetua sentiamus: atque inde æternæ fœlicitatis hæreditatem,summa & gratuita Dei liberalitate & misericordia, consequamur.
units.tr: It is useful for many writers to produce many books on the same questions, in different styles but not with different faith. For, as the same author says a little later, heretics are refuted all the more strongly the more ways there are open to escape their snares. So he writes. For just as those who strive for one and the same harbour cannot all be carried in one and the same ship (since, as the saying goes, one ship does not carry everyone [ναῦς μὴ μία πάντας ἄγει]), so too, in those who intend to defend the same truth of doctrine against human lies, the variety of their treatments and the dissimilarity of their style should not be found fault with. But since in the preface to our first disputation, on the written Word of God, we said a good deal on this subject, we will not be longer here. I ask only this of my brothers and fellow initiates, whom I rightly honour, and to whom I have dedicated these treatises; and likewise of all pious candidates of theology, whose studies we desire to help as far as we are able: that they take this little labour in good part, and add new arguments of their own to ours, and enrich with their own talent and learning the points we have put forward. As for the Papists, I exhort them, and even beseech them, through Jesus Christ, who loved us, as the Apostle says, and gave himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a fragrant odour: that they cast far from them the human inventions which God abhors, give up the zeal for contention, and, with the darkness of error dispelled, come over with us to the true doctrine concerning the one sacrifice of Christ; and that thus, with minds united and in the greatest reverence, we may adore Christ crucified for us; so that, relying on him alone as our priest, and celebrating the memory of that most holy sacrifice, which was made once for all on the cross, purely, not according to human institutions but according to the pure Word of God, we may feel its power continually, and from it obtain the inheritance of eternal happiness, by the highest and free liberality and mercy of God.

units.la: LOCVS DE VNICO CHRISTI SACERDOTIO ET SACRIFICIO, Aduersus commentitium Missæ Sacrificium, Theologici & Scholasticè tractatus.
units.tr: THE LOCUS ON THE ONE PRIESTHOOD AND SACRIFICE OF CHRIST, Against the Invented Sacrifice of the Mass, a Theological and Scholastic Treatise.

units.la: CAPVT PRIMVM.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: VT Theologicæ & Scholasticæ disputationis methodum à nobis propositam sequamur: primùm omnium proponeda est & explicanda nostra de vnico Christi sacerdotio & sacrificio sententia. Hæc autem est huiusmodi:
units.tr: To follow the method of theological and scholastic disputation that we have adopted, we must first set out and explain our own position on the one priesthood and sacrifice of Christ. It is as follows:

units.la: Christus est solus Pontifex, ac verè sacerdos noui Testamenti, & eius sacrificium semel in cruce peractum, est vnicum, reale, & externum Sacrificium in Ecclesia Christiana, idémque vnicum propitiatorium pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: Christ is the only High Priest and the true priest of the New Testament, and his sacrifice, once offered on the cross, is the one, real and external sacrifice in the Christian Church, and likewise the one propitiation for our sins.

units.la: Quæ quidé nostra, hoc est, Ecclesiæ Dei
units.tr: This is our position, that is, the position of the Church of God,

units.la: ex ipsius verbo reformatæ sententia, vt faci- lius intelligi posset, pauca quædam nobis de ipsis sacrificiis & eorum vsu dicenda sunt.
units.tr: reformed from his own Word. So that it may be understood more easily, we must first say a few things about the sacrifices themselves and their use.

units.la: Cum Dominus (quæ fuit ipsius erga generis humanum misericordia) Adamum in peccatum prolapsum spe certissima salutis confirmaret, eiusque animum in expectatione nem Mesiæ venturi excitasset, qui sua morte tum Adamum, tum eius posteros (prout imperuestigabili Dei consilio visum est) cum Deo reconciliaret, eosque redderet æternæ vitæ participes: non dubium est quin præclaram hanc promissionem, nō tantum impressam in animo, sed etiam externo aliquo signo, ceu pignore dato, confirmatam & ob signatam esse voluerit. Ex quo factum est vt Adamus liberos instituerit in pietate & cultu Dei, atque imprimis in sacrificiis offerendis: vt cuiuis perspicuum esse poteset, qui modo in Caini & Abelis historia versetur. Atque hoc diuinum institutum in piis aliquot familiis multos annos sanctè ac religiosè conseruatum fuisse, testatus est Noachus: cum post diluuiū offerret holocausta super altare, in quorū odore suauissimo (ita commemorante Mose) Dominus acquieuit: ne multa alia eodem spectantia mihi sint, tum ex libris Mosis, tum ex historia Iobi proferenda. Porrò cum Deus voluit Ecclesiam illustriori quodam modo colligere, Mosen excitauit, cuius ministerio traditi sunt Israelitis litis varij sacrificiorum ac cęremoniarum ritus, sacris literarum monumentis consignati:in quibus, ac przfertim in cęsis immolatísque victimis, ceu in tabula, non solum pœna peccatis nostris debita proponebatur: verumetiam Mefsias venturus, ita depictus, eiúsque sacrificium in cruce peragendumita advivum expressum est, vt res ipsa propemodum oculis subiecta videretur. Tandem nouissimis temporibus Christus in Lege & Prophetis promissus, exhibitus est: qui Legem impleuit, & aduentu suo,atque imprimis sua morte & oblatione corporis sui, hoc est,vnico illo ac praestatissimo sacrificio in cruce facto (cuius legalia sacrificia typi fuerunt & figurae)externa sacrificia abrogauit. Itaque primis illis ac vetustissimis temporibus quae Legem scriptam antecesserut, ritus sacrificiorum diuinis oraculis traditi, instar cuiusdam σκιαγραφίας, & crassioris delineationis fuere: cui postea per Mosen viui colores additi sunt, donec tandé Christus ipse veteribus sacrificiis, non adumbratus tantùm , sed etiam ad viuum expressus, mùdo patefactus est: ac propterea corporis exhibiti praesentia & sacrificium Christi reipsa peractum,finem legalibus cęremoniis, ceu pictusuch imposuit.Cùm aute vnici illius sacrificij virtus sit perpetua(vt etiá Christus est æternus sacerdos,semper viuens & interpellans pro nobis:) ratione Christus ipse in Ecclesia Christiana instituit, qua tanti beneficij fructum percipere posumus: nempe Euangelij praedicationem & Sacramenta noui Testamenti: quibus mediis atque instrumentis sacer Dei Spiritus, prout ipsi visum est, ut solet: ut nobis applicet illius sacrificij efficaciam & virtutem. Quamobrem, post mortem & resurrectionem Christi (nec enim illa duo seperamus, cum mortis Christi beneficium ideo sit efficax, quia Christus a mortuis resurrexit) externorum & reliqui sacrificiorum usum nullum in Ecclesia locum habere credimus: ne Christi exhibitionem & aduetum adeoque sacrificium ipsius semel oblatum negare velle videamur: quod profecto faciunt ij qui Missae sacrificium reale & externum obstinate defendunt. Ut enim si quis debitam a multis pecuniam semel creditori persoluerit, ea conditione, ut illi demum ab obligatione liberetur, qui hoc beneficio uti se velle profesi fuerint: stultum esset dicere, pecuniam toties numerandam, quoties hic, vel ille profitebitur: (quamquidem sufficit semel creditori fuisse satisfactum: ac tantum supereret, ut fructus solutionis semel facto profitentibus applicetur:) Ita, cum Dominus mortis suae sacrificio se mel pro nobis Deo satisfecerit, modo vera fide summu hoc beneficiu percipiamus: certe ineptum, atque etiam impium est dicere: ut nobis sacrificiu Christi applicetur, Christum stum esse denuò sacrificandum. Atque hæc de explicatione nostrę sententiæ: quæ tamē vt etiamnū fiat dilucidior, excutiamus tam Subiectum quàm Attributū superioris propositionis.
units.tr: When the Lord, in his mercy towards the human race, strengthened Adam after his fall into sin with a most certain hope of salvation, and stirred up in him an expectation of the coming Messiah, who by his death would reconcile both Adam and his posterity to God (as seemed good to God's unsearchable counsel) and make them partakers of eternal life, there is no doubt that he wished this glorious promise not only to be impressed upon the mind but also to be confirmed and sealed by some outward sign, as a pledge given. Hence it came about that Adam taught his children piety and the worship of God, and above all the offering of sacrifices, as anyone may see who reads the story of Cain and Abel. That this divine institution was kept holy and religiously in some pious families for many years is attested by Noah, who, after the flood, offered burnt offerings upon the altar, and in their most sweet savour (as Moses relates) the Lord was pleased. I shall not bring forward many other things pertaining to this, whether from the books of Moses or from the history of Job. Moreover, when God willed to gather his Church in a more distinguished manner, he raised up Moses, by whose ministry the various rites of sacrifices and ceremonies were handed down to the Israelites, recorded in the sacred writings. In these, and especially in the slain and sacrificed victims, as in a picture, not only was the punishment due to our sins set forth, but also the coming Messiah was portrayed, and his sacrifice to be accomplished on the cross was so vividly expressed that the thing itself seemed almost placed before the eyes. At last, in the final times, Christ, promised in the Law and the Prophets, was revealed. He fulfilled the Law, and by his coming, and above all by his death and the offering of his body, that is, by that one most excellent sacrifice made on the cross (of which the legal sacrifices were types and figures), he abolished the external sacrifices. Thus in those first and most ancient times, which preceded the written Law, the rites of sacrifice were handed down by divine oracles, like a kind of sketch [σκιαγραφία] and rougher outline. To this, afterwards through Moses, living colours were added, until at last Christ himself was made manifest to the world, not only shadowed forth in the old sacrifices but also portrayed to the life. Therefore the presence of the body that was offered, and the sacrifice of Christ actually accomplished, put an end to the legal ceremonies, as the picture is ended by its finish. But since the power of that one sacrifice is perpetual (just as Christ himself is an eternal priest, always living and interceding for us), Christ himself instituted in the Christian Church the means by which we may receive the fruit of so great a benefit: namely, the preaching of the Gospel and the sacraments of the New Testament. By these means and instruments the holy Spirit of God, as it has pleased him, applies to us the efficacy and power of that sacrifice. For this reason, after the death and resurrection of Christ (for we do not separate those two, since the benefit of Christ's death is effective precisely because Christ rose from the dead), we believe that the use of external and other sacrifices has no place in the Church, lest we seem to deny the manifestation and coming of Christ, and thus his sacrifice once offered. Those who obstinately defend the real and external sacrifice of the Mass certainly do exactly this. For if someone had once paid to a creditor a debt owed by many, on the condition that they should be freed from the obligation only if they professed that they wished to use this benefit, it would be foolish to say that the money must be counted out as often as this man or that one professes it. For it is enough that the creditor has once been satisfied, and all that remains is that the fruit of the payment, once made, be applied to those who profess it. Likewise, since the Lord has once satisfied God for us by the sacrifice of his death, if we receive this supreme benefit by true faith, it is certainly foolish, and even impious, to say that Christ must be sacrificed again so that the sacrifice of Christ may be applied to us. So much for the explanation of our position. However, so that it may become still clearer, let us examine both the subject and the predicate of the above proposition.

units.la: Subiectum est, Christus benedictus: de cuius nominis expositione, nulla hoc in loco nobis est cum Pontificiis controuersia. Sed in Attributo, & in singulis eius partibus tota hæc disputatio sita est. Quare operæpretium fuerit Attributum ipsum paulò accuratius expendere, vt cùm in aciem disputationis ventum fuerit, nostræ tum obiectiones,tum responsiones facilius intelligantur.
units.tr: The subject is Christ, blessed be he. There is no controversy with the Papists here over the explanation of his name. But the whole of this dispute lies in the predicate and in its individual parts. Therefore it will be worth while to weigh the predicate itself a little more carefully, so that when we come to the battle of the disputation, our objections and replies may be more easily understood.

units.la: Quædam sunt in hoc Attributo, quæ fortasse lucem aliquam desiderent. Cùm enim Christum appellamus Pontificem ac sacerdotem: licet ea nomina vsurpemus quę temporibus veteris Testamenti tam Aaroni quàm eius posteris indita fuerunt: hunc tamen nostrum Pontificem & sacerdote longissimo interuallo à Leuiticis omnibus sacerdotibus distinguimus: quippe sacerdote æternum,cuius legales sacerdotes typi fuerunt. Atque id ex iis quæ sequuntur in Attributo,perspicuum esse potest: præsertim cùm eum noui Testamenti sacerdotem esse dicimus. Nec tamen sum nescius,Ministros Euangelij sæpe à veteribus vocatos fuisse Sacerdotes, quum illi ad vetus Testamentum aluderent: sed nos vocabulum proprie vsurpamus,ac propterea dicimus,Christum esse vere sacerdotem:vt allusiones & similitudines remoueamus. Deinde nequid insidiarũ lateat in vocabulo sacrificij (quantum enim hinc fallere conetur Potificij,fiet ex sequeti disputatione manifestum) diligenter nobis vocabulum illud excutiendum est, & quatuor proponenda:ex quibus sententię nostrę veritas manifestior esse posit.
units.tr: There are some matters in this predicate which perhaps need some light. For when we call Christ High Priest and priest, although we use those names which in the times of the Old Testament were given both to Aaron and to his posterity, we nonetheless distinguish this our High Priest and priest by a very great interval from all the Levitical priests, since he is an eternal priest, of whom the legal priests were types. This can be clearly seen from what follows in the predicate, especially when we call him the priest of the New Testament. Nor am I unaware that the ministers of the Gospel were often called priests by the ancients, when they were alluding to the Old Testament; but we use the word properly, and therefore we say that Christ is truly a priest, so that allusions and similitudes may be set aside. Next, lest any snare lie hidden in the word sacrifice (for how far the Papists try to deceive by this will become plain from the following disputation), that word must be carefully examined by us, and four points must be set forth, from which the truth of our position may be made clearer.

units.la: Primum: etsi inanis est de vocabulis ipsis concertatio,quoties tamen iis vtimur vocabulis,quæ extant in Scriptura:simul retinenda est ea significatio,in qua ab ipsa Scriptura vsurpantur:Nam siquis,arbitratu suo,nouas illis significationes affingeret: ille certe ab ipsis Theologicæ disputationis finibus arceretur.Quamobrem diligenter animaduertendum est,quid Scriptura intelligat sacrificij nomine. Vocabula Hebraica,Courban,Mincha,Hola,Zeuach,& siqua forte similia occurrunt, Græci his vocabulis expresserūt: προσφορα, δωρον, ὁλοκαυτωμα, ὁλοκαρπωσις, θυσια, θυσιασμα, & aliquot aliis consimilibus. Latini vero interpretes modo vocabula Græca retinuerunt,vt,holocaustum,& holocautoma:modo, Sacrificij & Oblationis nominibus vsi sunt,quibus superiora vocabula nobis explicarent. Ex quo perspicuum est, Sacrificij vocabulũ ita late patere apud Latinos Bibliorum Interpretes, vt non solum significet sacras illas cæremonias, quibus bus olim victimæ ex præscripto Legis immolabantur: sed etiam oblationes ex rebus inanimatis confectas. Quinetiam vocabulum Zeuach apud Hebræos latius aliquando accipitur.Quamquam autem multæ olim ac variæ fuerunt sacrificiorum species(vt patet ex libris Mosis, ac præsertim ex Leuitico) tamen mihi rectè videntur Theologi omnia illa sacrificia ita distribuisse,vt alia ἱλαστικά, siue propitiatoria: alia εὐχαριστικά, siue gratiarum actionis dici posint. Quæ distributio facilè colligi potest ex ipsis præceptis legalibus.
units.tr: First: although a dispute over words themselves is empty, nevertheless whenever we use those words which occur in Scripture, the meaning in which Scripture itself employs them must at the same time be kept. For if anyone were to assign new meanings to them at his own pleasure, he would certainly be excluded from the very bounds of theological disputation. Therefore we must consider carefully what Scripture understands by the name sacrifice. The Hebrew words Courban, Mincha, Hola, Zeuach, and whatever similar words occur, the Greeks expressed by these words: [προσφορά] oblation, [δῶρον] gift, [ὁλοκαύτωμα] whole burnt offering, [ὁλοκάρπωσις] whole burnt offering, [θυσία] sacrifice, [θυσιασμός] sacrifice, and several other like words. The Latin translators sometimes retained the Greek words, as holocaustum and holocautoma, and sometimes used the terms sacrifice and oblation, by which they explained for us the former words. From this it is plain that the word sacrifice has so wide a range among the Latin interpreters of the Bible that it signifies not only those sacred ceremonies by which victims were formerly slain according to the prescription of the Law, but also offerings made from inanimate things. Indeed, the Hebrew word Zeuach is sometimes taken in a wider sense. Although there were many and various kinds of sacrifices in former times (as is clear from the books of Moses, and especially from Leviticus), nonetheless the theologians seem to me to have rightly divided all those sacrifices so that some may be called [ἱλαστικά] propitiatory, that is, for atonement, and others [εὐχαριστικά] eucharistic, that is, of thanksgiving. This division can easily be gathered from the legal precepts themselves.

units.la: Secundum: licet Hebraica nomina, & ipsum sacrificij vocabulum, non actionem tantùm,qua res offertur: sed etiam rem ipsam oblatam significet:tamen vsus obtinuit, vt Sacrificium magis proprie ad actionem referatur: res autem oblata, vel hostia, vel victima appelletur. Hæc igitur est propria & primaria acceptio vocabuli Sacrificij, vt significet sacram actionem qua res aliqua externa offertur & consecratur Deo in eum finem & iis ritibus,qui sunt ab ipso instituti. Ex hac primaria significatione, altera (vt fere fit) per similitudinem deriuata est, qua spiritualis & interior Dei cultus, atque ipsa pietatis & charitatis officia, sacrificia dici solet. Itaque ne nobis imponat homonymia vocabuli, hæc distinctio necessario proponenda est:Sacrificiu aut proprie dici: atque ita significare prius illud reale (ita enim dicamus) & externum sacrificium: aut figurate: & tunc posterius hoc sacrificium denotare, quod diximus ad spiritualem Dei cultum & ad vitæ sanctimoniam pertinere. Atque id loquendi genus tum in veteri,tum in nouo Testamento sepe occurrit. De hoc posteriori nulla est in hac quæstione inter nos dissensio: omnes enim agnoscimus, sacrificia eiusmodi interiora & spiritualia, etiam noui Testamenti temporibus locum habere: de externis & realibus sacrificiis tota hæc nostra instituta est disputatio. Nos enim affirmamus, post Christum exhibitum peractumque ipsius sacrificium, quo seipsum pro nobis obtulit Deo, nullum amplius externum & reale sacrificium superesse: quandoquidem externum omne & reale sacrificium, aut fuit typus & figura sacrificij Christi, aut fuit ipsum Christi sacrificium semel oblatum in cruce: nec iam vllum in Ecclesia Christiana externum & reale sacrificium a Christo institutum est. Cum igitur non humanæ sed Diuinæ institutionis Sacrificium esse debeat: nobisque non temere, sed ex vsu Scripturæ loquendum sit: Scriptura vero post aduentum Christi nihil tradiderit de reali sacrificio a nobis peragendo: sed potius sacrificium Christi, vnicum sacrificiū appellet: nos vnico illo salutari & perfectissimo Christi sacrificio contenti sumus.
units.tr: Secondly: although the Hebrew words, and the word sacrifice itself, signify not only the action by which a thing is offered but also the thing offered, usage has prevailed so that "sacrifice" refers more properly to the action, while the thing offered is called the offering or the victim. This, then, is the proper and primary sense of the word sacrifice: a sacred action by which some external thing is offered and dedicated to God, for the purpose and with the rites that he himself has instituted. From this primary meaning a second sense has been derived by resemblance, as usually happens, by which the spiritual and inward worship of God, and the duties of piety and love themselves, are commonly called sacrifices. So that the ambiguity of the word may not mislead us, this distinction must necessarily be set out: sacrifice is used either properly, and so denotes the first, real (as we may call it) and external sacrifice, or figuratively, and then it denotes the second sort, which we have said pertains to spiritual worship of God and to holiness of life. This manner of speaking occurs often in both the Old and the New Testament. Concerning the latter there is no disagreement between us in this question, for we all acknowledge that such inward and spiritual sacrifices have their place even in the times of the New Testament. Our whole dispute concerns external and real sacrifices. For we affirm that after Christ was revealed and his sacrifice accomplished, by which he offered himself for us to God, no further external and real sacrifice remains. For every external and real sacrifice either was a type and figure of Christ's sacrifice, or was Christ's own sacrifice once offered on the cross; and no external and real sacrifice has been instituted by Christ in the Christian Church. Since, therefore, a sacrifice ought to be of divine and not of human institution, and since we must speak not rashly but in accordance with the usage of Scripture, and since Scripture after the coming of Christ has handed down nothing about a real sacrifice to be performed by us, but rather calls the sacrifice of Christ the one sacrifice, we are content with that one, saving and most perfect sacrifice of Christ.

units.la: Tertium
units.tr: Third

units.la: Tertium : cum legalia sacrificia fuerint, vel ἱλαστικα, vel εὐχαριστικα (vt ante dictum est) affirmamus : Sacrificium Christi quod in cruce semel oblatum est, proprie & vere fuisse & esse propitiatorium. Nam Deus mittit Christum (inquit Ioannes) vt esset propitiatio pro peccatis nostris: & alibi, Ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris: adeo vt qui nouum aliud propitiatorij sacrificij genus introduxerint, ij morti Christi, quantum in ipsis est, renuntiare videantur.
units.tr: Thirdly: since the legal sacrifices were either propitiatory or eucharistic (as was said above), we affirm that the sacrifice of Christ, once offered on the cross, was and is truly and properly propitiatory. For "God sent Christ," says John, "to be a propitiation for our sins"; and elsewhere, "He himself is the propitiation for our sins." So much so that those who have introduced some other new kind of propitiatory sacrifice seem, as far as in them lies, to renounce the death of Christ.

units.la: Quartum: diligenter obseruandum est: Sacrificium Christi distinguendum esse ab applicatione ipsius sacrificij: adeo vt applicatio sacrificij Christi, dici non possit ipsum Christi sacrificium : quod vel ipso naturae sensu facile intelligi potest, neque res haec desiderat probationem longiorem. Cum ergo Christus semel sacrificatus, nec debeat, nec etiam possit amplius sacrificari: superest tantum vt virtus ipsius Sacrificij nobis applicetur. In ipsa vero applicatione duo confideramus: videlicet, efficacitatem Spiritus Sancti in nobis operantis, & rationes externas quibus, tanquam instrumentis, ipse Dei Spiritus vtitur vt opus suum in nobis peragat: quae quidem externa media publica & in vsum totius Ecclesiae introducta, sunt, ipsa praedicatio verbi Dei, &, Sacramenta a Christo instituta: quemadmodum ex scriptis Apostolicis didicimus.
units.tr: Fourthly: it must be carefully observed that the sacrifice of Christ must be distinguished from the application of that sacrifice, so that the application of Christ's sacrifice cannot be called Christ's sacrifice itself. This can easily be understood even by the sense of nature, and the matter does not require a longer proof. Since Christ, having been sacrificed once, neither ought nor is able to be sacrificed again, it remains only that the power of that sacrifice be applied to us. In the application itself we consider two things: namely, the efficacy of the Holy Spirit working in us, and the external means by which the Spirit of God himself makes use, as by instruments, to accomplish his work in us. These external means, which have been introduced as public means for the use of the whole Church, are the preaching of the word of God itself and the sacraments instituted by Christ, as we have learned from the apostolic writings.

units.la: {a}Quæ cum ita sint: cum sacrificij vocabulum in ea tantum significatione in qua extat in Scriptura à Theologis vsurpari debeat: Et Scriptura vnicum tantum reale & externum noui Testamenti sacrificium proponat, nempe Iesu Christi Sacerdotis simul & Victimæ, mortem & sacrificium: quod quidem semel pro nobis in cruce factum, vere est ac proprie ἱλαστικὸν & propitiatorium pro peccatis nostris: cum ipsius vnici sacrificij virtus sit infinita, ac perpetua, eáque nobis applicetur ἐνεργείᾳ Spiritus Sancti, adhibitis (prout ipsi videtur) Instrumentis ac Mediis, videlicet prædicatione verbi Dei, & Sacramentis à Christo in Ecclesia Christiana institutis: cum denique applicatio sacrificij cum ipso sacrificio non sit confundenda: efficitur, planam esse ac dilucidam superiorem nostram sententiam, qua dicebamus: Christum esse solum Pontificem & vere Sacerdotem noui Testameti & eius sacrificium semel in cruce peractum, esse vnicum noui Testamenti sacrificium externum & reale, atque etiam propitiatorium pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: {a}Since these things are so: since the word sacrifice ought to be used by theologians only in the sense in which it stands in Scripture; and since Scripture sets forth only one real and external sacrifice of the New Testament, namely that of Jesus Christ, at once priest and victim, his death and sacrifice, which indeed was made once for us on the cross and is truly and properly propitiatory [ἱλαστικὸν] for our sins; and since the power of this one sacrifice is infinite and perpetual, and is applied to us by the energy [ἐνεργείᾳ] of the Holy Spirit, with the instruments and means (as it pleases him) of the preaching of the word of God and the sacraments instituted by Christ in the Christian Church; and since, finally, the application of the sacrifice must not be confused with the sacrifice itself: it follows that our above-stated opinion is plain and clear, in which we said that Christ is the only High Priest and true Priest of the New Testament, and that his sacrifice once accomplished on the cross is the only real and external sacrifice of the New Testament, and also propitiatory for our sins.

units.la: Iam proponamus Pontificiorum sententiam, eámque cum nostra comparemus: vt facilius cognoscamus quisnam sit huiusce disputationis status: sic igitur illi opinantur:
units.tr: Now let us set out the opinion of the Papists and compare it with ours, so that we may more easily see what the state of this dispute is. They think as follows:

units.la: In Missa fieri verum, reale & externum sacrificium, quo sacerdotes offerunt Deo corpus & sanguisanguinem Christi sub speciebus panis & vini: quod quidem sacrificium est propitiatorium pro vivis & mortuis.
units.tr: In the Mass a true, real and external sacrifice takes place, in which the priests offer to God the body and blood of Christ under the species of bread and wine; and this sacrifice is propitiatory for the living and the dead.

units.la: Hanc suam sententiam ita exponunt. Sacrificium Christi duobus modis considera- ri; aut, vt cruentu: aut, vt incruentu. Cruentum Christi sacrificiu semel tantum in cruce factum esse: Incruentum autem saepe a sacerdotibus factitari, idque ex Institutione Christi, qui suae mortis memoriam voluit, non solum verbis & Euangelica praedicatione renouari: sed etiam externa Missae actione repraesentari a sacerdotibus Ecclesiae Christianae. Christum quidem esse primarium Ecclesiae Christianae sacerdote, sed Episcopos & Presbyteros esse secundarios sacerdotes Christi ipsum secundarie offerentes. Cum autem (vt illi quidem tradunt) cruenti & incruenti sacrificij Christi differentia sit, non in re ipsa, sed in modo tantum: idcirco Missae sacrificium incruentu, aiunt esse propitiatorium pro peccatis, quandoquidem illud ipsum tribuitur cruento Christi sacrificio. Iam quia censent hominum peccata, nō hic tantum remitti, sed etiam post mortem poenis purgatoriis expiari, eo fit, vt Sacrificium Missae affirment esse propitiatorium tam pro viuis, quam pro mortuis. Atque haec est summa huius dogmatis Pontificij, pro quo tantopere decertant, non modo variis disputationibus, sed, quod longe
units.tr: They explain this opinion thus: the sacrifice of Christ may be considered in two ways, either as bloody or as unbloody. The bloody sacrifice of Christ was made only once, on the cross; but the unbloody sacrifice is often performed by priests, and this by the institution of Christ, who willed that the memory of his death be renewed not only by words and evangelical preaching, but also be represented by the external action of the Mass by the priests of the Christian Church. Christ is indeed the chief priest of the Christian Church, but the bishops and presbyters are secondary priests, offering him in a secondary way. Since, however (as they teach), the difference between the bloody and unbloody sacrifice of Christ lies not in the thing itself but only in the manner, therefore they say that the unbloody sacrifice of the Mass is propitiatory for sins, since that very efficacy is attributed to the bloody sacrifice of Christ. Now, since they hold that the sins of men are not only remitted here, but are also expiated after death by purgatorial punishments, it follows that they affirm the sacrifice of the Mass to be propitiatory both for the living and for the dead. And this is the sum of this Papist doctrine, for which they contend so fiercely, not only with various disputations but, what is far more

units.la: grauius est, flammis ac gladiis, & quantum eis licuit totos ab hinc septuaginta annos, assidua crudelitate: adeò vt dum suum nobis sacrificium incruentum toties inculcat, vniuersam propemodum Europam piorum hominum cruore repleuerint.
units.tr: with fire and sword, and, as far as they have been permitted, with relentless cruelty for the past seventy years, so that while they keep pressing their unbloody sacrifice upon us, they have filled almost all of Europe with the blood of godly people.

units.la: Ex his igitur perspicuum est, nostram & Pontificiorum sententiam ἀντιφατικῶς opponi. Nos enim solum Christum noui Testamenti vere sacerdotem esse affirmamus: illi nō solum Christum agnoscunt noui Testamenti sacerdotē. Nos Christi sacrificium oblatum in cruce pro nobis, vnicum, reale & externum in Ecclesia Christiana sacrificium esse dicimus: Illi, non vnicū esse contendunt. Nos vnicum illud Christi reale sacrificium, esse pro peccatis propitiatorium ex verbo Dei statuimus: Illi, non vnicū esse autumant, qui ippe illud ipsum Missæ sacrificio tribuentes. Porrò quod illi vim ac pondus suæ Missæ ad inferos vsque ita demergunt, vt inde extinguant atque opprimant flammas purgatorias, quas ipsi alio etiamnum errore confinxerunt: non pluribus hoc loco persequemur: quandoquidem ea de re συνθέσεως peculiare disputatione instituemus.
units.tr: From this it is plain that our view and the view of the Papists are set against each other contradictorily [ἀντιφατικῶς]. For we maintain that Christ alone is truly the priest of the New Testament, whereas they acknowledge not only Christ but others as priests of the New Testament too. We say that the sacrifice of Christ offered on the cross for us is the one, real and external sacrifice in the Christian Church; they deny that it is the only one. We establish from the Word of God that this one real sacrifice of Christ is the propitiation for sins; they claim that it is not the only one, since they attribute that very same propitiation to the sacrifice of the Mass. Moreover, the way they plunge the force and weight of their Mass down into hell, so as to quench and smother the purgatorial flames, which they have invented by yet another error, we will not pursue further here, since we shall give that matter a separate treatise [συνθέσεως].

units.la: En ergo quisnam sit totius controuersiæ status & τὸ κρινόμενον: An solus Christus sit verè sacerdos noui Testamenti, & mors eius sit vnicum noui Testamenti sacrificiū reale & proprie dictū. Quæ si semel definita fuerint; rint; reliquæ quæstiones ex superioribus dependentes & à Pontificiis propositæ, sua sponte dissoluentur. Nam quod illi quærūt, quatenus Missa sit vtilis, ipsis etiam sacerdotibus: &, quasi de rationibus referendis agerent, disputant de proportionibus (vt illi quidè loquūtur) Intensiuè & extensiuè taxatis: hoc, inquam, ludicrum & puerile somnium ex superioris quæstionis tractatione satis evanescet, nec erit opus longiori disputatione. Nisi forte expectant, vt sibi hac in re gratificemur, fateamurque, Missam sacrificulis Pontificiis vtilem quidem atque imprimis quæstuosam fuisse: qui subtili hoc reticulo amplissima vectigalia, & innumerabiles diuitias undique corraserunt. At nos ea demū vtilitatè probantes, quæ cum Dei verbo & Ecclesiæ saluti congruit: ista nō inutilē modò, sed etiam exitiosam vtilitatè damnamus; quę homines auertit à Christiane Religionis puritate, & beneficio mortis ac passionis Christi crassissimas tenebras offudit. Sed iā nostræ sententiæ confirmatio proponenda est.
units.tr: Here, then, is the state of the whole controversy and the point at issue [τὸ κρινόμενον]: whether Christ alone is truly the priest of the New Testament, and whether his death is the one real and properly so-called sacrifice of the New Testament. Once these are settled, the remaining questions, which depend on what has gone before and which the Papists raise, will resolve themselves. For what they ask, how far the Mass is useful, even to the priests themselves, and, as if they were giving an account of their reasons, they dispute about proportions (as they call them) rated intensively and extensively: this, I say, is a trifling and childish fancy that will vanish sufficiently from the treatment of the previous question, and there will be no need for a longer discussion. Unless perhaps they expect us to oblige them in this matter and to admit that the Mass was indeed useful, and above all profitable, to the Papist little priests, who by this subtle net have scraped together enormous revenues and countless riches from every side. But we, who approve only that usefulness which agrees with the Word of God and the salvation of the Church, condemn this usefulness not merely as useless but as deadly, since it turns men away from the purity of the Christian religion and has spread the thickest darkness over the benefit of Christ's death and passion. But now the confirmation of our view must be set forth.

units.la: CAPVT II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: OSTEAQVAM sententiam nostrā proposuimus, & quoad eius fieri potuit, explicauimus, eámq; cū aduersariorū senten- tia cōparauimus, vt ita magis eluceret huiusce disputationis statuus: iam nobis ad nostræ sententiæ confirmatione accedendum est. Quia vero recte aliquando dixit Irenæus, Euangelium, hoc est, scripta Apostolica, esse fidei nostræ fundamentum; opereprætiū erit locos Scripturæ primum substernere, ex quibus deinde ἀποδείξιν conficiamus, quæ nostræ sententiæ veritatem omnium oculos constituat. Ac ne Syllogismorum multitudo lectoribus molestiam pareret, non singulis Scripturæ locis singulos Syllogismos subiecimus: sed satis fuit uno verbo significare, quodnam argumentum ex unoquoque loco depromi possit.
units.tr: Having set out our opinion, and explained it as far as we could, and having compared it with the opinion of our opponents, so that the state of this dispute may stand out more clearly, we must now proceed to confirm our opinion. Since Irenaeus rightly said on one occasion that the Gospel, that is, the apostolic writings, is the foundation of our faith, it will be worth while first to lay down the passages of Scripture, from which we may then construct a demonstration [ἀπόδειξιν] that will set the truth of our opinion before everyone's eyes. And so that a multitude of syllogisms might not weary the readers, we have not attached a separate syllogism to each passage of Scripture. It was enough to indicate in a single word what argument could be drawn from each passage.

units.la: Lex umbram habens futurorum bonorum, non expressam formam rerum iis hostiis quæ singulis annis easdem assiduè offerunt, nunquam potest accedentes sanctificare, &c. Quapropter ingrediens mundum: Sacrificium & oblationē noluisti, corpus autem aptasti mihi: Holocautomata & hostiā pro peccato non approbasti: Tunc dixi, Ecce adsum, ut faciam, Deus, voluntatem tuam, &c. Tollit primùm ut posterius statuat.
units.tr: The law, having a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices, which they offer year by year continually, make the comers thereunto perfect, etc. Wherefore, when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: in burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure. Then said I, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God, etc. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.

units.la: Quæ sunt umbra futurorum, corpus autem, Christi.
units.tr: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is Christ's.

units.la: Habebat quidē primùm [Testamentum] constitutos religionis ritus & Sanctuarium mundanum, &c. His ita ordinatis, in primùm quidē Tabernaculum quonis tempore ingrediuntur sacerdotes qui ritus obeunt: In secundum autē semel quotannis solus Pontifex non sine sanguine quē offert pro seipso & pro populi erratis. Hoc declarante rante Spiritu Sancto, nondum patefactam fuisse viam ad Sacrarium priore Tabernaculo adhuc consistente: quod erat exemplar pro tempore illo praesenti quo dona sacrificia, offeruntur, quae non possunt conscientia sanctificare cultorem: in cibis duntaxat & potionibus & diuersis ablutionibus ac ritibus carnalibus, usque ad tempus correctionis imposita.
units.tr: The first [covenant] indeed had ordinances of divine service and a worldly sanctuary, etc. These things being thus ordained, the priests go always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the services; but into the second goes the high priest alone, once every year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the errors of the people. The Holy Spirit signifying this, that the way into the holiest was not yet made manifest while the first tabernacle still stood, which was a figure for the present time, in which both gifts and sacrifices are offered, which cannot make the worshipper perfect as touching the conscience, being only in meats and drinks and divers washings and carnal ordinances, imposed until the time of reformation.

units.la: Sacerdotes qui secundum legem offerunt dona, exemplari & umbrae deseruiunt rerum caelestium sicut diuino dictum est Mosi: Vide ut facias omnia ad exemplar quod tibi ostensum est in monte, &c.
units.tr: The priests who offer gifts according to the law serve the copy and shadow of heavenly things, as was said by divine oracle to Moses: See that thou make all things according to the pattern shown to thee in the mount, etc.

units.la: Ex his & consimilibus locis efficitur: Christum fuisse veteris Testamenti sacerdotibus & sacrificiis adumbratum.
units.tr: From these and similar passages it follows that Christ was foreshadowed by the priests and sacrifices of the Old Testament.

units.la: Ecce dies venient, dicit Dominus, cum pangam cum domo Israel & cum domo Iuda foedus nouum, &c. dum dicit nouum antiquauit prius, &c.
units.tr: Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah, etc. In saying a new covenant, he has made the first old.

units.la: Tollit prius ut posterius statuat, &c.
units.tr: He takes away the first that he may establish the second, etc.

units.la: Nihil sanctificauit Lex, sed ascita spes melior per quam appropinquamus Deo.
units.tr: The law made nothing perfect, but there is the bringing in of a better hope, by which we draw near to God.

units.la: Potioris foederis sponsor factus est Iesus.
units.tr: Jesus has been made the surety of a better covenant.

units.la: Itaque ob id noui Testamenti Mediator est, ut morte intercedente ad redemptionem earum praeuaricationum quae fuerant sub veteri Testamento, vocati, promissionem accipiant aeternae hereditatis, &c. In consummatione seculorum ad abolendum peccatum patefactus est, &c.
units.tr: And therefore he is the Mediator of the new testament, so that, by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the old testament, those who are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance, etc. In the consummation of the ages he has been revealed to put away sin, etc.

units.la: Vnus Deus, unus & Mediator Dei & hominum homo Christus Iesus qui semetipsum dedit redemptionis, &c.
units.tr: There is one God, and one Mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself a ransom, etc.

units.la: Accessistis ad noui Testamenti Mediatorem Iesum & sanguinem aspersionis, &c.
units.tr: You are come to Jesus, the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, etc.

units.la: Aduenies autem Christus Pontifex futurorum bonorum, &c. ingressus est semel in sacrarium aeternam redemptionem nactus.
units.tr: But Christ, coming as the high priest of good things to come, etc., entered once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption.

units.la: Vt misericors esset & fidelis Pontifex in iis quae apud Deum, ad expiandum peccatum populi.
units.tr: That he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

units.la: Considerate Apostolum & Pontificem professionis nostrae Iesum fidelem ei qui ipsum constituit.
units.tr: Consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Jesus, who was faithful to him who appointed him.

units.la: Habentes Pontificem magnum qui penetrauit coelos, Iesum filium Dei, teneamus professionem.
units.tr: Having a great high priest who has passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.

units.la: Christus non sibi hunc honorem tribuit vt fieret Pontifex, sed is qui dixerat ei, filius meus es tu: ego hodie genui te, &c.
units.tr: Christ did not glorify himself to be made a high priest, but he who said to him, Thou art my Son, today have I begotten thee, etc.

units.la: Talis nos decebat Pontifex, pius, innocens, impollutus, segregatus a peccatoribus, & sublimior coelis factus, &c.
units.tr: For such a high priest became us: holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens, etc.

units.la: Ex quibus consequitur ἐξ ἀνάγκης, Christum nouissimis temporibus exhibitum esse solum noui Testamenti Mediatorem ac Pontificem veteris Testamenti sacerdotio sublato, & caeremoniis abrogatis. Haec autem: Mediatorem, &, Pontificem esse noui Testamenti, ita coniuncta sunt, vt nullo modo disiungi possint: Nam Christus Mediatoris munere tunc imprimis defunctus est, quum sacerdos pro nobis factus seipsum obtulit pro peccatis nostris; ut patet ex locis superioribus, ac praesertim 1. Timot. 2. & Heb. 9.
units.tr: From these passages it follows of necessity that Christ, revealed in the last times, is the only Mediator and High Priest of the new covenant, the priesthood of the Old Testament being taken away and its ceremonies abrogated. Moreover, being Mediator and High Priest of the new covenant are so joined together that they cannot in any way be separated. For Christ performed the office of Mediator especially when, having become a priest for us, he offered himself for our sins; as is plain from the passages above, and especially from 1 Timothy 2 and Hebrews 9.

units.la: Christus dilexit nos & tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem ac victimam Deo in odorem bonae fragrantiae.
units.tr: Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweet-smelling savour.

units.la: Ut gratia Dei pro omnibus mortem gustaret, &c. per mortem aboleret eum qui mortis habet imperium, hoc est, Diabolum, & liberos redderet quotquot metu mortis per omnem vitam obnoxii erant servituti.
units.tr: That by the grace of God he might taste death for all, etc., that through death he might destroy him who has the power of death, that is, the devil, and deliver all those who through fear of death were subject to bondage all their lives.

units.la: Nunc semel in consummatione seculorum, ad abolendum peccatum per immolationem sui ipsius patefactus est, &c. Christus semel oblatus ut multorum peccatum tolleret, &c.
units.tr: Now once in the consummation of the ages he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself, etc. Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many, etc.

units.la: Qua voluntate sanctificati sumus per oblationem corporis Jesu Christi semel (factam.)
units.tr: By whose will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once (made).

units.la: Ecce agnus Dei qui tollit peccatum mundi.
units.tr: Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world.

units.la: Qui dedit semetipsum pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: Who gave himself for our sins.

units.la: Qui proprio filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit eum, &c.
units.tr: Who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, etc.

units.la: Qui dedit semetipsum pro nobis ut redimeret nos ab omni iniquitate & purificaret sibi ipsi populum peculiarem studiosum bonorum operum, &c.
units.tr: Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works, etc.

units.la: Pro eis ego sanctifico meipsum, ut sint & ipsi sanctificati per veritatem, &c.
units.tr: For their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also may be sanctified through the truth, etc.

units.la: Unica oblatione consecrauit in perpetuum eos qui sanctificantur.
units.tr: By one offering he has perfected for ever those who are sanctified.

units.la: Ex quibus consequitur Christum seipsum semel obtulisse & se tradidisse pro nobis oblationem & victimam Deo, factu sacerdotem simul & victimam,ut peccata nostra tolleret, & vnica illa oblatione eos qui sanctificantur in perpetuum consecraret.
units.tr: From these things it follows that Christ offered himself once and gave himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God, being made at once priest and victim, so that he might take away our sins, and by that one offering consecrate for ever those who are sanctified.

units.la: Vnica pro peccatis oblata hostia in perpetuum sedet ad dextram Dei.
units.tr: The one sacrifice offered for sins sits for ever at the right hand of God.

units.la: Non in manufactum sacrarium ingressus est Christus, exemplar vero sacrario respondens, sed in ipsum cœlum, ut appareat nunc in conspectu Dei pro nobis. Neq; ut sæpe offerat semetipsum, &c. alioquin oportuisset eum sæpe passum fuisse à condito mundo.
units.tr: Christ has not entered into a sanctuary made with hands, a copy corresponding to the true one, but into heaven itself, to appear now in the presence of God for us; nor that he should offer himself often, etc., for otherwise he would have had to suffer often since the foundation of the world.

units.la: Illi quidem plures facti sunt sacerdotes, quod mors prohibere eos permanere. At hic, propterea quod in æternum manet, perpetuum habet sacerdotium. Vnde & seruare prorsus potest eos qui per ipsum accedunt ad Deum, semper viuens ut interpellet pro eis, &c. Cui non sit quotidie necesse, quemadmodum illis Pontificibus, prius pro peccatis proprijs victimas offerre, deinde pro peccatis populi: Id enim fecit semel quum semetipsum obtulit, &c.
units.tr: Indeed, those priests were made many, because death prevented them from continuing. But this one, because he remains for ever, has an everlasting priesthood. Whence he is also wholly able to save those who come to God through him, always living to make intercession for them, etc. He has no daily need, as those high priests did, to offer sacrifices first for their own sins and then for the sins of the people; for this he did once, when he offered himself, etc.

units.la: Habentes Pontificem magnum qui penetrauit cœlos Iesum Filium Dei, teneamus professionem. Non enim habemus Pontificem qui non possit affici sensu infirmitatum nostrarum, sed tentatum in omnibus similiter absque peccato. Accedamus igitur cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ, ut consequamur misericordiam & gratiam inuenia mus ad opportunum auxilium.
units.tr: Having a great high priest who has passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession. For we have not a high priest who cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one tempted in all points like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and find grace to help in time of need.

units.la: Quò præcursor pro nobis ingressus est Iesus, secundum cundum ordinem Melchisedec, Pontifex factus in aeternum.
units.tr: Whither the forerunner Jesus entered for us, according to the order of Melchizedek, made a high priest for ever.

units.la: Talem habemus Pontificem qui consedit ad dextrā throni maiestatis illius cœlestis sanctuarij minister ac veri illius tabernaculi quod fixit Deus & non homo.
units.tr: We have such a high priest, who has sat down at the right hand of the throne of the majesty in the heavens, a minister of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched and not man.

units.la: Quanto magis sanguis Christi qui per seipsum æternum seipsum obtulit inculpatum Deo, purgabit conscientiam vestram à mortuis operibus ad seruiendum Deo viuo?
units.tr: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?

units.la: Qui in diebus carnis suæ quum deprecationes & supplicationes apud eum qui poterat ipsum seruare à morte, cum clamore valido, & lacrymis obtulisset, & exauditus esset, &c.
units.tr: Who, in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears to him who was able to save him from death, and was heard, etc.

units.la: Non pro eis rogo tantum, sed & pro eis qui per sermonem eorum credituri sunt in me, &c.
units.tr: I pray not for these alone, but also for those who shall believe in me through their word, etc.

units.la: Cum habeamus sacerdotem magnum præfe- ctum domui Dei, accedamus cum vero corde & certa persuasione fidei, puris cordibus à conscientia mala.
units.tr: Since we have a great priest set over the house of God, let us draw near with a true heart and a firm assurance of faith, with our hearts cleansed from an evil conscience.

units.la: Si quum inimici essemus, reconciliati fuimus Deo per mortem filij eius, multò magis reconciliati seruabimur per vitam ipsius.
units.tr: If, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, now reconciled, shall we be saved by his life.

units.la: Si quis peccauerit Aduocatum apud Patrem habemus Iesum Christum iustum, & ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris. Item, Misit filium suum vt esset propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, &c.
