units.tr: If anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, and he himself is the propitiation for our sins. Likewise: He sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins, etc.

units.la: Quis est qui condemnet? Christus is est qui mortuus est, imò verò qui etiam excitatus est, qui etiam est ad dextram Dei, qui etiam postulat pro nobis.
units.tr: Who is it that condemns? It is Christ who died, or rather who was also raised, who is also at the right hand of God, and who also makes intercession for us.

units.la: Ex superioribus locis colligitur; Christū posteaquam sese pro nobis hostiam obtulit Deo, sedere ad dextram Patris: non vt seipsū rursus offerat, sed vt prorsus eos seruet qui per ipsum accedunt ad Deum, perpetuum habens sacerdotium, & semper viuens vt interpellet pro eis: & vnici sacrificij semel in cruce peracti, ac nunquam iterandi perpetua, perfectaque virtute & efficacia, eos plenissimè Deo reconciliet, qui vera fide summum hoc beneficium recipiunt.
units.tr: From the passages above it is gathered that Christ, after he offered himself to God as a sacrifice for us, sits at the right hand of the Father, not so that he might offer himself again, but so that he might utterly save those who come to God through him. He has a perpetual priesthood and always lives to make intercession for them. By the perpetual and perfect power and efficacy of the one sacrifice, performed once on the cross and never to be repeated, he fully reconciles to God those who receive this supreme benefit by true faith.

units.la: His igitur omnibus aggregatis, nostram ἀπόδειξιν conficiamus in hunc modum.
units.tr: Therefore, having gathered all these things together, let us frame our demonstration [ἀπόδειξιν] in this way.

units.la: Ἀπόδειξις.
units.tr: Demonstration [Ἀπόδειξις]

units.la: Quem Scriptura dicit fuisse veteris Testamenti sacerdotibus sacrificiisq;, adumbratum, & nouissimis temporibus, (Veteris Testamenti sacerdotio sublato & caeremoniis abrogatis) noui Testamenti Mediatorem & Pontificem exhibitu: seipsum semel in cruce obtulisse & tradidisse pro nobis oblationem & victimam Deo: & factum esse sacerdotem simul & victimam, vt peccata nostra tolleret, & vnica illa oblatione eos qui sanctificantur in perpetuum consecraret: eaque hostia oblata, in perpetuum sedere ad dextram Dei Patris, non vt seipsum rursus offerat, sed vt prorsus eos seruet, qui per ipsum accedunt ad Deum, perpetuum habens sacerdotium, & semper viuens vt interpellet pro eis, & vnici sacrificij semel in cruce peracti ac nunquam iterandi perpetua perfectaque efficacia eos plenissime Deo reconciliet, reconciliet,qui vera fide summu hoc beneficium recipiunt: Is est solus Pontifex ac vere sacerdos noui Testamenti,& eius sacrificiu semel in cruce peractum,est vnicum,reale & externum sacrificium in Ecclesia Christiana : idemque vnicum Propitiatorium pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: Christ, whom Scripture says was foreshadowed by the priests and sacrifices of the Old Testament, and who in the last times, the priesthood of the Old Testament having been taken away and its ceremonies abrogated, was presented as Mediator and High Priest of the New Testament; who once on the cross offered and gave himself up for us as an offering and a victim to God; who was made both priest and victim, so that he might take away our sins and by that single offering consecrate for ever those who are sanctified; and who, that victim having been offered, sits for ever at the right hand of God the Father, not so that he may offer himself again, but so that he may utterly save those who come to God through him. He has a perpetual priesthood and always lives to make intercession for them, and by the perpetual and perfect efficacy of the one sacrifice, performed once on the cross and never to be repeated, he fully reconciles to God those who receive this supreme benefit by true faith. He alone is the High Priest and truly the priest of the New Testament, and his sacrifice, performed once on the cross, is the only real and external sacrifice in the Christian Church; and the same is the only propitiation for our sins.

units.la: Christum Scriptura dicit fuisse veteris Testa- menti sacerdotibus sacrificisque adumbratum, & nouissimis temporibus (veteris Testamenti sacerdotio sublato & caremonijs abrogatis) noui Testamenti Mediatorem & Pontificem exhibitum,seipsum semel in cruce obtulisse & tradidisse pro nobis,&c.
units.tr: Christ, whom Scripture says was foreshadowed by the priests and sacrifices of the Old Testament, and who in the last times (the priesthood of the Old Testament having been taken away and its ceremonies abrogated) was presented as Mediator and High Priest of the New Testament, who offered and gave himself once on the cross for us, etc.

units.la: Quare: Christus est solus Pontifex ac vere sa- cerdos noui Testamenti, & eius sacrificium semel in cruce peractum,est vnicum, reale & externum sacrificiu in Ecclesia Christiana: idemq; vnicum propitiatorium pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: Therefore: Christ alone is the High Priest and truly the priest of the New Testament, and his sacrifice, performed once on the cross, is the only real and external sacrifice in the Christian Church; and the same is the only propitiation for our sins.

units.la: Expendamus superiorem demonstratio- nem,vt facilius intelligi posit,quàm sit eui dens & necessaria, quæ sunt ϑεόθεν veræ demonstrationis.Medium non tantum describit ac designat subiectum, nempe Christu, ex veris eius notis in Scriptura propositis, (quatenus huius loci ratio postulare visa est) sed etiam continet definitionem illius Attributi quod de Christo dicitur. Perspicuum est enim ex iis locis,quibus nostra ἀπόδειξις firmissimè nititur: quid sit, esse Pontificem ac sacerdotem noui Testamenti : itémque: quid sit, sacrificium reale & externum noui Testamēti. Quæ quidem ita dicuntur per se de Christo, vt sine Christo, nec intelligi possint, nec definiri. Siquis enim quærat: quis sit sacerdos ac Pontifex noui Testamenti: respondebo eum esse, quem veteris Testamenti legales sacerdotes adumbrarunt: &c. qui perpetuum habet sacerdotium, &c. atq; vno verbo: eum qui factus est sacerdos simul & victima pro peccatis nostris. Itemq; dicam: sacrificium reale & externum noui Testamenti esse sacram illam actionem qua Christus seipsum in cruce pro nobis obtulit Deo, vt nos ab æterna morte redimeret, & cum Deo reconciliaret. Atq; ita vides eò semper esse redeundum: illud demum esse sacrificium externum & reale noui Testamenti (sicum Scriptura loqui volumus) in quo realiter & verè idem est sacerdos & victima. Ex quo fit vt necessariò nobis sit subsistendū in eo sacrificio, quod semel in cruce factum est. Omnia sunt igitur reciproca in nostra demonstratione ex legibus ac præceptis demonstrandi. Nam Christus est is, quem Scriptura dicit fuisse adumbratum legalibus sacerdotibus & factum fuisse sacerdotem simul & victimam, &c. Et vicissim, Quem Scriptura dicit adumbratum legalibus sacerdotibus, & factum sacerdote simul & victimam: is est Christus solus: Itemque Pontifex ac verè sacerdos noui Testamenti Christus solus est. Quod & retro commeat: quandoquidem,si Scriptura audimus, Christus solus est Pontifex & sacerdos noui Testamenti. Quod idem de ipsius Christi sacrificio dicendum est: vt nobis redeat superior nostra sententia: nempe Christum esse solu sacerdote noui Testamenti & ipsius Christi sacrificium in cruce peractu, esse vnicum, reale & externum sacrificium noui Testamenti: quod erat demonstrandum.
units.tr: Let us weigh the demonstration above, so that it may be more easily understood how evident and necessary are the things that belong to a true demonstration [ϑεόθεν]. The middle term does not merely describe and designate the subject, namely Christ, by his true marks set forth in Scripture (so far as the reasoning of this place seemed to require); it also contains the definition of the attribute that is said of Christ. For it is plain from the passages on which our demonstration rests most firmly what it is to be High Priest and priest of the New Testament, and likewise what the real and external sacrifice of the New Testament is. These things are said of Christ in such a way that they can be neither understood nor defined without Christ. If anyone asks who the priest and High Priest of the New Testament is, I will answer that it is the one whom the legal priests of the Old Testament foreshadowed, who has a perpetual priesthood, and, in a word, the one who was made both priest and victim for our sins. Again I will say that the real and external sacrifice of the New Testament is that sacred action by which Christ offered himself on the cross to God for us, to redeem us from eternal death and reconcile us to God. And so you see that we must always return to this point: that is the external and real sacrifice of the New Testament (if we wish to speak as Scripture does), in which the same person is really and truly both priest and victim. From this it follows that we must necessarily rest in that sacrifice which was made once on the cross. Therefore all the terms of our demonstration are reciprocal, according to the laws and precepts of demonstrating. For Christ is he whom Scripture says was foreshadowed by the legal priests and made both priest and victim, and conversely, he whom Scripture says was foreshadowed by the legal priests and made both priest and victim is Christ alone. Likewise, the High Priest and truly the priest of the New Testament is Christ alone. This also runs back again, since, if we listen to Scripture, Christ alone is the High Priest and priest of the New Testament. The same must be said of Christ's own sacrifice, so that our earlier conclusion returns to us: namely, that Christ alone is the priest of the New Testament, and that Christ's sacrifice performed on the cross is the only real and external sacrifice of the New Testament. This was to be demonstrated.

units.la: CAPVT III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: OGNITIO veritatis (inquit Augustinus) mendacium euertit: ac propterea ex superiori capite vbi sententiae nostrae veritatem ex ipsius veritatis firmamento, hoc est, ex certissimis Scripturae locis asseruimus: satis refellitur aduersariorum sententia. Veruntamen vt sequamur eū ordinem quē ipsi nobis propositimus: Pontificiorum errores de Missae sacrificio iam nobis redarguendi sunt.
units.tr: KNOWLEDGE of the truth, says Augustine, overturns falsehood. For this reason, our opponents' view is already sufficiently refuted by the previous chapter, where we established the truth of our view from the firm foundation of truth itself, that is, from the most certain passages of Scripture. Nevertheless, to follow the order we have set for ourselves, the errors of the Papists concerning the sacrifice of the Mass must now be refuted.

units.la: Pontificiorum sententia est huiusmodi: In Missa fieri verum, reale & externum seu visibile sacrificium, quo sacerdotes offerunt Deo corpus & sanguinem Christi sub speciebus panis & vini: quod quidem sacrificium est propitiatorium pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: The Papists hold the following view: in the Mass there is performed a true, real and external or visible sacrifice, by which the priests offer to God the body and blood of Christ under the appearances of bread and wine; and this sacrifice is propitiatory for our sins.

units.la: Hanc sententiam nos ita sequentibus argumentis euertimus.
units.tr: We overturn this view with the following arguments.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: OMne legitimū sacrificium nititur expressis Scripturæ verbis, ex quibus manifestum esse possit eiusmodi sacrificium fuisse à Deo institutum. Sacrificium Missæ non nititur expressis Scripturæ verbis, ex quibus manifestum esse possit eiusmodi sacrificium fuisse à Deo institutum. Quare sacrificium Missæ non est legitimum sacrificium: & vi consequentis reiciendum est.
units.tr: Every lawful sacrifice rests on the express words of Scripture, from which it can be made clear that such a sacrifice was instituted by God. The sacrifice of the Mass does not rest on express words of Scripture from which it can be made clear that such a sacrifice was instituted by God. Therefore the sacrifice of the Mass is not a lawful sacrifice, and by the force of the consequence it must be rejected.

units.la: Structus est Syllogismus in 2. fig. quia negat ὅτι ἐς, cuius partes iam explicandæ sunt.
units.tr: This syllogism is constructed in the second figure, since it has a negative conclusion; its parts must now be set out.

units.la: Maior propositio, siquidem opus habeat probatione, satis probatur ex iis quæ alibi disputauimus in loco De verbo D. scripto aduersus hum. traditiones: atque etiam num confirmari potest ex locis sequentibus.
units.tr: The major premise, if it needs proof, is sufficiently proved from what we have argued elsewhere, in the place on the written Word of God against human traditions; and it can also be confirmed from the following passages.

units.la: Frustra me colunt docentes doctrinas quae sunt mandata hominum.
units.tr: In vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines that are the commandments of men.

units.la: Hoc verbum præcepi eis, dicendo: Audite vocem meam & ero vester Deus: vos autem eritis populus meus: & ambulate in omni via quā præcepi vobis ut bene sit vobis: Illi autem non paruerunt sed ambularunt iuxta voluntates suas, et iuxta libidinem cordis sui mali, &c. ædificarunt excelsa Tophet, quod nunquam præcepera, neque in cor meum ascenderat.
units.tr: I commanded them this word, saying: Hear my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people; and walk in all the way that I have commanded you, that it may go well with you. But they did not obey, but walked according to their own purposes and the stubbornness of their evil heart, etc. They built the high places of Topheth, which I never commanded, nor did it come into my mind.

units.la: Adde frequentes reprehensiones Prophetarum quòd populus adoraret in excelsis. Item, quòd Ieroboam nouum & alienū cultum instituisset præter verbum Dei. huc etiā spectat quod Paulus dānat ἐθελοθρησκείαν. Et eiusmodi permulta, quibus recitandis non ero longior: quippe cum Pontificij id negare non soleant. Effet enim perabsurdū, licere hominibus arbitratu suo rem diuinam facere cultúmque Dei atque imprimis sacrificiū instituere. Itaque quanuis Ethnici verae Dei cognitionis expertes, passim & in vniuerso terrarum orbe sacrificarint: eorum tamen sacrificia Deus reiecit, eáque tantum accepta habuit, quae ab ipsius Spiritu profecta sunt: quemadmodum diximus in i.cap. huiusce disputationis.
units.tr: Add the frequent rebukes of the Prophets because the people worshipped on the high places; likewise, that Jeroboam instituted a new and foreign worship beside the Word of God. To this also belongs what Paul condemns as self-chosen worship [ἐθελοθρησκεία]. There are very many such passages, and I will not be longer in reciting them, since the Papists are not accustomed to deny this. For it would be utterly absurd if men were free to perform divine worship and the worship of God at their own pleasure, and above all to institute sacrifice. Therefore, although the heathen, ignorant of the true knowledge of God, offered sacrifices everywhere and throughout the whole world, God nevertheless rejected their sacrifices, and accepted only those that proceeded from his own Spirit, as we said in the first chapter of this disputation.

units.la: Minorem propositionē esse verisimam, perspicuum esse potest ex Scriptis Apostolicis. Perlegantur enim ea omnia quę Apostoli scripserunt: nusquam istud Missae sacrificium, imò ne Missae quidem vocabulum reperies. Nam quod Pontificij proferre solet, haec Christi verba: HOC FACITE, & contendunt verbū facere idem esse ac sacrificare, eò quòd Poeta aliquando dixerit, facere vitula, pro, immolare vitulam (de quo vitulino argumento plura dicemus sequenti capite, cùm Pontificiorum argumenta discutiemus) id non probat Missę sacrificium. Vt enim omittam, apud Euangelistam non agi de Missa, sed de Coenae Dominicae Sacramento: ecquis vnquam iure existimauerit illis Christi verbis contineri praeceptum sacrificandi? nec enim hic quaero, An verbū facere apud Latinos: vel verbum Asa apud Hebraeos significet aliquando sacrificare: sed affirmo, istud complexum orationis, hoc facite, nusquam, nec in sacris libris, nec in Ethnicorum scriptis idem significare ac si dicatur, sacrificate. Voluant, euoluant omnia Pontificij & ferant ἐνεργεῖν posse int. Iam eos velim mecum attendere, quam planis, expressis & dilucidis verbis sacrificia veteris Testamenti a Deo fuerint instituta, sacrificiorum ritus expositi, omnis denique sacrificiorum ratio certis legibus tam aperte fancita, ut nec de sacrificiis, nec de sacrificiorum modo dubitari vnquam possit. Cur igitur, obsecro, si Deus sacrificium aliquod reale & externum temporibus noui Testamenti, in Ecclesia Christiana esse voluit: de eo legem certam, verbis manifestis, non tulit? Quid? sacrificia legalia tam expresse & aperte fuisse instituta: hoc vero longe praestantissimum (vt isti quidem volunt) Missae sacrificium, non modo non claris & distinctis verbis institutum, sed ne nominatum quidem vnquam a Christo & ab Apostolis fuisse? Sequeretur: nouum Testamentum obscurius esse veteri Testamento: quod est ἀθεόλογον. Omnes enim veri Theologi fatentur, veteris Testamenti vmbras exorta luce Euangelica fuisse discussas. Quum igitur Missae sacrificium nullis vel Christi vel Apostolorum verbis fuerit institutum. tutum (tantùm abest vt expressis Scripturæ verbis nitatur, quod in legitimo sacrificio esse necessarium diximus) tenet nostra conclusio: commentitium esse illud sacrificiû, & idcirco reiiciendum. Ab hoc autem Syllogismo manat sequens ratiocinatio.
units.tr: That the minor premise is true can be clear from the apostolic writings. For let someone read through all that the Apostles wrote: nowhere will you find this sacrifice of the Mass, nor even the word Mass. As for what the Papists are accustomed to bring forward, the words of Christ, DO THIS, and they contend that the word facere means the same as to sacrifice, because a poet once wrote facere vitula for to sacrifice a calf (about this calf-argument we will say more in the next chapter, when we discuss the Papists' arguments), this does not prove the sacrifice of the Mass. For, to pass over the fact that the Evangelist is not speaking of the Mass but of the sacrament of the Lord's Supper, who could ever rightly think that a command to sacrifice is contained in those words of Christ? I do not here ask whether the verb facere among the Latins, or the verb Asa among the Hebrews, sometimes means to sacrifice; but I affirm that this combination of words, hoc facite, nowhere, neither in the sacred books nor in the writings of the heathen, means the same as if it were said, sacrifice. Let the Papists turn over and unroll everything and bring forward whatever they can, ἐνεργεῖν. Now I would like them to consider with me how plainly, expressly and clearly the sacrifices of the Old Testament were instituted by God; the rites of the sacrifices were set out, and finally the whole manner of the sacrifices was so openly ordained by fixed laws that no doubt could ever arise either about the sacrifices or about their mode. Why then, I beg you, if God wished some real and external sacrifice to exist in the Christian Church in the times of the New Testament, did he not lay down a fixed law about it in clear words? What? The legal sacrifices were instituted so expressly and openly, but this sacrifice of the Mass, far the most excellent (as they wish it to be), was not only not instituted in clear and distinct words, but was never even named by Christ or by the Apostles? It would follow that the New Testament is more obscure than the Old Testament, which is impious. For all true theologians confess that the shadows of the Old Testament were dispelled when the light of the Gospel arose. Since, then, the sacrifice of the Mass was instituted by no words of Christ or of the Apostles (so far is it from resting on express words of Scripture, which we said is necessary for a lawful sacrifice), our conclusion stands: that this sacrifice is invented and therefore to be rejected. From this syllogism the following reasoning flows.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: SI quoties Apostoli loquuntur de Christianorû sacrificiis, hoc est, à Christianis faciendis: proponunt spiritu lia tantùm sacrificia, nec vn-quam mentionem faciunt alicuius realis & externi sacrificij: Et nobis cum Apostolis loquendû & sentiendum est: Certè nullum externum & reale Christianorum sacrificium agnoscere debemus.
units.tr: If whenever the Apostles speak of the sacrifices of Christians, that is, sacrifices to be made by Christians, they set forth only spiritual sacrifices, and never make mention of any real and external sacrifice, then we too must speak and think with the Apostles. Certainly we ought to acknowledge no external and real sacrifice of Christians.

units.la: Verum est Antecedens: Verum igitur est consequens: & vi consequentis Missæ sacrificium reiiciendum est.
units.tr: The antecedent is true. Therefore the consequent is true too, and by the force of the consequent the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Huius Connexi Hypothetici consequentia cùm ex superiori Syllogismo, tum etiam per se satis lucet.
units.tr: The consequence of this hypothetical connection is clear enough, both from the preceding syllogism and in itself.

units.la: Assumptum patet eorum locorum induction, in quibus Apostoli de sacrificiis Christianorum loquuti sunt.
units.tr: The assumption is plain from a survey of the passages in which the Apostles spoke of the sacrifices of Christians.

units.la: Vt sistatis corpora vestra hostiam viuâ, sanctâ, acceptam Deo, rationale cultum vestrû, &c.
units.tr: That you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, your reasonable service, etc.

units.la: Peripsum Christum assiduè offeramus sacrificium laudis, id est, fructum labiorum confitentiû nomini eius.
units.tr: Through him, then, let us always offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips confessing his name.

units.la: Beneficentiæ & communicationis nolite obliui. uisci, talibus enim victimis delectatur Deus.
units.tr: Do not forget beneficence and sharing, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

units.la: Expletus sum acceptis ab Epaphrodito quae a vobis missa fuerunt, odore bonae fragrantiae, hostia Deo accepta & grata.
units.tr: I am full, having received from Epaphroditus the things sent from you, a fragrant odour, an acceptable and pleasing sacrifice to God.

units.la: Vt sim minister Iesu Christi apud Gentes, operans Euangelio Dei, vt oblatio Gentium fiat accepta sanctificata per Spiritum Sanctum.
units.tr: That I might be a minister of Jesus Christ among the Gentiles, serving the gospel of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles might become acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Si pro libamento offerar super hostia, sacrificioque fidei vestra, gaudeo & gratulor omnibus vobis.
units.tr: Even if I am poured out as a drink offering upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and congratulate you all.

units.la: Ipsi quoque vivi lapides aedificemini, domus spiritualis, sacerdotium sanctum, ad offerendum spirituales hostias acceptas Deo per Iesum Christum, &c.
units.tr: You also, as living stones, are built up as a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ, etc.

units.la: Fecit nos reges & sacerdotes Deo & Patri suo.
units.tr: He has made us kings and priests to God and his Father.

units.la: Et siqui sunt loci consimiles: In quibus omnibus perspicuum est agi de Spiritualibus sacrificiis. Iam autem admonuimus in primo cap. huius disputationis de homonymia vocabuli, cum diceremus vocabulum Sacrificij non tantum vsurpari proprie ad significandum verum, reale, visibile, & externum sacrificium: sed etiam metaphoricē, vt videre licet in locis proximè citatis. Quanuis autem in sanctis Christianorum operibus, quae per similitudinem dicuntur sacrificia, vt in eleemosina, & reliquis eiusmodi, est aliquid externum: tamen dicuntur sacrificia, non propter id quod externum est, sed propter interiorem affectum animi: ac proinde nō externa dicuntur, sed spiritualia sacrificia.
units.tr: And there are other similar passages, in all of which it is plain that spiritual sacrifices are meant. We have already noted in the first chapter of this disputation the ambiguity of the word, when we said that the word sacrifice is used not only properly, to signify a true, real, visible and external sacrifice, but also metaphorically, as can be seen in the passages just cited. Although in the holy works of Christians, which are called sacrifices by way of likeness, such as almsgiving and others of that kind, there is something external, nevertheless they are called sacrifices not because of what is external in them but because of the inward disposition of the mind. Accordingly they are not called external sacrifices but spiritual ones.

units.la: Nec me mouet quod afferunt Pontificij: nempe, nihil referre, licet Apostoli vocabu- lum ipsum sacrificij non vsurparint in hac quaestione: quandoquidem, inquiunt, nec Baptismus, nec Coena Domini ab Apostolis Sacramentum appellatur. Non enim disputamus de nominibus, aut de apicibus litera-rum, sed de re quae subest & significatur ipsis vocabulis. Ia quod pij maiores nostri intellexerunt Sacramenti nomine, idipsum Apostoli de Baptismo & de Coena Domini tradiderunt. At quod isti intelligunt nomine sacrificij, cum Missam suam nobis explicant: pernego vsquam ab Apostolis traditum fuisse. Quare perperam faciunt, qui perinde loquuntur de suo dogmate, ac si esset simplex aliquod vocabulum: quod longe secus est. Nam corpus Christi offerri Deo ab Ecclesiae Ministris, externo & reali sacrificio, eodemque propitiatorio pro peccatis (quod illi dicunt) non est vnum vocabulum, sed est dogma, quod nusquam extare in Apostolorum scriptis affirmamus. Sepe quidem Apostoli sacrificia nobis commendant, sed spiritualia: saepe victimas, hostias, oblationes proponunt, sed spirituales: nec vnquam realis & externi alicuius sacrificij a nobis faciendi meminerunt. Sunt-ne ergo Pontificij Apostolis vel perspicaciores, vel diligentiores? Quinetiam quum in Epist. ad Hebr. Apostolus de sacrificiis externis, deque ipso Christi sacrificio semel in cruce facto ita copiose differat, vt nihil supra: num, obsecro, de Missae sacrificio, & de Christo quotidie ab Ecclesiae Ministris offerendo tacuisset? atqui hoc esset rem maximi momenti & quae ad ipsius propositum maxime pertineret, omittere: quod absit ab Apostolo accuratissime in illa Epistola de sacrificiis disputante. Per Christum, inquit, offeramus assidue Deo sacrificium laudis. Non dixit, Christum offeramus, sed, per Christum. Quia vero haec repugnant: manifestum est, Pontificios cum Apostolis pugnare: & dum externum illud suum sacrificium, Apostolis incognitum, obtrudut, nec cum Apostolis loqui, nec sentire.
units.tr: Nor am I moved by what the Papists allege, namely that it makes no difference whether the Apostles used the very word sacrifice in this question, since, they say, neither Baptism nor the Lord's Supper is called a sacrament by the Apostles. For we are not disputing about names, or about the marks of letters, but about the thing that lies beneath and is signified by the words themselves. Indeed, what our godly forefathers understood by the name sacrament, the Apostles handed down in the same sense of Baptism and the Lord's Supper. But what those men understand by the name sacrifice, when they explain their Mass to us, I flatly deny was ever handed down by the Apostles anywhere. Therefore they act wrongly who talk about their dogma as though it were some simple word, which is far from the case. For that the body of Christ is offered to God by the ministers of the Church as an external and real sacrifice, and at the same time a propitiatory sacrifice for sins (as they call it), is not one word but a doctrine, which we affirm is nowhere to be found in the writings of the Apostles. Often indeed the Apostles commend sacrifices to us, but spiritual ones; often they set before us victims, sacrifices and offerings, but spiritual ones; and they never mention any real and external sacrifice to be made by us. Are the Papists then sharper-sighted or more diligent than the Apostles? Moreover, when the Apostle in the Epistle to the Hebrews discourses so fully about external sacrifices, and about the sacrifice of Christ himself, made once on the cross, that nothing could be fuller, would he, I ask, have kept silent about the sacrifice of the Mass, and about Christ being offered daily by the ministers of the Church? Yet to omit this would be a matter of the greatest moment and most pertinent to his own purpose, and that is far from the Apostle, who in that Epistle argues about sacrifices with the greatest care. Through Christ, he says, let us offer continually to God the sacrifice of praise. He did not say, let us offer Christ, but through Christ. Since these things are inconsistent, it is manifest that the Papists are at odds with the Apostles, and that in pressing their external sacrifice, unknown to the Apostles, they neither speak nor think with the Apostles.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: OMne dogma quod secum pugnat, neque potest sine contradictione explicari, ineptum est & ἑτεροδοξον.
units.tr: Every doctrine that conflicts with itself and cannot be explained without contradiction is absurd and heterodox [ἑτεροδοξον].

units.la: Dogma de Missae sacrificio secum pugnat, neque potest sine contradictione explicari.
units.tr: The doctrine of the sacrifice of the Mass conflicts with itself and cannot be explained without contradiction.

units.la: Quare dogma de Missae sacrificio ineptum est & ἑτεροδοξον: ac proinde reiiciendum.
units.tr: Therefore the doctrine of the sacrifice of the Mass is absurd and heterodox [ἑτεροδοξον], and so must be rejected.

units.la: Maiorem citra controuersiam vel ipsi Philosophi veram agnoscunt: quanto magis Theologi, qui norunt rerum sacrarum veritatem perpetuo συμφωνοῦντα, nihilque continere quod repugnet.
units.tr: Even the philosophers themselves, beyond any controversy, acknowledge the major premise as true; how much more must theologians, who know that the truth of sacred things is always in harmony [συμφωνοῦντα] and contains nothing that contradicts itself.

units.la: Minorem sic probamus: Quum Pontifici Missae suae sacrificium nobis exponunt, dicunt: illud sacrificium esse externum & simul affirmant, verum Christi corpus illic offerri Deo, sub speciebus panis & vini. At enim, si sacrificium est externum, est igitur visibile: Nullum autem sacrificium externū & visibile esse potest, quin id quod offertur, sit visibile. Sacrificium enim sine victima intelligi non potest. Quare si corpus Christi est inuisibile in Missa (vt volunt, quippe aliē nis speciebus & externis accidentibus opertum) non est igitur visibile sacrificium: si nō visibile, certè, nec externum: In externo autem & visibili sacrificio, victimam esse inuisibilem, ne fando quidem auditum est. Quæso, Misisifice Sacrificator: quid intelligis nomine sacrificij, quum ais, Missam esse externū & verum sacrificium? teipsum-ne, an altare tuum, an miras illas tuas cæremonias, cruces centies repetitas, totam denique illam tuam visibilem actionem? At ista omnia sacrificiū non faciunt. Corpus Christi, inquis, est victima. Audio: Sed: corpus Christi est ne externum? consule ipsos sensus rerum externarum indices, & illi pro te negabunt. Panis, inquis, accidentia videntur, & externa sunt. Certè: sed, aut panis accidentia offers Deo (quod negas) aut offers visibile sacrificium sine visibili victima (quod non potes) aut, visibile, &, inuisibile, externum, &, internum de vno eodemque affirmas.
units.tr: We prove the minor premise thus. When the Papists set forth to us the sacrifice of their Mass, they say that it is an external sacrifice, and at the same time they affirm that the true body of Christ is offered there to God under the appearances of bread and wine. But if the sacrifice is external, it is therefore visible; yet no external and visible sacrifice can exist without the thing offered being visible, for a sacrifice cannot be understood without a victim. Therefore if the body of Christ is invisible in the Mass (as they would have it, being covered by other appearances and external accidents), then the sacrifice is not visible; and if not visible, certainly not external either. But that a victim in an external and visible sacrifice should be invisible has never been heard of, not even in tales. I ask you, sacrificing sacrificer: what do you understand by the word sacrifice, when you say that the Mass is an external and true sacrifice? Is it yourself, or your altar, or those marvellous ceremonies of yours, the crosses repeated a hundred times, or, in short, that whole visible action of yours? But all these do not make a sacrifice. The body of Christ, you say, is the victim. I hear it. But is the body of Christ external? Consult the senses, the judges of external things, and they will deny it on your behalf. The accidents of the bread, you say, are seen and are external. Certainly; but either you offer the accidents of the bread to God (which you deny), or you offer a visible sacrifice without a visible victim (which you cannot do), or you affirm of one and the same thing both that it is visible and invisible, external and internal.

units.la: Secundò: ipsa verba quæ ad conficiendum
units.tr: Secondly, the very words that are used in consecrating

units.la: Refutatio responsionis Pontificiorum. istud Missæ sacrificium adhibentur,pugnant cum eorum sententia. Sic enim inquiunt.
units.tr: Refutation of the Papists' answer: the words used for this Mass sacrifice conflict with their opinion. For thus they say.

units.la: Te igitur clementissime pater per Iesum Christum filium tuum Dominum nostrum supplices rogamus ac petimus,vti accepta habeas & benedicas hæc dona,hæc munera,hæc sancta sacrificia illibata: imprimis quæ tibi offerimus pro Ecclesia tua, &c.
units.tr: Therefore, most merciful Father, through Jesus Christ your Son our Lord, we humbly ask and beseech you to accept and bless these gifts, these offerings, these holy unblemished sacrifices, especially those which we offer to you for your Church, etc.

units.la: Quàm apte rogetur Deus per Christum, vt Christum oblatum recipiat, viderint sacrificuli Pontificij, aut pro iis (vix enim presbyterculi illi quotidiani, vel ipsa vocabula legere possunt, nedum intelligere) viderint magni eorum & cucullati Doctores. Item,satis-ne pie rogent, vt Deus Pater Iesu Christum Filium suum acceptum habeat. Ite,An non hæc sit blasphemia potius quàm precatio,vt Deus benedicat hæc dona:dicut enim se Christum offerre. Item: si (quemadmodum vigilantes somniant) offerunt illud ipsum sacrificium quod Christus obtulit: cur ergo,sacrificia,dicunt numero multitudinis? Sed tantisper dum solutionem quærent,nos iam alia consimilia audiamus.
units.tr: How aptly God is asked, through Christ, to receive the offered Christ, let the Papists' little sacrificers see to it (for those little priests of every day can scarcely read the words themselves, let alone understand them), or let their great hooded doctors see to it. Likewise, do they pray sufficiently piously that God the Father may accept his Son Jesus Christ? Come, is this not blasphemy rather than prayer, that God should bless these gifts, since they say that they offer Christ? Again: if (as dreamers dream while awake) they offer that very sacrifice which Christ offered, why then do they speak of sacrifices in the plural number? But while they seek an answer to this, let us hear other similar prayers.

units.la: Suscipe Domine preces populi tui cum oblationibus hostiarum, &c. Item:
units.tr: Receive, Lord, the prayers of your people together with the offerings of victims, etc. Likewise:

units.la: Hostias quas tibi pro animabus famulorum, famularúmque tuarum offerimus. Item:
units.tr: The victims which we offer to you for the souls of your menservants and maidservants. Likewise:

units.la: His sacrificiis,Domine,placatus, suscipe animam famulæ tuæ à peccatis exutam,&c. Item:
units.tr: Be appeased, Lord, by these sacrifices, and receive the soul of your handmaid, freed from sins, etc. Likewise:

units.la: Propitiare quæsumus, Domine,animæ famuli tui {a}tui pro qua tibi hostias placationis offerimus. Ite: Hostias vbi, Domine, humili supplicatione pro animafamuli tui deferimus, vt per hæc salutis nostræ sacrificia perpetuä lucis beatitudinis misericordiam consequantur. Quibus superioribus aduersatur sequens eorum precatio.
units.tr: Be merciful, we beseech you, Lord, to the soul of your servant, for whom we offer to you victims of propitiation. Again: where, Lord, we bring victims in humble supplication for the soul of your servant, so that through these sacrifices of our salvation they may obtain the mercy of eternal light and blessedness. The following prayer of theirs runs counter to these earlier ones.

units.la: Pro animabus famulorum, famularumque tuarum hostiam, Domine, suscipe benignus oblatam, vt hoc sacrificio SINGVLARI, Vinculis horrēdæ mortis exuti vitam mereantur æternam.
units.tr: "Receive graciously, Lord, the victim offered for the souls of your male and female servants, so that by this SINGLE sacrifice, freed from the chains of dreadful death, they may merit eternal life."

units.la: Sic Tridentina Synodus Missæ sacrificium vocat singulare.
units.tr: Thus the Council of Trent calls the sacrifice of the Mass "single."

units.la: Hic valde æstuant Pötificij: Quidam enim, eò quòd verba illa Canonis præcedunt consecrationem, per dona, munera & sacrificia intelligunt substantiam panis & vini: atque itá suæ sententiæ de Missæ sacrificio renuntiant: sequeretur enim, nō Christum ipsum, sed panem & vinum offerri Deo in Missa, id que (vt sequitur in eorum precatione) pro animarum redemptione, quo vix aliud quicquam deteflabilius dici potest. Alij exponūt verbum præsens pro futuro, quoniam, inquiunt, mox futura est Transsubstantiatio: ac proinde verba illa de corpore & sanguine Christi exponunt. Sed corpus & sanguinem Christi, adeóque Christū ipsū dici, hostias, non, hostiam: sacrificia, non, sacrificiū, ante illa Missæ secreta, inauditū fuit. Videant etiam quàm bellè hæc sententia de corpore & sanguine Christi conueniat cū sequentibus.
units.tr: The Papists are hard pressed here. Some, because those words of the Canon come before the consecration, understand "gifts," "offerings" and "sacrifices" to mean the substance of bread and wine, and so they give up their own view of the sacrifice of the Mass. For it would follow that in the Mass not Christ himself but bread and wine is offered to God, and that for the redemption of souls (as the prayer goes on to say), than which hardly anything more detestable could be said. Others explain the present tense as the future, since, they say, transubstantiation is about to take place, and so they refer those words to the body and blood of Christ. But to call the body and blood of Christ, and so Christ himself, "victims" rather than "victim," and "sacrifices" rather than "sacrifice," before those secret prayers of the Mass, has never been heard of. Let them also see how neatly this interpretation, referring to the body and blood of Christ, agrees with what follows.

units.la: Ibid. Missalis con-tradictio. Ibid. Sessione 6. in proœmio. Pontifici sub terfugiu quæ rentes, nec in uenientes.
units.tr: Ibid. The contradiction of the Missal. Ibid. Session 6, in the preface. The Pontiffs, seeking subterfuges, neither ... [the marginal note is garbled in the scan].

units.la: Quam oblationem tu Deus in omnibus quæ-sumus benedictam, ascriptam, ratam, rationabi-lem, acceptabilemque facere digneris, ut nobis corpus & sanguis fiat dilectissimi filij tui Iesu Christi. Hæc illi. Sed si oblatio iam est cor-pus, cur rogant, ut fiat corpus? Item.
units.tr: "We beseech you, God, graciously to deign to make this offering blessed, approved, ratified, reasonable and acceptable, so that it may become for us the body and blood of your most beloved Son, Jesus Christ." So they say. But if the offering is already the body, why do they ask that it may become the body? Likewise:

units.la: Munera quæsumus, Domine, oblata sanctifi-ca. Item.
units.tr: "Lord, we beseech you, sanctify the gifts offered." Likewise:

units.la: Supra quæ propitio ac sereno vultu respicere digneris, & accepta habere sicut accepta habere dignatus es munera pueri tui iusti Abel & sa-crificium Patriarchæ nostri Abrahæ. Item.
units.tr: "Look upon them, we pray, with a kind and serene countenance, and deign to hold them accepted, as you deigned to accept the gifts of your righteous servant Abel and the sacrifice of our patriarch Abraham." Likewise:

units.la: Supplices te rogamus Omnipotens Deus, iube hæc perferri per manus sancti Angeli tui in sublı-me altare tuum, in conspectu Diuinæ maiestatis tuæ, &c.
units.tr: "We humbly beseech you, almighty God, command these things to be carried by the hands of your holy angel to your high altar, in the sight of your divine majesty, etc."

units.la: Si hæc dona, hæc munera, hæc sancta sa-crificia illibata, sunt corpus & sanguis Christi, adeoque ipse Christus: cur rogant, ut Deus hæc munera oblata sanctificet? Quid? videtur-ne illis corpus Christi sancti-ficandum, vel Christus ipse sanctificandus? Quod rogant (siquidem hæc interpre-tatio vera est) ut Deus corpus & sanguinem Christi & Christum ipsum acceptabile ha-beat? Ergo-ne Pontifici sacrificuli se me-diatores pro Christo apud Deum consti-tuunt? Imo ut Deus istam oblationem ac-ceptam habeat, Sanctorum merita proferunt, quoties in honorem Sanctorum Missas suas celebrant. Hoc autem viderint satis-ne sibi concōsentiat: videlicet celebrare Missas in memoriam Sanctorum, in quibus haec verba Christi recitant. Hæc quotiescumque feceritis in mei memoriam facietis. Porrò: cur corpus & sanguinem Christi in cœlum (ubi Christus est) deferri volunt per manus Angeli? Denique potest-ne dici quicquam absurdius, dum rogant ut corpus Christi Deus acceptum habeat, quemadmodum olim accepta habuit Abelis & Abrahami sacrificia? Explicent omnia sua sophismata Pontificij, & quantumuis licet omnia suarum distinctionum præsidia conquirant: nunquam se profecto ex his laqueis expedient quos ipsi in sese contexuerūt. Quod enim aliquando de Heraclito & Anaxagora vulgò dictum est, ipsorum sententias seipsas tollere, id verisimè de Pontificiis dici potest, Missæ sacrificium defendentibus: iisdémque Missæ sacrificium euertentibus.
units.tr: If these gifts, these offerings, these holy unblemished sacrifices are the body and blood of Christ, and so Christ himself, why do they ask that God sanctify these offered gifts? What? Do they think the body of Christ is to be sanctified, or Christ himself to be sanctified? What they ask (if this interpretation is true) is that God hold the body and blood of Christ, and Christ himself, acceptable? Do the Papist priestlings then set themselves up as mediators with God on Christ's behalf? Indeed, that God may hold this offering accepted, they bring forward the merits of the saints, as often as they celebrate their Masses in honour of the saints. But let them see whether this agrees with itself: namely, that they celebrate Masses in memory of the saints, in which they recite these words of Christ: "As often as you do these things, you will do them in remembrance of me." Further, why do they want the body and blood of Christ carried to heaven (where Christ is) by the hands of an angel? Finally, can anything more absurd be said than their request that God hold the body of Christ accepted, just as he once held accepted the sacrifices of Abel and Abraham? The Papists may unfold all their sophistries, and though they seek out every defence of their distinctions, they will never free themselves from those snares which they have woven around themselves. For what was commonly said of Heraclitus and Anaxagoras, that their opinions destroy themselves, can truly be said of the Papists who defend the sacrifice of the Mass and at the same time overturn it.

units.la: IIII.
units.tr: IIII.

units.la: OMne dogma cuius ἀντίφασις & contradictio dilucidis expresisque verbis extat in Scriptura, ab omnibus Christianis constanter repudiandum est.
units.tr: Every dogma whose contradiction [ἀντίφασις] is found in Scripture in clear and express words must be constantly rejected by all Christians.

units.la: Dogma de sacrificio Missæ est eiusmodi, ut eius ἀντίφασις & contradictio dilucidis, expresisque verbis extet in Scriptura.
units.tr: The dogma of the sacrifice of the Mass is of such a kind that its contradiction [ἀντίφασις] is found in Scripture in clear and express words.

units.la: Quare, dogma de sacrificio Missæ ab omnibus Christianis constanter repudiandum est.
units.tr: Therefore the dogma of the sacrifice of the Mass must be constantly rejected by all Christians.

units.la: Maioris propositionis veritas in promptu est.
units.tr: The truth of the major premise is plain.

units.la: Minor sic probatur. Ex illo dogmate sequitur Christum toties offerri Deo, quoties Pontifici suum illud Missae sacrificium celebrant. Cui ἀντιφατικῶς opponuntur sequentes loci.
units.tr: The minor is proved thus. From that dogma it follows that Christ is offered to God as often as the Papist priests celebrate their Mass-sacrifice. Against this the following passages stand in contradiction [ἀντιφατικῶς]:

units.la: Sanctificati sumus per oblationem corporis Iesu Christi semel [factam.]
units.tr: "We have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once [made]."

units.la: Omnis sacerdos adstat quotidie operans, & easdem saepius offerens hostias, quae nunquam possint auferre peccata: hic vero una pro peccatis oblata victima, in perpetuum sedet ad dextram Dei id quod superest expectas, donec inimicieius scabellum pedum eius fiant. Unica enim oblatione consecravit in perpetuum eos qui sanctificantur.
units.tr: "Every priest stands daily ministering, and offering often the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins; but this man, having offered one sacrifice for sins, sits for ever at the right hand of God, henceforth expecting until his enemies are made his footstool. For by one offering he has perfected for ever those who are sanctified."

units.la: Non ut saepe offerat semetipsum, sicut Pontifex ingreditur in sacrarium quotannis cum sanguine alieno (alioquin oportuisset eum saepe passum fuisse a condito mundo) sed nunc semel in consummatione saeculorum ad abolendum peccatum per immolationem sui ipsius patefactus est.
units.tr: "Not that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters the sanctuary every year with blood not his own (otherwise he would have had to suffer often since the foundation of the world); but now once, at the end of the ages, he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself."

units.la: Ut statutum est omnibus semel mori, postea vero iudicium: ita & Christus semel oblatus ut multorum peccata tolleret, altera vice absque peccato conspicietur iis qui ipsum expectant ad salutem.
units.tr: "As it is appointed for men to die once, and after that the judgment: so also Christ, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, apart from sin, to those who eagerly await him for salvation."

units.la: Christus per proprium sanguinem ingressus est semel in sacrarium, aeternam redemptionem nactus. Talis nos decebat Pontifex cui non sit quotidie necesse, quemadmodum illis Pontificibus prius pro peccatis propriis victimas offerre, deinde pro peccatis populi: id enim fecit semel quum semetipsum obtulit,&c.
units.tr: "Christ entered once into the sanctuary through his own blood, having obtained eternal redemption." Such a high priest was fitting for us, who has no need daily, as those high priests did, to offer victims first for his own sins and then for the sins of the people; for he did this once, when he offered himself, etc.

units.la: Quamobrem cum haec repugnent: Oblatio Christi unica: & Oblatio Christi non unica: item, Oblatio semel facta: & Oblatio non semel facta, sed quotidie facienda: Itemque Christus semel oblatus: & Christus non semel sed saepe oblatus: efficitur necessario, dogma istud Pontificium contradicere Scripturae, ac propterea salsissimum esse: quando quidem eius ἀντίφασις, quae in Scriptura continetur, est verissima.
units.tr: Therefore, since these things are opposed: the offering of Christ is unique, and the offering of Christ is not unique; also, an offering made once, and an offering not made once but to be made daily; likewise, Christ offered once, and Christ not offered once but often: it necessarily follows that this Papist dogma contradicts Scripture, and is therefore most false, since the contradiction which is found in Scripture is most true.

units.la: Hinc ut sese expediant Pontificij, variis subterfugiis utuntur. Nam aliquando distin̹ctionem hanc adhibent, ut dicant, oblationem Christi quae fit in Missa, non esse primariam illam oblationem, quam Christus semel fecit in cruce, sed esse oblationem commemoratiuam, & repraesentatiuam. Quod si ita est, relinquitur, ut ista Missalis oblatio non sit vera & realis oblatio corporis Christi: sed tantum verae & realis oblationis commemoratio. Nam quod est alicuius rei commemoratiuum: non est ipsa res cuius commemoratiuum est: alioqui sequeretur praeteritum tempus & praesens idem esse: quod nescio an Pontificij tueri velint. Ecce autem & alia distinctio a Pontificiis propositia: Oblationem quæ fit in Missa eandem esse oblationem quæ in cruce facta est: sed tantum differre modo & ratione. Quo vix quicquam dici potuit imperitius. Etenim is est modus oblationis Christi, vt semel & ab ipso Christo tantum fieri potuerit, quemadmodum ex Apostolo ante audiuimus: & cum ille modus necessario insit in oblatione Christi: siquis eam consideret sine hoc modo, ille profecto negabit ipsum esse ipsum, quam ignorantiam Philosophi crassissimam esse tradiderunt. Atque vt magis pateat quàm Pontifici, dum subtilissimi videri volunt, telam araneæ texant (vt hoc mutuer à Chrysostomo) atque etiam ipsam artem recte differendi violent, in qua tamen excellere videri volunt: quaedam addamus ad faciliorem huius rei explicationem.
units.tr: Hence, to extricate themselves, the Papists use various subterfuges. For sometimes they adopt this distinction, saying that the offering of Christ which takes place in the Mass is not that primary offering which Christ made once on the cross, but a commemorative and representative offering. But if this is so, it follows that this Missal offering is not a true and real offering of the body of Christ, but only a commemoration of a true and real offering. For what is commemorative of something is not the very thing of which it is the commemoration; otherwise the past tense and the present would be the same, which I do not know whether the Papists want to maintain. Yet they also put forward another distinction: that the offering made in the Mass is the same offering as that made on the cross, differing only in mode and manner. Scarcely anything more ignorant could be said. For the mode of Christ's offering is such that it could be made once only, and by Christ himself, as we heard earlier from the Apostle; and since that mode necessarily belongs to the offering of Christ, anyone who considers the offering without this mode will certainly deny that it is the same offering, a crassest ignorance, as the philosophers have taught. And so that it may be clearer how the Papists, while wishing to seem most subtle, weave a spider's web (to borrow this image from Chrysostom), and even violate the very art of right reasoning in which they wish to seem to excel, let us add a few points for an easier explanation of this matter.

units.la: Vnius euisdemque substantiæ plures ac varias esse, tum Actiones, tum Passiones etiam sine τρόπῳ παιδείας auxilio facile cuiuis perspicuum esse poterit. Rursus vnius eiusdemque hominis esse tum Actiones tum Passiones, eadem quidem specie, sed numero plures. Vt, siquis dicat eundem hominem sæpius ambulare. Denique quædam sunt Actiones & Passiones eiusmodi vt sint singulares, nec vnquam possint iterari: vt, natiuitas, mors & resurrectio Christi, quarum hæc est natura, vt semel tantum fieri potuerint.
units.tr: That a single and the same substance has many and various actions as well as passions, even without the aid of any figure of speech [τρόπου παιδείας], can easily be seen by anyone. Again, one and the same man has actions and passions which are of the same kind but numerically many, as when someone says that the same man walks often. Finally, some actions and passions are of such a kind as to be singular and can never be repeated, such as the birth, death and resurrection of Christ, whose nature is that they could happen only once.

units.la: Iam ipsa Christi oblatio, de qua disputamus, necessaria necessario ipsius mortem includit: dicitur enim semetipsum obtulisse Deo pro nobis, quia pro nobis mortuus est: Et affirmo nusquam in Scriptura Christum dici offerri Deo, nisi ratione eius mortis, ut infra copiosius dicemus. Quare si mortem tollis, simul tollis oblationem Christi, quae sine morte esse non potest. Mors enim est necessarius modus huiusce oblationis. Ex quo fit ut Actio Christi, nempe oblatio, simul inferat eiusdem Christi Passionem: cum sit Actio Christi patientis. Quamobrem, videntur Pontificij ex Actione & Passione singulari facere speciem quandam Actionis, cuius speciei, plures Actiones numero esse possint: τὸ δὲ τι cū τῶ καθ' ὅλυ confundentes. Quod si dicant esse eandem subiecto: erit igitur eadem numero, ut Philosophi tradiderunt. Atque ita, si Deo placet, una Christi oblatio, & centum milliaMissarum, erunt una numero oblatio. Ex quibus intelligitur, Pontificiorum distinctiones, tum Theologiae, tum ipsi τρόπῳ παιδείας ita aduersari, ut nulla ratione stare possint.
units.tr: Now the very offering of Christ that we are discussing necessarily includes his death. For it is said that he offered himself to God for us because he died for us. I affirm that nowhere in Scripture is Christ said to be offered to God except by reason of his death, as we shall say more fully below. So if you remove the death, you remove at the same time the offering of Christ, which cannot exist without death. For death is the necessary manner of this offering. Hence the action of Christ, namely the offering, at the same time carries with it the passion of the same Christ, since it is the action of Christ as one who suffers. Therefore the Papists seem to make out of a single action and passion a certain kind of action, of which kind there can be many actions in number, confusing [τὸ δὲ τι] with [τὸ καθ' ὅλου]. But if they say that it is the same in its subject, then it will be the same in number, as the philosophers have taught. And so, God willing, the one offering of Christ and a hundred thousand masses will be one offering in number. From this it is understood that the Papists' distinctions are so opposed both to theology and to the very way of instruction [τρόπῳ παιδείας] that they cannot stand on any ground.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: NVllum dogma quo legalium caeremoniarum umbrae renovantur recipiendum est.
units.tr: No dogma by which the shadows of the legal ceremonies are renewed is to be received.

units.la: Dogma de externo & reali Missae sacrificio est eiusmodi, ut eo legalium caeremoniarum umbrae renovantur.
units.tr: The dogma of the external and real sacrifice of the Mass is of such a kind that by it the shadows of the legal ceremonies are renewed.

units.la: Quare dogma de externo & reali Missæ sacrificio ecipiendum non est.
units.tr: Therefore the dogma of the external and real sacrifice of the Mass is not to be received.

units.la: Maioris propositionis veritas sæpe extat in scriptis Apostolicis, vt Galat.5. Coloss.2. Hebr.7.8.9.10.12.13.&c. nec eam Pontificij solent in dubium reuocare.
units.tr: The truth of the major premise often appears in the apostolic writings, as in Gal. 5, Col. 2, and Heb. 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, etc., and the Papists do not usually call it into question.

units.la: Minorem sic probamus. Sacrificia externa & realia spectasse ad legis pædagogiam & ad vmbras veteris Testamenti, manifestū est ex libris Mosis: Adde luculentissimam doctrinam Apostoli in epist.ad Hebr.vbi testatur externa illa vsque ad tempus correctionis fuisse impositā: hoc est, durasse vsque ad aduentum Christi, ac tunc fuisse abrogata. Quod si vsum externorum sacrificiorum reuoces: nonne ad veterem Legis pædagogiam regrederis? Non reuoco, inquis, legalia sacrificia. Nempe ita dicis. Verum: quid iuuat nominis mutatio, cum res ipsę propemodum eædem esse videantur? Age, dispiciamus quàm prope Missa vestra ad legales cæremonias accedat. Nunc enim idola vestra & sexcenta eiusmodi prætermitto, quibus non iam Veteris Testamenti cæremonias, sed ipsorum Ethnicorum ritus, magnopiorum omnium gemitu, estis imitati.
units.tr: We prove the minor premise thus. That external and material sacrifices belonged to the schooling of the law and to the shadows of the Old Testament is plain from the books of Moses. Add the most lucid teaching of the Apostle in the Epistle to the Hebrews, where he testifies that those external rites were imposed until the time of correction; that is, they lasted until the coming of Christ and were then abrogated. But if you revive the use of external sacrifices, do you not return to the old schooling of the Law? "I do not revive legal sacrifices," you say. Indeed you say so. But what good is a change of name, when the things themselves seem almost the same? Come, let us examine how closely your Mass approaches the legal ceremonies. For I set aside for now your idols and the countless things of that kind, by which you have imitated not the ceremonies of the Old Testament but the very rites of the heathen, to the groaning of all good men.

units.la: Legalium cæremoniarum temporibus, Tabernaculum velo distinctum fuit: In tempĺis vestris, sacerdotes, quos vocatis, ab reliquo populo cancellis & locorum discrimine separantur. In legali Tabernaculo altare tare fuit: Vos non vno, imò ne pluribus quidem altaribus, estis contenti. In Tabernaculo fuit candelabrum cum lampadibus: Tem pla vestra candelabris & lampadibus collucent. Illic sacerdos ab aliis certo & præscripto vestimenti genere differebat: Vestri sacerdotes præscriptarum vestium amictu & tunicis talaribus inuoluti non nisi lento passu in medium prodeunt. Illic sacerdotes offerebant tam pro suis quàm pro populi peccatis: Apud vos qui sacerdotes dicuntur, tam pro se quàm pro tota Ecclesia sacrificium se Deo facere profitentur. Quid thuribula, suffimenta, & reliqua eiusmodi commemorem, quæ vos à legalibus cæremoniis ad commentitia illa vestra sacra perperam traduxistis? Atque vt ad Missam vestram accedam: adeò vos hîc delectat præpostera illa veteris legis imitatio, vt ipsum etiā Missæ nomen velitis ex lege deriuatum: nempe ex Hebraico vocabulo Missa (quod sufficientiam significat) licet, Missa, Latinum esse vocabulum nemo vel mediocriter eruditus hactenus ignorauit. Cur autem Missam à sufficientia dictam esse existimetis, non video: cùm amplius centies centena Missarum millia nec viuis nec mortuis (siquidem vobis fides habenda est) hactenus suffecerint. Quinetiam siquis legales illos ritus in memoriam reuocet, quos Hebræi, Teruma, & Tenupha vocarunt, quum videlicet oblatio
units.tr: In the time of the legal ceremonies the Tabernacle was divided by a veil. In your temples the priests, whom you call such, are separated from the rest of the people by railings and by a difference of place. In the legal Tabernacle there was an altar; you are content not with one, nor even with several altars. In the Tabernacle there was a candlestick with lamps; your temples shine with candelabra and lamps. There the priest was distinguished from others by a fixed and prescribed kind of clothing; your priests, wrapped in prescribed vestments and tunics reaching to the heels, come forward into the middle only with slow step. There the priests offered both for their own sins and for the sins of the people; among you, those who are called priests profess that they offer a sacrifice to God both for themselves and for the whole Church. Why should I mention censers, incense, and the other things of this kind, which you have wrongly carried over from the legal ceremonies into your made-up sacred rites? And to come to your Mass: you take such delight in that perverse imitation of the old law that you wish even the name Mass itself to be derived from the law, namely from the Hebrew word Missa (which signifies sufficiency). Yet that Missa is a Latin word no one even moderately learned has hitherto been ignorant of. But why you think Mass was named from sufficiency I do not see, since hundreds of thousands of hundreds of Masses have so far sufficed for neither the living nor the dead (if indeed you are to be believed). Moreover, if anyone recalls those legal rites which the Hebrews called Teruma and Tenupha, when, namely, the offering

units.la: Deut. 16. vel ex azyma conspersione, vel ex frugum primitiis & rebus aliis fiebat, & res oblata sursum tollebatur à sacerdote, & variè mo- uebatur, qua postea sacerdos ipse vescere- tur: ac postea consideret quid in Pontificio- rum Missa fieri soleat,dum illi tollunt, mo- uent, ac variè tractant agitántque sua illa accidentia fine subiecto: is profecto Ponti- ficiorum Iudaizantiu κακοζηλίαν facilè ani- maduertet. Quapropter, cùm & ipsum fa- crificij externi nomen, & ipsi Missæ ritus, proximè accedant ad cæremonias veteris Testamenti,& legalibus vmbris lucem E- uangelicam obscurent: manet quod dixi- mus: dogma istud de Missæ sacrificio non esse recipiendum.
units.tr: Deut. 16. was made either from a sprinkling of unleavened cake or from first fruits and other things, and the offered thing was lifted up by the priest and variously moved, after which the priest himself would eat it; and then considers what is done in the Papists' Mass, while they lift up, move, and variously handle and toss about their accidents without any subject: he will certainly notice the Judaizing evil zeal [κακοζηλία] of the Papists. Wherefore, since both the very name of external sacrifice and the rites of the Mass itself come close to the ceremonies of the Old Testament, and obscure the Evangelical light with legal shadows, what we have said remains: the dogma of the sacrifice of the Mass is not to be received.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: SI in Missa sacrificium fit propitiatorium pro peccatis: ergo (quod absit) stare non possunt hæc Christi verba: Consummatum est: quod idem de his Apostoli verbis dicendum est.
units.tr: If the Mass is a sacrifice that propitiates for sins, then (which God forbid) these words of Christ cannot stand: It is finished. The same must be said of these words of the Apostle.

units.la: Et consummatus factus est author salutis æterna omnibus qui ipsi auscultant.
units.tr: And, being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation to all who obey him.

units.la: Vnica oblatione consummauit in perpetuum eos qui sanctificantur.
units.tr: By one offering he has perfected for ever those who are sanctified.

units.la: Christus semel oblatus vt multorum peccata tolleret.
units.tr: Christ, having been offered once, to bear the sins of many.

units.la: Deus misit filium suum vt effet propitiatio pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: God sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.

units.la: Delens quod aduersus nos erat chirographum ipsum e medio sustulit affixum cruci.
units.tr: Having blotted out the handwriting that was against us, he took it out of the way, nailing it to the cross.

units.la: Qua voluntate sanctificati sumus per oblationem corporis Iesu Christi semel.
units.tr: By that will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

units.la: Quod mortuus est, peccato mortuus est semel. Christus pro peccatis semel passus fuit: justus pro iniustis ut nos ad Deum adduceret.
units.tr: He who died has died to sin once for all. Christ suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God.

units.la: Consequens est salsissimum & blasphemum:
units.tr: The consequent is most false and blasphemous.

units.la: Falsissimum igitur & blasphemum est Antecedens.
units.tr: Therefore the antecedent is most false and blasphemous.

units.la: Et vi Consequentis: sacrificium Missæ reiiciendum est.
units.tr: And by the force of the consequence, the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexi Hypothetici consequentia patet. Nam si vnico Christi sacrificio in cruce facto peccata deleta sunt, nobisque Deus redditus est propitius: ipse etiam Christus clarissimis verbis in cruce testatus est, se tū ea omnia absoluisse quæ ad offerendum pro peccatis nostris sacrificium pertinebāt: certè nullis aliis sacrificiis locus superest, quæ sint propitiatoria pro peccatis. Idque manifestè constat ex natura perfectionis, quam verba à Christo & Apostolis vsurpata significant. Quod enim semel perfectum est, non fit adhuc: & quod adhuc fit, non est perfectum. Porrò Christi sacrificium in cruce factum, absit vt imperfectum, contra tot Scripturę testimonia, dicamus. Quod si perfectū est, quid opus est alio sacrificio propitiatorio pro peccatis? Præterea si chirographum quod aduersus nos erat, ita è medio sublatū est,vt cruci fuerit affixum; sequitur nulli alij sacrificio quàm vnico sacrificio in cruce facto remissionem peccatorum nostrorum,& ipsam pro peccatis propitiationem esse tribuendam: Vrget enim vocabulum AFFIXVM: adeò vt frustra conentur Pontificij remissionem peccatorum soli cruci & passioni Christi affixam, inde detrahere, vt eam suæ Missæ sacrificio perperam affigant.
units.tr: The consequence of the hypothetical connection is plain. For if sins have been blotted out by the one sacrifice of Christ offered on the cross, and God has been made propitious to us, then Christ himself, in the clearest words on the cross, testified that he had then completed everything that pertained to offering a sacrifice for our sins. Certainly no other sacrifices remain that could propitiate for sins. This is clearly evident from the nature of the perfection which the words used by Christ and the Apostles signify. What has been made perfect once is not still being made, and what is still being made is not perfect. Moreover, to say that Christ's sacrifice made on the cross was imperfect, far be it from us, is contrary to so many testimonies of Scripture. But if it is perfect, what need is there of another sacrifice that propitiates for sins? Furthermore, if the handwriting that was against us has been so taken out of the way that it was nailed to the cross, it follows that the forgiveness of our sins, and the propitiation itself for sins, must be ascribed to no other sacrifice than the one sacrifice made on the cross. The word NAILED presses this point. So the Papists try in vain to detach the forgiveness of sins, which is fastened to the cross and passion of Christ alone, in order to attach it wrongly to the sacrifice of their Mass.

units.la: Respondent: duos esse gradus remissionis peccatorum. Vnum, vt Deus velit reconciliari, quantum in ipso est. Alterum, vt efficaciter homines in gratiam recipiat, accedente eorum fide & poenitentia. Priore gradum esse in ipso mortis Christi sacrificio: Posteriorem verò in Missæ sacrificio inesse. Atque ad huiusce distinctionis cofirmationem proferunt 2. Cor. 5.
units.tr: They reply that there are two degrees of the forgiveness of sins. One is that God is willing to be reconciled, as far as lies in himself. The other is that he effectively receives men into grace, when their faith and repentance are added. They say the first degree is in the very sacrifice of Christ's death, but the second is present in the sacrifice of the Mass. To confirm this distinction they bring forward 2 Corinthians 5:

units.la: Deus erat in Christo mundum reconcilians sibi, non imputans eis peccata ipsorum. Et paulò post:
units.tr: God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not imputing to them their sins. And a little after:

units.la: Reconciliamini Deo.
units.tr: Be reconciled to God.

units.la: Ex hac Pontificiorum responsione ita Missæ sacrificium euertimus. Posterior gradus remissionis peccatorum ab illis assignatus, nihil aliud est quàm applicatio sacrificij Christi ad singulos homines: vt perspicuum est ex ea definitione quam afferunt: & ex Apostoli loco quem citant. Nam perinde est ac si diceret, tunc nos sacrificij Christi ac tanti beneficij esse participes, quum ipsum vera fide recipimus: quemadmodum ex Apostoli doctrina, tum fruimur reconciliatione per Christum facta, quum percepta Euangelij praedicatione, re vera, cum Deo reconciliamur.Quinetiam Tridentina Synodus definit, Missae sacrificium fuisse institutum, Vt, inquit, cruenti sacrificij salutaris virtus in remissionem eorum quae a nobis quotidie committuntur peccatorum applicaretur. Hactenus Synodus. Iam nos igitur ita concludamus: Si applicatio sacrificij propitiatorij non est ipsum sacrificium propitiatorium (nam qui rem cum rei applicatione confundit, is laborat ἀρρωστία διανοίας) & in Missa est posterior ille gradus applicationis (quemadmodum ipsi Pontificij definiunt) sequitur, in Missa non fieri sacrificium propitiatorium pro peccatis. Vrgeamus enim locum Apostoli, hoc modo.
units.tr: By this reply of the Papists we overthrow the sacrifice of the Mass in this way. The second degree of the forgiveness of sins, which they assign, is nothing other than the application of Christ's sacrifice to individual men, as is plain from the definition they themselves give and from the passage of the Apostle they cite. For it is just as if he were saying that we then become sharers in Christ's sacrifice and in so great a benefit, when we receive it by true faith; just as, according to the Apostle's teaching, we then enjoy the reconciliation made through Christ, when, having received the preaching of the gospel, we are truly reconciled to God. Indeed the Council of Trent also defines that the sacrifice of the Mass was instituted so that the saving power of the bloody sacrifice might be applied to the remission of the sins that we commit daily. So far the Council. Now let us conclude as follows: if the application of a propitiatory sacrifice is not the propitiatory sacrifice itself (for whoever confuses the thing with the application of the thing suffers from a weakness of mind [ἀρρωστία διανοίας]), and in the Mass there is that second stage of application (as the Papists themselves define), it follows that no propitiatory sacrifice for sins is made in the Mass. Let us press the Apostle's passage in this way.

units.la: Deus, inquit, reconciliauit nos sibi per Iesum Christum, dedit nobis ministerium reconciliationis. Item.
units.tr: God, he says, reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave us the ministry of reconciliation. Likewise:

units.la: Posuit in nobis (inquit) sermonem reconciliationis. Itaque nomine Christi legatione fungimur velut Deo exhortante per nos: oramus Christi nomine, reconciliamini Deo. Fecit enim ut qui non nouit peccatum, pro nobis peccatum esset, ut nos efficeremur iustitia Dei in illo. Haec Apostolus. Cum autem reconciliatio cum Deo sit effectum sacrificij Christi: duo colligo ex his Apostoli verbis. Vnum: Pastores Ecclesiae esse ministros applicationis sacrificij Chri- sti: hoc est, ministros, non faciendi (vt isti volunt) sed applicandi illius sacrificij cuius virtute cum Deo reconciliamur. Alterum: ipsam applicationem fieri, non sacrificando Christum (quod somnium est Pontificiorū) sed docendo, monendo, hortando, iis deni- que praestandis omnibus quae ad Euangelicā prædicationem pertinent. Sic enim Paulus, Dedit, inquit, nobis ministerium reconciliatio- nis. Itémque, Posuit in nobis sermonem reconci- liationis, nomine Christi legatione fungimur. Et rursus, Oramus Christi nomine: Reconciliamini Deo, &c. Itaque non dicit Apostolus: Sacri- ficamus Christū pro vobis (quin potius nos reuocat ad vnicum Christi sacrificium, quū ait Christum pro nobis factum esse peccatū, id est, oblationem pro peccato) sed: oramus, monemus, hortamur, vt cum Deo reconciliemini: nempe vt summum hoc, per Euangelij prædicatione vobis oblatum beneficium, qua decet fide ac reuerentia reci- piatis. Porrò, hac etiam in parte sibi contradicunt. Cùm enim velint sacerdotem tam pro seipso quàm pro aliis sacrificare: eúmque vetent ad altare accedere nisi post peccatorum confessionem & absolutionem: quomodo, respectu sacerdotis sacrificium istud propitiatorium pro peccatis esse potest? Vlterius etiam progredior, & affirmo, hoc commento ruere aliud Pontificiorum commentum mentum de pœnitentia, indulgentiis,& clau-uium potestate. Tradunt enim in pœnitentię sacramento (quod vocât) merita Christi dis-pensari à sacerdotibus, & ita pœnitentibus applicari vt plane à peccatis liberentur. Ob secrò, si hæc vera sunt, quorsum ergo ista Mis-salis applicatio, quam isti vocant sacrificiū propitiatorium pro peccatis? Denique, vt error alius alium trudit, quum dicunt homi-nes in gratiam recipi per Missæ sacrificium, accedente eorum fide: tollunt quod alibi af-firmat de opere (vt ipsi quidem loquuntur) operato: quod imprimis in Missæ sacrificio commendant. Maneat igitur nostra conclu-sio: nempe vnicum Christi sacrificium in cruce pro nobis oblatum ita fuisse perfectū, suisque omnibus numeris absolutum, vt rur-sus fieri neque debeat, nec etiam possit: ac propterea id esse salsissimum quod Pontifi-cij de Missæ sacrificio propitiatorio so-mniarunt.
units.tr: He has put in us, he says, the word of reconciliation. Therefore we act as ambassadors in the name of Christ, as though God were exhorting through us; we beg in Christ's name, be reconciled to God. For he made him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in him. So the Apostle. Since reconciliation with God is the effect of Christ's sacrifice, I draw two conclusions from these words of the Apostle. The first: the ministers of the Church are ministers of the application of Christ's sacrifice; that is, ministers not of making that sacrifice (as they wish) but of applying it, by whose power we are reconciled to God. The second: the application itself is made not by sacrificing Christ (which is a dream of the Papists) but by teaching, admonishing, exhorting, and by performing all those duties that pertain to the preaching of the gospel. For thus Paul says: He gave us the ministry of reconciliation. And likewise: He has put in us the word of reconciliation; we act as ambassadors in the name of Christ. And again: We beg in Christ's name: Be reconciled to God, etc. Therefore the Apostle does not say: We sacrifice Christ for you (rather he recalls us to the one sacrifice of Christ, when he says that Christ was made sin for us, that is, an offering for sin). He says: we beg, admonish, exhort you to be reconciled to God; that is, that you receive with the fitting faith and reverence this highest benefit offered to you through the preaching of the gospel. Moreover, they contradict themselves on this point as well. For since they want the priest to sacrifice both for himself and for others, and they forbid him to approach the altar unless after confession of sins and absolution, how can this sacrifice be a propitiatory sacrifice for sins with respect to the priest? I go further, and affirm that by this device another Papist fiction also collapses, concerning penance, indulgences, and the power of the keys. For they teach that in the sacrament of penance (as they call it) the merits of Christ are dispensed by priests and so applied to penitents that they are completely freed from their sins. If these things are true, why then is that application of the Mass, which they call a propitiatory sacrifice for sins, needed? Finally, as one error drags along another, when they say that men are received into grace through the sacrifice of the Mass, with their faith added, they take away what they teach elsewhere about the work (as they themselves put it) worked, which they especially commend in the sacrifice of the Mass. Let our conclusion therefore stand: the one sacrifice of Christ offered for us on the cross was so perfect and so complete in all its parts that it ought not, and indeed cannot, be made again; and therefore that is most false which the Papists have dreamed about a propitiatory sacrifice in the Mass.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: SI in Missa fit sacrificium propitiatorium pro peccatis: ergo (quod absit) irrita sunt hæc Apostoli verba:
units.tr: If a propitiatory sacrifice for sins is made in the Mass, then (God forbid) these words of the Apostle are void:

units.la: Vbi est peccatorum remissio, non est amplius oblatio pro peccato.
units.tr: Where there is remission of sins, there is no longer an offering for sin.

units.la: Purgatione peccatorum nostrorum per seipsum facta sedit ad dextram Maiestatis in excelsis.
units.tr: When he had by himself made purification of our sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

units.la: Consequens est impium.
units.tr: The consequent is impious.

units.la: Impium igitur est Antecedens : Et vi Consequentis sacrificium Missæ reiiciendum est.
units.tr: The antecedent is therefore impious: and by the force of the consequent, the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexi Hypothetici consequentia manifesta est: quia verba Apostoli ἀντιφατικῶς opponuntur iis quæ Pontifici de suo sacrificio proponūt. Nam Apostolus post remissionem peccatorum, quam Dominus noster Iesus Christus pretioso suo sanguine nobis comparauit, negat amplius esse oblationem pro peccato, quod Pontificij affirmant.
units.tr: The consequence of the hypothetical connection is plain, because the words of the Apostle are set contradictorily [ἀντιφατικῶς] against what the Papists propose about their own sacrifice. For the Apostle, after the remission of sins, which our Lord Jesus Christ obtained for us by his precious blood, denies that there is any longer an offering for sin, which the Papists affirm.

units.la: Recurrunt illi ad distinctionem primariæ oblationis, & commemoratiuæ, quam nos iam ante refutauimus. Addo etiam istam distinctionem pugnare cum Apostolo qui oblationem Christi, vnicam esse, in illo ipso loco, affirmauit. Quod autem dicitur primarium, cum ad id referatur quod secundarium est, vnicum esse non potest. Quare cum ex hac incepta (ne quid grauius dicam) Pontificiorum distinctione sequatur, plures esse Christi oblationes: Scriptura vero doceat, vnicam esse Christi oblationem: tenet superior nostra Conclusio. Quid, quod ista distinctio est extra propositum huiusce obiectionis? Quæro enim, annon ea Christi oblatione, quam vocant primariam, comparata sit peccatorum remissio? Credo no negaturos, ne innumerabiles Scripturæ locos expungere velle videantur. At si est remissio peccatorum: non amplius est oblatio pro peccato, inquit Apostolus. Quorsum igitur hæc distinctio? Expecto sane dum dicant remissionem peccatorum unam esse primariam, & alteram secundariam: ac tum huius distinctionis rationem ab illis postulabimus.
units.tr: They fall back on the distinction between a primary offering and a commemorative one, which we have already refuted before.
