I add that this distinction is at odds with the Apostle, who affirmed in that very passage that the offering of Christ is one and unique. But what is called primary, since it is related to what is secondary, cannot be unique. Therefore, since from this novel distinction of the Papists (to say nothing harsher) it follows that there are several offerings of Christ, while Scripture teaches that the offering of Christ is one, our conclusion above stands. Moreover, is this distinction not beside the point of this objection? For I ask: has not the remission of sins been procured by that offering of Christ which they call primary? I suppose they will not deny it, unless they seem willing to strike out countless passages of Scripture. But if there is remission of sins, there is no longer an offering for sin, says the Apostle. To what purpose, then, is this distinction? I certainly look forward to their saying that the remission of sins is one primary and another secondary; then we shall demand from them the reason for this distinction.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: SI in Missa fit vera, realis & externa oblatio corporis & sanguinis Christi: ergo vera & reipsa Christus in Missa occiditur.
units.tr: If in the Mass there is a true, real and external offering of the body and blood of Christ, then Christ is truly and actually slain in the Mass.

units.la: Consequens est salsissimum.
units.tr: The consequence is most absurd.

units.la: Falsissimum igitur est Antecedens. Et vi consequentis sacrificium Missae reijciendum est.
units.tr: Therefore the antecedent is most false, and by the force of the consequence the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexi Hypothetici consequentia sic probatur. Scriptura docet; Christum se pro nobis obtulisse Deo, quia pro nobis mortuus est, vt patet ex sequentibus locis.
units.tr: The hypothetical connection is proved thus. Scripture teaches that Christ offered himself to God for us, because he died for us, as the following passages make plain.

units.la: Id fecit semel quum semetipsum obtulit.
units.tr: He did this once, when he offered himself.

units.la: Quanto magis sanguis Christi qui per Spiritum aeternum seipsum obtulit inculpatum Deo purgabit conscientiam vestram, &c.
units.tr: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleanse your conscience, etc.

units.la: Neque vt saepe offerat semetipsum, &c,
units.tr: Nor that he should offer himself often, etc.

units.la: Christus semel oblatus vt multorum peccata tolleret.
units.tr: Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many.

units.la: Qui traditus est propter peccata nostra, & excitatus est propter iustificationem nostri.
units.tr: He was delivered up for our sins, and was raised for our justification.

units.la: Qui proprio filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit eum, &c.
units.tr: He who did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all, etc.

units.la: Qui dilexit me, & tradidit semetipsum pro me, &c.
units.tr: He who loved me and gave himself for me, etc.

units.la: Christus dilexit nos, & tradidit semetipsum pro nobis oblationem & victimam Deo. Christus dilexit Ecclesiam & semetipsum tradidit pro ea. Ego sum Pastor bonus. Bonus Pastor animam suam dat pro ovibus. Qui dedit semetipsum pro peccatis nostris. Qui semetipsum dedit redemptionis pretium pro quibusuis. Qui dedit semetipsum pro nobis. Qua voluntate sanctificati sumus per oblationem corporis Iesu Christi. Neque ut saepe offerat semetipsum, &c. alioquin oportuisset eum saepe passum fuisse, &c.
units.tr: Christ loved us and gave himself for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God. Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for her. I am the good Shepherd. The good Shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. He who gave himself for our sins. He who gave himself as the ransom price for all. He who gave himself for us. By that will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ. Nor that he should offer himself often, etc.; for otherwise he would have had to suffer often, etc.

units.la: Ex his & consimilibus locis (quos in hac distinctione saepius repetere & inculcare cogimur) efficitur: Christum ex usu Scripturae, non alia ratione dici offerri Deo, nisi propter veram ac realem ipsius mortem: adeo ut huius locutionis: Christus oblatus est, necessario hic fit sensus: Christus mortuus est. Affirmo nunquam aliter Scriptura loqui: ferat ἐνσασιν Pontificij, si modo possint. Quamobrem si Christus vere offertur in Missa; Christus in Missa vere occiditur: quod absit. Christus enim non amplius moritur: Mors illi ultra non dominabitur, inquit Paulus.
units.tr: From these and similar passages (which we are obliged to repeat and press again and again in this discussion) it follows that, in the usage of Scripture, Christ is said to be offered to God for no other reason than his true and real death; so that when we read "Christ was offered," the necessary sense is "Christ died." I affirm that Scripture never speaks otherwise; let the Papists bring their evasion [ἔνστασιν], if they can. Therefore, if Christ is truly offered in the Mass, Christ is truly slain in the Mass, which God forbid. For Christ does not die again; death no longer has dominion over him, as Paul says.

units.la: Respondent sacramentalem fieri immolationem Christi in Missa: propterea quod, inquiunt, vi transubstantionis separatim conficitur corpus: & separatim sanguis etiam conficitur: licet, propter concomitantiam, tiam,non fe parentur.At nos Scripturæ locū poscebamus: quorsum igitur peregrina ista & commentitia transsubstantiatio? Quis enim non videt transsubstantiationem sacrificio minimè conuenire? Nam in sacrificio nō cosiciebatur:hoc est,nō ficbat:sed confi-ciebatur,id est,occidebatur victima.Volunt autem sua transsubstantiatione facere corpus illud Christi quod offerant.Quid igitur habet illa cum sacrificio commune? Cæte-rùm hæc distinctio, & secum pugnat, & ip-sam Pontificiorū sententiam euertit.Nam corpus & sanguinem separatim confici,& propter concomitantiā corpus à sanguine non separari: hæc duo ἀντιφατικῶς & contradictorie dicuntur. Rursus si sacramentalis est: non igitur vera est immolatio. Quia sacramentale relatè dicitur, refertúrque ad τὸ ἀληθινὸν & ad eam veritatē cuius signum continet.Quòd si idem est, & sacramentū & veritas : iam periit vtriúsque relatio, quæ non potest esse sine duobus distinctis termi-nis.Adhæc si propter transsubstantiationem immolatio Christi in Missa dicitur sacra-mentalis: sequitur,transsubstantiationē esse sacramentum.Atqui: sacramentum est visi-bile: ista verò transsubstantiatio quam sin-gunt Pontificij,est plane inuisibilis: imò nō modò non corporis, sed ne animi quidem atq; intelligentiæ oculis hactenus vnquam patuit: quippe cuius rationem transsubstantiationis parentes nec intelligunt ipsi nec aliis vnquam intelligibilem reddere potuerunt: quemadmodum nos, si Dominus concesserit, peculiari hac de re instituta disputatione aliquando probabimus. Ad summa: nihil respondent Pontifici; quia proferunt testem, qui alio teste opus habet (absit enim vt somnium illud transsubstantiationis admittamus) &, quod etiam grauius est, haec distinctio sacramentalis immolationis, qua suffulciunt Missae sacrificio, confirmat nostra sententiam, nedum eam euertat. Nam si oblatio dicitur propter immolationem: & immolatio est sacramentalis: est igitur sacramentalis quoque oblatio, ac propterea non vera, nec realis: quod isti dicunt, & nos impugnamus. Forte tamen videri possint non incommode plane immolationem ad suam transsubstantiationem referre: quandoquidem ea iampridem in causa fuit, cur innumerabiles homines veram de Coena Domini doctrinam amplexi, in tota propemodum Europa, gladiis, flammisque immolati fuerint.
units.tr: The Papists answer that the immolation of Christ in the Mass is sacramental, because, they say, by the power of transubstantiation the body is consecrated separately, and the blood is also consecrated separately, though because of concomitance the body is not separated from the blood. But we were asking for a passage of Scripture; why then this foreign and invented transubstantiation? For who does not see that transubstantiation is by no means suited to a sacrifice? In a sacrifice the victim was not "made" (that is, brought into being), but "consumed" (that is, slain): the victim was killed. Yet they want their transubstantiation to make the body of Christ which they offer; so what does that have in common with a sacrifice? Moreover this distinction both contradicts itself and overturns the Papists' own position. For to say that the body and blood are consecrated separately, and that on account of concomitance the body is not separated from the blood, are two statements that are opposed [ἀντιφατικῶς] and contradictory. Again, if it is sacramental, then it is not a true immolation, because the sacramental is spoken of in relation to the true [τὸ ἀληθινὸν] and to the truth whose sign it contains. But if the sacrament and the truth are the same, then the relation between the two perishes, since a relation cannot exist without two distinct terms. Besides, if the immolation of Christ in the Mass is called sacramental because of transubstantiation, it follows that transubstantiation is a sacrament. But a sacrament is visible, whereas the transubstantiation the Papists invent is plainly invisible; indeed it has never yet appeared, not only to the eyes of the body, but not even to the eyes of the mind and understanding. Its inventors neither understand the nature of this transubstantiation themselves, nor have they ever been able to make it intelligible to others; as we shall, the Lord willing, prove at some time in a separate disputation on this matter. In short, they answer the Papist not at all, since they bring forward a witness who needs another witness (for God forbid that we should admit that dream of transubstantiation); and, what is more serious, this distinction of sacramental immolation, with which they prop up the sacrifice of the Mass, confirms our position rather than overturning it. For if the offering is called such on account of the immolation, and the immolation is sacramental, then the offering is also sacramental, and therefore not true or real; which they deny and we oppose. Yet perhaps it may not be inappropriate to say that the immolation has been referred, quite plainly, to their transubstantiation, since that doctrine has long been the cause why countless men who embraced the true doctrine of the Lord's Supper were put to death with swords and fires throughout almost the whole of Europe.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Si haec est natura veri & externi sacrificij, vt victima immutetur: & Christus iam immutari non potest: Certe Christus no potest in Missa sacrificari.
units.tr: If this is the nature of a true and external sacrifice, that the victim is changed, and Christ cannot now be changed, then certainly Christ cannot be sacrificed in the Mass.

units.la: Verum est Antecedens.
units.tr: The antecedent is true.

units.la: Verum igitur & consequens: Et vt consequentia tis sacrificium Missæ commentitium est.
units.tr: Therefore the consequent is also true, and by the force of the consequence the sacrifice of the Mass is an invention.

units.la: Connexũ Hypotheticũ fatis per fe lucet. Assumptũ habet duas partes. Prior, nempe in sacrificio victimam immutari, probatur ex iis omnibus locis qui agunt de sacrificiorum externorum ritibus, vt Exod. 29. Leuit. 1. 2. 3. &c. patet etiam eorum omnium exemplis qui vnquam sacrificia externa & victimas Deo obtulerunt. Posteriorem Assumpti partem: videlicet, Christum iam esse omnis mutationis expertem, nemo Christianus hactenus negauit.
units.tr: The hypothetical connection shines forth clearly enough in itself. The assumption has two parts. The first, namely that in a sacrifice the victim is changed, is proved from all those passages which treat of the external rites of sacrifices, such as Exodus 29 and Leviticus 1, 2, 3, etc. It is also evident from the examples of all who have ever offered external sacrifices and victims to God. As for the second part of the assumption, namely that Christ is now free from all change, no Christian has ever denied it.

units.la: Rursus illi ad suam transsubstantiationem tanquam ad asylum refugiunt, ac respondet, in suo sacrificio mutationem quoque fieri: quia substantia panis & vini (inquiunt) mutatur in corpus & sanguinem Christi. At enim si ita sit substantia, igitur panis & vini erit illa victima, quæ offertur; non autè corpus & sanguis Christi: quod tamen illi volunt. Nam isthæc mutatio, non accideret Christo, sed pani: ac proinde panis ipse esset victima. Versent se in omnes partes Pontificij: ex his tamè duobus incommodis semper in alterum incurrent: aut, panem sacrificari & offerri Deo (quod nolunt:) aut, Christo mutationè accidere: (quod absit.) Ecce quemadmodum Pontificij sine Scripturæ gubernaculo navigates, ea tempestate iactentur, vt omnino, aut in Scyllam incidant, aut in Charybdim.
units.tr: Again, they take refuge in their transubstantiation as in a sanctuary, and reply that a change also takes place in their sacrifice, because the substance of bread and wine (they say) is changed into the body and blood of Christ. But if it is so, then the victim which is offered will be the bread and wine, and not the body and blood of Christ, which nevertheless they want. For this change would not happen to Christ but to the bread, and so the bread itself would be the victim. Let the Papists turn themselves in every direction: from these two inconveniences they will always fall into one or the other. Either the bread is sacrificed and offered to God (which they do not want), or the change happens to Christ (which God forbid). See how the Papists, sailing without the rudder of Scripture, are tossed about in such a storm that they must fall either into Scylla or into Charybdis.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: SI quotidie Christus in Missa sacrificatur, ergo Christus quotidie satisfacit pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: If Christ is sacrificed every day in the Mass, then Christ makes satisfaction for our sins every day.

units.la: Consequens est falsum.
units.tr: The consequent is false.

units.la: Falsum igitur Antecedens: Et vi consequentis, Missa sacrificium reijciendum est.
units.tr: Therefore the antecedent is false; and by the force of the consequence, the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexi Hypothetici consequentia probatur ex his locis.
units.tr: The connection of the hypothetical consequence is proved from these passages.

units.la: Qui traditus est propter peccata nostra, &c. Qui semetipsum dedit redemptionis pretium pro quibusdam.
units.tr: Who was delivered up for our sins, etc. Who gave himself as a ransom for some.

units.la: Sanctificati sumus per oblationem corporis Iesu Christi semel.
units.tr: We have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once.

units.la: Si quum inimici essemus, reconciliati fuimus Deo per mortem filij eius: multò magis reconciliabimur per vitam ipsius.
units.tr: If, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more shall we be reconciled through his life.

units.la: Deus misso suo filio confirmato carni peccato obnoxiæ, de peccato damnauit peccatum in carne.
units.tr: God, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, condemned sin in the flesh.

units.la: Fecit ut qui non nouit peccatum, pro nobis peccatum esset; ut nos efficeremur iustitia Dei in eo.
units.tr: He made him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

units.la: Tradidi vobis Christum mortuum esse pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: I delivered to you that Christ died for our sins.

units.la: Qui dedit semetipsum pro peccatis nostris, ut eximeret nos è præsenti seculo malo.
units.tr: Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from the present evil age.

units.la: In quo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem ipsius, remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins.

units.la: Placuit, pace per sanguinem crucis eius facta, per Ela, per eum reconciliare nos sibi, &c.
units.tr: It pleased [the Father], having made peace through the blood of his cross, to reconcile us to himself through him, etc.

units.la: Vos quondam abalienatos & hostes nunc sanè reconciliauit in corpore carnis suæ per mortem, &c.
units.tr: You, who were once alienated and enemies, he has now reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, etc.

units.la: Purgatione peccatorum nostrorum per seipsum facta, sedit ad dextram maiestatis illius excelsissima.
units.tr: When he had made purification of our sins through himself, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

units.la: Nunc semel in consummatione seculorum ad abolendum peccatum per immolationem sui ipsius patefactus est.
units.tr: Now once, at the end of the ages, he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.

units.la: Vnica pro peccatis oblata victima in perpetuum sedet ad dextram Dei.
units.tr: One victim, offered for sins, sits forever at the right hand of God.

units.la: Qui peccata nostra pertulit in corpore suo super lignum, ut peccatis mortui, iustitiæ viueremus, cuius vibicibus sanati estis.
units.tr: Who bore our sins in his body on the tree, so that we, dead to sins, might live to righteousness; by whose stripes you have been healed.

units.la: Christus lauit nos à peccatis nostris per sanguinem suum. Quoniam mactatus es & redemisti nos Deo per sanguinem tuum.
units.tr: Christ washed us from our sins by his blood. For you were slain and redeemed us to God by your blood.

units.la: Non rebus caducis, argento vel auro fuistis redempti: sed pretioso sanguine agni immaculati.
units.tr: You were redeemed not with perishable things, silver or gold, but with the precious blood of a spotless lamb.

units.la: Ob id noui fœderis mediator est, ut morte intercedente ad redemptionem earum prævaricationum quæ fuerunt sub priore Testamento, vocati, promissionem accipiant æternæ hæreditatis.
units.tr: For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that, death intervening for the redemption of the transgressions committed under the former testament, those who are called may receive the promise of an eternal inheritance.

units.la: Hoc est sanguis meus noui Testamenti qui pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: This is my blood of the new testament, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

units.la: Exhis Scripturæ locis & plerisque aliis eôdem spectantibus, effecitur: satisfactionem pro peccatis nostris esse effectum necessarium sacrificij Christi: adeò vt, ex vsu Scripturæ, posita satisfactione pro peccatis ponatur sacrificium Christi: & vicissim,posito Christi sacrificio, ponatur satisfactio peccatis: id qp in causa σωτηρία fieri debet.
units.tr: From these passages of Scripture, and from many others bearing on the same point, it follows that satisfaction for our sins is the necessary effect of Christ's sacrifice. So much so that, by the use of Scripture, once satisfaction for sins is posited, Christ's sacrifice is posited; and conversely, once Christ's sacrifice is posited, satisfaction for sins is posited. This ought to hold in the matter of salvation [σωτηρία].

units.la: Falsitas consequentis facile colligitur ex iisdem locis: ex quibus constat satisfactionem pro peccatis semel à Christo pro nobis factam esse: tunc videlicet quum se obtulit in cruce victimam Deo pro peccatis nostris.Quinetiam hac conclusione res ipsa facillime patebit. Nam Christus pro nobis in cruce moriens, aut perfectè satisfecit Deo, aut, imperfectè. Imperfectè satisfecisse, absit à Christo redemptionis nostræ autore & effectore perfectissimo: atque id ne cogitari quidem potest ab homine verè Christiano. Si perfectè Christus satisfecit Deo, quum seipse sacrificauit in cruce pro nobis: cur, obsecrò, quotidie Christus est sacrificandus vt pro nobis satisfaciat?
units.tr: The falsity of the consequent is easily gathered from the same passages, which establish that satisfaction for sins was made once for us by Christ, namely when he offered himself as a victim to God on the cross for our sins. Moreover, the matter itself will be made very plain by this conclusion. For Christ, dying for us on the cross, either satisfied God perfectly or imperfectly. That he satisfied imperfectly is far from Christ, the most perfect author and effecter of our redemption, and such a thing cannot even be thought by a man who is truly a Christian. If Christ satisfied God perfectly when he sacrificed himself for us on the cross, then why, I beg you, must Christ be sacrificed every day so that he may satisfy for us?

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Si hodie sacrificandus esset Christus, id fieret aut vt satisfaceret pro peccatis nostris: aut vt eius satisfactio semel in cruce pro nobis facta, nobis applicaretur.
units.tr: If Christ were to be sacrificed today, this would happen either so that he might make satisfaction for our sins, or so that his satisfaction, once made for us on the cross, might be applied to us.

units.la: Neutra ratione sacrificandus est.
units.tr: For neither reason is Christ to be sacrificed.

units.la: Nulla igitur. Et vi Consequentis: Sacrificium Missæ reiiciendum est.
units.tr: Therefore for no reason. And by the force of the consequence, the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexu est perspicuum, nisi tertia ratione Pontificij proferant, qua doceat nos errasse παρὰ τὸ ἀλλοτρίως διαιρέσεως, at non possunt.
units.tr: The connection is plain, unless the Papists bring forward a third reason by which they might show that we have erred by a faulty division [παρὰ τὸ ἀλλοτρίως διαιρέσεως]; but they cannot.

units.la: Assumptum habet duo membra. Prius est: ChriChristum non esse sacrificandum vt satisfaciat pro peccatis nostris: atque id argumento, superiori proximo confecimus. Quod etiamnum confirmo sequenti ratione ad incommodum adigente. Non si hodie sacrificandus est Christus, vt satisfaciat Deo pro nobis: ergo hodie Christo patiendum & moriendum est. Si causam quaeris: attende quid sit satisfacere Deo pro nobis: quod proculdubio idem est, ac, soluere Deo quod debemus. Debemus autem mori, nisi Christus pro nobis sit mortuus. Quare dicimus, Christum Deo satisfecisse, quia Christus semel persoluit pro nobis, quatenus poenas peccatis nostris iusto Dei iudicio debitas, pro nobis pati dignatus est. Quare, aut, non plene Christus pro nobis satisfecit: (quod impium est vel cogitare:) aut, Deus eiusdem debiti solutionem bis exigit: (quod blasphemum est dicere:) aut, Satisfacere, non est soluere, hoc est, ipsum non est ipsum: quod affirmare, id non est differentis, sed delirantis.
units.tr: The assumption has two parts. The first is that Christ is not to be sacrificed so that he may make satisfaction for our sins; and we have established this by the argument above. I confirm it further by the following reasoning, which leads to an absurdity. If Christ must today be sacrificed to satisfy God for us, then Christ must today suffer and die. If you ask why: consider what it is to satisfy God for us, which undoubtedly is the same as paying God what we owe. We owe death, unless Christ has died for us. Therefore we say that Christ satisfied God because he once paid for us, in that he deigned to suffer for us the punishments owed to our sins by the just judgement of God. Hence, either Christ did not fully satisfy for us (which is impious even to think), or God demands payment of the same debt twice (which is blasphemous to say), or else to satisfy is not to pay, that is, the thing is not itself; and to affirm this is not the mark of one who differs, but of one who raves.

units.la: Posterius membrum est: Non esse hodie sacrificandum Christum, vt eius satisfactio semel in cruce facta nobis applicetur. Quod manifestum habet rationem: alioqui, necessario (vt vulgo in scholis dicitur) sequeretur implicatio contradictionis. Nam satisfactionis applicatio infert satisfactionem prius factam. At isti volunt, in ipsa applicatione esse faciendam. Repugnat autem id esse factum, & faciendum.
units.tr: The second part is that Christ need not today be sacrificed so that his satisfaction, once made on the cross, may be applied to us. The reason for this is manifest: otherwise, as is commonly said in the schools, a contradiction would necessarily follow. For the application of a satisfaction presupposes a satisfaction already made. But these men want it to be made in the very act of application. Yet for a thing to have been made and also to be made is self-contradictory.

units.la: Secundò: si iterum sacrificari debet Christus, vt eius sacrificium semel factum nobis applicetur: ergo, simili ratione; incarnari iterum debet Christus, vt fructus eius ἐνσαρκώσεως & incarnationis, nobis applicetur: iterum Christo moriendum est, vt meritum mortis eius nobis applicetur: denique debet iterum Christus resurgere, vt beneficium resurrectionis ipsius nobis applicetur; nec poterunt Pontificij rationem dissimilitudinis proferre. At nemo non sentit quàm haec incepte dicantur.
units.tr: Secondly: if Christ must be sacrificed again so that his sacrifice, once made, may be applied to us, then by the same reasoning Christ must be incarnated again, so that the fruit of his incarnation [ἐνσαρκώσεως] may be applied to us; Christ must die again so that the merit of his death may be applied to us; and finally Christ must rise again so that the benefit of his resurrection may be applied to us. Nor will the Papists be able to offer a reason for the dissimilarity. Yet everyone can see how absurdly these things are said.

units.la: Tertiò: si Missa est applicatio sacrificij Christi: non est igitur ipsum Christi sacrificium. Vt enim donatio rei, aliud est quàm res donata: ita applicatio, aliud est quàm id quod applicatur. Quartò: si in Sacramento Baptismi sacrificium Christi & mors ipsius nobis verè applicatur (ita docente Apostolo) nec tamen in Baptismo fit sacrificium (etiam Pontificiis assentientibus) nihil est causæ quamobrem necesse sit in celebranda Cœna D. fieri sacrificium, vt mortis Christi beneficium nobis applicetur.
units.tr: Thirdly: if the Mass is the application of Christ's sacrifice, then it is not Christ's sacrifice itself. For as the giving of a thing is other than the thing given, so the application is other than that which is applied. Fourthly: if in the sacrament of Baptism the sacrifice of Christ and his death are truly applied to us (as the Apostle teaches), and yet no sacrifice is made in Baptism (the Papists agreeing), then there is no reason why a sacrifice must be made in celebrating the Lord's Supper in order that the benefit of Christ's death may be applied to us.

units.la: Quintò: ea demum ratio applicandi sacrificij Christi tenenda est, quam ipse Christus instituit. Est autem duplex, vt antè dictum est: vna est, interior efficacitas Spiritus Sancti: altera, est exterior prædicatio Euangelij, & ea quæ ex ipsius Christi instituto ad Euangelicam prædicationem pertinet. Nec vsquam extat in Scriptura, Christum esse sacrificium.
units.tr: Fifthly: that method of applying Christ's sacrifice is alone to be held which Christ himself instituted. There are two, as said before: one is the inward efficacy of the Holy Spirit; the other is the outward preaching of the Gospel, together with those things which, by Christ's own institution, belong to evangelical preaching. Nor does it anywhere appear in Scripture that Christ is a sacrifice.

units.la: Rom.6. Coloss.1. erificandum,vt eius sacrificium nobis applicetur.Cùm enim sanctissimum hoc sacrificium semel in cruce factum applicetur credentibus: & fides in nobis ingeneretur a Spiritu Sancto per Euangelij prædicationem: hinc perspicuum esse potest,quæ nam sit vera ratio huiusce sacrificij nobis applicandi. Ad eam rem faciunt sequentes loci.
units.tr: Rom. 6. Col. 1. ...to be sacrificed, so that his sacrifice may be applied to us. For since this most holy sacrifice, made once on the cross, is applied to believers, and faith is engendered in us by the Holy Spirit through the preaching of the Gospel, it can be seen from this what the true way of applying this sacrifice to us is. The following passages bear on this matter.

units.la: Pro eis ego sanctifico meipsum,vt sint & ipsi sanctificati per veritatem: non pro eis autem rogo tantùm,sed & pro iis qui per sermonem eorum credituri sunt in me.
units.tr: For them I sanctify myself, that they also may be sanctified through the truth; and I pray not for them only, but also for those who will believe in me through their word.

units.la: Christi participes sumus, si modò principium illud quo sustentamur,firmum tenuerimus ad finem vsque.
units.tr: We are partakers of Christ, if indeed we hold fast the beginning of our confidence firm to the end.

units.la: Cùm habeamus sacerdotem magnum præfectum domui Dei,accedamus cum vero corde & certa persuasione fidei.
units.tr: Since we have a great priest set over the house of God, let us draw near with a true heart and a sure persuasion of faith.

units.la: Quem proposuit Deus propitiationem per fidem in sanguine ipsius.
units.tr: Whom God set forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood.

units.la: Accessistis ad nouì Testamenti mediatorem Iesum & ad sanguinem aspersionis. Et loci consimiles, ex quibus intelligitur, beneficia Christi nobis applicari fide, quam videlicet Spiritus Dei in nobis efficit & format per Euangelij prædicationem. Fateor quidem ipsam prædicationem esse aliquod sacrificij genus, nempe spiritualis & figurate dicti: quemadmodum Paulus aliquoties de prædicando Euangelio verba faciens, ad sacrificium allusit. Verùm,quid hoc ad Missæ sa-
units.tr: You have come to Jesus, the mediator of the new testament, and to the blood of sprinkling. And there are similar passages, from which it is understood that the benefits of Christ are applied to us by faith, which the Spirit of God effects and forms in us through the preaching of the Gospel. I grant indeed that the preaching itself is a kind of sacrifice, namely a spiritual one, and so called figuratively: as Paul, when at times speaking of preaching the Gospel, alluded to sacrifice. But what has this to do with the sacrifice of the Mass?

units.la: crificium? Quid, obsecrò, commune esse potest Euangelio clarè & apertè annuncianto & exposito, cum Missæ theatralibus, ac mutis signis, eiúsque perobscuris susurrationibus? Imò verò sacrificium spirituale Euangelij prædicandi, commentitio Missæ sacrificio plane repugnat. Nam quoties prædicatur Euangelium ex instituto Christi, toties Christus offertur, non Deo (quod isti de sua Missa somniant) sed nobis, vt ipsum vera fide receptum totis animis amplectamur. Quinetiam per Euangelij prædicationem, non Christus sacrificatur, sed nos ipsi Deo sacrificamus, quatenus verbi Diuini gladio spiritualiter mactati, Deo consecramur, & (vt Pauli verba vsurpemus) nostri oblatio fit accepta, sanctificata per Spiritum Sanctum. Quid plura? expendant quid sibi velit vocabulum, Applicari; & facilè intelligent, Christi sacrificium nobis applicari, dum Christus offertur, non Deo, sed nobis. Ex quibus omnibus concludo, Pontificiorum effugium de applicatione sacrificij non modò non adiuuare, sed omnino potius euertere ipsorum de Missæ sacrificio sententiam.
units.tr: What, I ask you, can the gospel have in common with the Mass, when the gospel is announced and expounded clearly and openly, while the Mass has its theatrical rites, its mute signs, and its very obscure mutterings? Indeed, the spiritual sacrifice of preaching the gospel plainly contradicts the fabricated sacrifice of the Mass. For whenever the gospel is preached according to Christ's institution, Christ is offered, not to God (as those men dream about their Mass) but to us, so that we may receive him by true faith and embrace him with our whole hearts. Moreover, through the preaching of the gospel Christ is not sacrificed; rather, we ourselves sacrifice to God, in so far as we, spiritually slain by the sword of the divine Word, are consecrated to God, and (to use Paul's words) our offering becomes acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit. What more is there? Let them consider what the word "applied" means, and they will easily understand that the sacrifice of Christ is applied to us when Christ is offered, not to God, but to us. From all this I conclude that the Papists' evasion about the application of the sacrifice not only does not help them, but altogether overturns their opinion about the sacrifice of the Mass.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: SI inter sacrificium Christi semel in cruce factum, & futurum eius aduentum vltimum, Scriptura nullum Christi sacrificium intermediū commemorat, sed affirmat, Christum Mediatorem tore & sacerdote vnicu noui Testamenti interpellare pro nobis: no aute sese pro nobis offerre: certe sacrificiu Missæ humanu est commentum.
units.tr: If, between the sacrifice of Christ once made on the cross and his future final coming, Scripture records no intermediate sacrifice of Christ, but affirms that Christ, the sole Mediator and priest of the New Testament, intercedes for us and does not offer himself for us, then certainly the sacrifice of the Mass is a human invention.

units.la: Verum est Antecedens.
units.tr: The antecedent is true.

units.la: Verum igitur & consequens. Et vi consequentis sacrificium Missæ reiciendum est.
units.tr: Therefore the consequent is true too; and by force of the consequent the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexi Hypothetici consequentia firmissima est,& nititur iis quæ alibi à nobis disputata sunt de verbi Dei scripti autoritate. Debemus enim & loqui & sentire cum Scriptura, e cuius finibus (inquiebat aliquando Hieronymus) vera Dei Ecclesia nō egreditur. Cur enim Scriptura, quum disserit de eo quod Christus facturus est ad diem vsq; nouissimum, hoc, quod isti volunt esse præcipuum fidei nostræ caput, omitteret? nempe fore vt Christus quotidie amplius centies millies sacrificetur pro nobis, vsque dum venia t viuos & mortuos iudicaturus. Rem tanti momenti, (siquidem vera esset) procul dubio clarissimis scriptis Apostoli testatam nobis reliquissent. Num dicent Pontificij, interpellare, idem esse, quod, seipsum sacrificare? Atqui ipsa interpellatio est effectum sacrificij semel in cruce facti: ac propterea dicit Apostolus sanguine aspersionis loqui.
units.tr: The consequence of this hypothetical connection is most firm, and it rests on what we have argued elsewhere about the authority of the written Word of God. For we ought to speak and think in agreement with Scripture, beyond whose limits (as Jerome once said) the true Church of God does not go. For why, when Scripture discusses what Christ is going to do until the last day, would it omit this, which our opponents want to be the chief head of our faith: namely, that Christ will be sacrificed for us every day, many more times than a hundred thousand, until he comes to judge the living and the dead? A matter of such weight, if it were true, the Apostles would undoubtedly have attested in the clearest writings and left to us. Will the Papists say that to intercede is the same as to sacrifice oneself? Yet intercession itself is the effect of the sacrifice made once on the cross; and for this reason the Apostle says that it "speaks through the blood of sprinkling."

units.la: Accessistis, inquit, ad sanguinem aspersionis præstantiora loquente quam (loqueretur) sanguis Abel. Adde hunc ordinem à Paulo obseruatum: Christū mortuum esse & excitatum, sedere ad dextram Dei & pro nobis postulare.
units.tr: "You are come," he says, "to the blood of sprinkling, which speaks better things than the blood of Abel." Add the order Paul observes: that Christ died and was raised, sits at the right hand of God, and makes intercession for us.

units.la: Iam quia semper & assiduè pro suis Christus interpellat: si interpellare, est sacrificari: sequeretur, Christum assiduè sacrificari, adeò vt matutinum tempus Missis celebrandis iam non sufficeret.
units.tr: Now, since Christ intercedes always and continually for his own, if to intercede is to be sacrificed, it would follow that Christ is sacrificed continually, so much so that the morning hours would no longer be sufficient for celebrating Masses.

units.la: Assumptum probatur his Apostoli verbis. Quis est qui condemnet? Christus (is est) qui mortuus est: imò verò qui etiam excitatus est, qui etiam est ad dextram Dei, qui etiam postulat pro nobis.
units.tr: The assumption is proved by these words of the Apostle: "Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us."

units.la: Non dicit sacrificatur pro vobis.
units.tr: He does not say, "is sacrificed for you."

units.la: Aduocatum apud Patrem habemus Iesum Christum Iustum, & ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: "We have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous; and he is the propitiation for our sins."

units.la: Christus propterea quod in aeternum manet perpetuum habet sacerdotiu: unde & seruare prorsus potest eos qui per ipsum accedunt ad Deum semper viuens vt interpellet pro eis: Talis enim nos decebat Pontifex, &c. cui non sit quotidie necesse, quemadmodum illis Pontificibus, prius pro peccatis propriis victimas offerre: deinde pro peccatis populi: Id enim fecit semel, quum semetipsum obtulit.
units.tr: "Christ, because he abides for ever, has a perpetual priesthood; whence also he is able to save completely those who come to God through him, always living to make intercession for them. For such a high priest became us, etc., who does not need daily, as those high priests did, first to offer sacrifices for their own sins and then for the sins of the people. For this he did once, when he offered himself."

units.la: Expectantes beatam illam spem & illustrem illum aduentum gloriae magni Dei & seruatoris nostri Iesu Christi: Qui dedit semetipsum pro nobis,&c.
units.tr: "Looking for that blessed hope and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us, etc."

units.la: Non in manufactum sacrarium ingressus est Christus exemplar vero sacrario respondens: sed in ipsum caelum, vt appareat nunc in conspectu Dei pro nobis. Christus semel oblatus vt multorum peccata tolleret, altera vice absque peccato conspicietur ijs qui ipsum expectant ad salutem.
units.tr: "Christ has not entered into a sanctuary made with hands, which is a copy of the true one, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us. Christ, offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, without sin, to those who wait for him for salvation."

units.la: Christus vna pro peccatis oblata victima in perpetuum sedet ad dextram Dei id quod super- est expectans: donec inimici ipsius scabellum pe- dum eius fiant. Vnica enim oblatione consecra- uit in perpetuum eos qui sanctificantur, & c.
units.tr: "Christ, having offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sits at the right hand of God, from then on waiting until his enemies are made his footstool. For by one offering he has perfected for ever those who are sanctified, etc."

units.la: En igitur quid Scriptura doceat de officio Christi Pontificis ad dextram Dei sedentis: nec vllam facit istius commentitij sacrificij mentionem: imo potius nos totos ad vnicum illud sacrificium reuocat, quod Christus in cruce pro nobis fecit; cuius ea virtus est, vt nobis liceat, non sacrificare Christum (quod Pontificij comminiscuntur) sed per Christum, semel pro nobis sacrificatum ad Deum accedere.
units.tr: Here, then, is what Scripture teaches about the office of Christ the priest, who sits at the right hand of God: it makes no mention of this fabricated sacrifice, but rather calls us back wholly to that one sacrifice which Christ made for us on the cross. Its power is such that we are allowed, not to sacrifice Christ (as the Papists invent), but through Christ, who was once sacrificed for us, to draw near to God.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: SI in Missa Christus vere offertur Deo a Pontificiis sacerdotibus: ergo Christus non est solus sacerdos noui Testamenti.
units.tr: If in the Mass Christ is truly offered to God by the Papist priests, then Christ is not the only priest of the New Testament.

units.la: Consequens est falsum.
units.tr: The consequent is false.

units.la: Est igitur falsum Antecedens: Et vi consequentis sacrificium Missae reijciendum est.
units.tr: Therefore the antecedent is false, and by the force of the consequence the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexi Hypothetici consequentia manifeste patet. Solus enim sacerdos, & plures sacerdotes, dicuntur ἀντιφαλικῶς.
units.tr: The consequence of the hypothetical connection is plainly evident. For "only priest" and "several priests" are opposites [ἀντιφαλικῶς].

units.la: Assumptum: nempe Christum esse solum sacerdotem noui Testamenti, verbis expressis docet Apostolus. Christus non sibi hunc honorem tribuit vt fieret Pontifex, sed is qui dixerat ei: filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te; sicut & alibi dicit: Tu es sacerdos in aeternum secundum ordinem Melchisedec.
units.tr: The assumption, namely that Christ is the only priest of the New Testament, the Apostle teaches in express words: Christ did not take this honour to himself, to become a high priest, but he who said to him, "You are my Son, today I have begotten you"; as he also says elsewhere, "You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek."

units.la: Et illi quidem plures facti sunt sacerdotes, quod mors prohibere eos permanere: At iste propterea quod in aeternum manet, perpetuum habet sacerdotium, &c.
units.tr: Indeed, those priests were made many in number, because death prevented them from remaining; but this one, because he remains for ever, has a priesthood that does not pass to another, etc.

units.la: Perspicuum est igitur Christum esse solum sacerdotem noui Testamenti, quia est sacerdos secundum ordinem Melchisedec, adhibito Dei iureiurando, constitutus Rex simul & sacerdos, adeoque sacerdos in aeternum, vt Scriptura docet. Ex quo necesse est, vt solus Christus sit noui Testamenti sacerdos: quippe cui soli haec conueniant.
units.tr: It is therefore clear that Christ is the only priest of the New Testament, because he is a priest after the order of Melchizedek, appointed with God's oath, a king and priest at once, and so a priest for ever, as Scripture teaches. From this it necessarily follows that Christ alone is the priest of the New Testament, since these things belong to him alone.

units.la: Hic Pontifici distinguunt inter primarium sacerdotem (quem agnoscunt esse Christum) & secundarios sacerdotes: quos innumerabiles esse volunt; quorum ministerio Christus sese offerat Deo. Sed quaero; cum sacerdotes veteris Testamenti ad venturum Christum referrentur: annon essent ipsius Christi respectu, secundarij sacerdotes, adeoque typus & figura Christi aeterni sacerdotis suo tempore exhibendi. Atqui postquam primarius sacerdos exhibitus est; Apostolus istis secundariis sacerdotibus locum vllum superesse noluit, nec alios secundarios sacerdotes noui Testamenti illis superioribus subsubstituit; sed in vno Christo subsistit, æterno sacerdote secundum ordinem Melchisedec. Quare ista distinctio falsa est: quia evertit ipsam Apostoli sententiam. Primarium enim & secundarium, no pugnant: quia sunt subordinata. At Apostolus ita opponit Christum hominibus sacerdotibus, vt eos no patiatur simul stare posse. Si ergo vlli sunt secundarij sacerdotes, profecto ruit argumentum Apostoli, & ea oppositio quam in illo loco proposuit. Dices; Apostolum excludere legales sacerdotes: Certe: sed adhibet ea rationem, quæ non minus quadrat in Pontificios sacrificulos, quàm in sacerdotes veteris Testamenti: his enim Christum opponit; nempe mortalibus immortale: quod profecto æquè de Pontificiis sacrificulis dici potest. Notissima autem est hæc regula τρόπῳ παιδείας: Cui ratio & perfectum medium Conclusionis conuenit; eidem ipsam Conclusionem conuenire. [Secundo: cum legalibus omnibus sacrificiis adumbratum sit vnicum illud Christi sacrificium quod in cruce factum est (teste Apostolo ad Heb.) obsecro te, quid amplius opus est sacerdotibus, posteaquam semel patefacta fuit veritas illis veteribus, tum sacrificiis adumbrata? Quorsum igitur Pontificij sacerdotes? An vt significent futurum Christi sacrificium? At hoc salsissimum est. Sacrificatus est enim Christus, inquit Paulus,
units.tr: Here the Papists distinguish between the primary priest (whom they acknowledge to be Christ) and secondary priests, whom they hold to be innumerable, and through whose ministry Christ offers himself to God. But I ask: since the priests of the Old Testament were referred to the Christ who was to come, would they not, in relation to Christ himself, be secondary priests, and so a type and figure of the eternal priest who was to be displayed in his time? But now that the primary priest has been displayed, the Apostle would allow no place for those secondary priests, nor did he substitute any other secondary priests of the New Testament in place of those earlier ones; but he rests in the one Christ, the eternal priest after the order of Melchizedek. Therefore this distinction is false, because it overthrows the very judgment of the Apostle. For primary and secondary do not conflict, since they are subordinate to one another. But the Apostle so sets Christ against mortal priests that he does not allow them to stand together. If therefore there are any secondary priests, surely the Apostle's argument and the opposition he set out in that passage collapse. You will say that the Apostle excludes the legal priests. Certainly; but he uses a reason that fits the Papist little priests no less than the priests of the Old Testament: for he sets Christ over against them, namely the immortal against the mortal, which can with equal truth be said of the Papist little priests. Moreover, this rule of the τρόπῳ παιδείας is very well known: whatever belongs to the reason and the perfect middle term of a conclusion, the same belongs to the conclusion itself. [Second: since the whole legal sacrificial system foreshadowed that one sacrifice of Christ which was made on the cross (as the Apostle teaches in Hebrews), I beg you, what further need is there of priests, once the truth which those old sacrifices foreshadowed has been revealed? Why then do the Papist priests exist? Is it to signify the future sacrifice of Christ? But this is most absurd. For Christ, says Paul, has been sacrificed,

units.la: 1.Cor.4 non, sacrificandus. An vero vt significent saſ‑ctum Christi sacrificiũ? At hic significandi modus continet contradictionē : contradicere autē, non est, significare, vel, repraesentare. Ecquid enim absurdius vnquā dici posſit: Christum esse quotidie sacrificandũ, vt significemus, Christũ semel fuisse sacrificatum? huc tamē redit Pontificiorū sententia.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 4 not to be sacrificed. Or is it rather to signify the sacrifice of Christ already accomplished? But this mode of signifying involves a contradiction; and to contradict is not the same as to signify or represent. For what could be said more absurd than that Christ must be sacrificed every day, in order that we may signify that Christ was sacrificed once? Yet this is where the opinion of the Papists comes to.

units.la: Tertiò: ista distinctio pugnat cum natura ipsius rei de qua agitur: volunt enim Pontificij a suis sacerdotibus Christum sacrificari. Atenim ea est natura huiusce sacrificij, vt a nullo alio fieri potuerit quam ab ipso primario sacerdote, nempe Christo. Quo fit vt in sacrificio Christi distinctio primarij & secundarij sacerdotis sit ineptissima: quia res haec ad solum primarium sacerdote pertinet. Sic enim Apostolus, In secundum sacrarium (inquit) semel quotannis solus Pontifex [ingreditur] non sine sanguine quem offert pro seipso & pro populi erratis: Hoc declarante Spiritu Sancto, nondum patefactam fuisse viam ad sacrarium, priore Tabernaculo adhuc consistente, &c. Adueniens autem Christus Pontifex futurorum bonorum per proprium sanguine ingressus est semel in sacrarium, &c. Docet igitur Apostolus, sacrificium Christi fuisse ad viuum expressum legali illa caeremonia, quũ summus sacerdos solus in intimum sacrarium semel ingrediebatur: atque ita significabat sacrificium illud perfectissimū a solo Christo Christo. sto vere summo sacerdote tandem aliquan-do semel faciendum. Quamobrem nihil hic opus est secundariis sacerdotibus.
units.tr: Thirdly: this distinction conflicts with the very nature of the matter under discussion. For the Papists want Christ to be sacrificed by their priests. But the nature of this sacrifice is such that it could be performed by no one other than the primary priest himself, namely Christ. Hence in Christ's sacrifice the distinction between primary and secondary priest is most inept, because this matter pertains to the primary priest alone. For the Apostle says, Into the second tabernacle the high priest alone went once a year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people. The Holy Spirit thereby showed that the way into the sanctuary had not yet been opened while the first tabernacle still stood, etc. But Christ, coming as the high priest of the good things to come, entered once into the sanctuary through his own blood, etc. The Apostle therefore teaches that Christ's sacrifice was vividly expressed by that legal ceremony, in which the high priest alone entered the innermost sanctuary once; and so that most perfect sacrifice signified was one to be made once, at last, by Christ alone, the true high priest. Therefore there is no need here for secondary priests.

units.la: Quartò: si sacerdotes Pontificij sunt tantum ministri sacrificii quod fit in Missa, Christus autem est primarius ac verus sacerdos, qui sacrificium illud facit, ut dicunt: cum sacerdotes Pontificij offerant tam pro se, quàm pro populo: sequeretur, Christum (absit dicto blasphemia) etiam pro se offerre. Nam ministerium & instrumentum referri ad causam efficientem, fortasis isti non ignorant. Quid fiet igitur his Apostoli verbis? Cui non sit quotidie necesse quemadmodum illis Pontificibus prius pro peccatis propriis victimas offerre, deinde pro peccatis populi. Id enim fecit semel quum semetipsum obtulit, &c. Annon, obsecro, qui volut noui Testamenti temporibus esse sacerdotes, qui sacrificium offerat Deo, tam pro se quàm pro peccatis populi: ij, tum superioribus Apostoli verbis, tum Evangelicae veritati bellum indixerunt?
units.tr: Fourthly: if the Papist priests are only ministers of the sacrifice that is made in the Mass, while Christ is the primary and true priest who performs that sacrifice, as they say, then, since the Papist priests offer both for themselves and for the people, it would follow that Christ (let not the word be taken as blasphemy) offers also for himself. For they perhaps are not unaware that a minister and an instrument are referred to the efficient cause. What then will become of these words of the Apostle? He has no need, as those high priests did, to offer sacrifices daily, first for his own sins and then for the sins of the people. For he did this once, when he offered himself, etc. Surely, I beg you, those who want there to be priests in the times of the New Testament, to offer a sacrifice to God both for themselves and for the sins of the people, have declared war on the preceding words of the Apostle and on the truth of the Gospel?

units.la: Quintò: hanc distinctionem ipsi Pontificij refellunt. dicunt enim Missae sacrificium esse ipsum Christi sacrificium quod in cruce oblatum est. Atqui, solus Christus sese in cruce obtulit, sine vllo ministerio secundariorum sacerdotum. Alterum igitur negent necesse est: aut esse idem sacrificium: aut, sacrificium in Missa fieri ministerio secundariorum sacerdotum. Vtrumque autem esse falsum, commentitiū & ἑτεροδόξον, freti certissimis rationibus, affirmamus. Nisi forte Pontificij suos illos innumerabiles sacrificulos velint cum ea cohorte ac turba multa, & cum iis militibus comparare, quorum opera & ministerio Christus prehensus fuit & in crucem actus. Qua in re, habeat sane locum vocabulum, Secundarij, pro quo tantopere laborant. Nam, quantum in ipsis est, Christum secundario quodam modo in crucem agunt: idq;, pretio numerato (quod etiam de Iuda Iscariote memoriæ proditum est) libenter, si liceret, Euangelicam veritatem e medio sublaturi. Sed de secundariis mortis Christi ministris, hactenus.
units.tr: Fifthly: the Papists themselves refute this distinction. For they say that the sacrifice of the Mass is the very sacrifice of Christ which was offered on the cross. But Christ alone offered himself on the cross, without any ministry of secondary priests. Therefore they must deny one of two things: either that these are the same sacrifice, or that the sacrifice in the Mass is made through the ministry of secondary priests. But we, relying on the most certain reasons, affirm that both are false, fabricated and heterodox [ἑτεροδόξον]. Unless perhaps the Papists wish to compare their innumerable little sacrificers with that band and great crowd, and with those soldiers by whose work and ministry Christ was seized and driven to the cross. In that matter the word "secondary", for which they labour so hard, would certainly have its place. For, so far as lies in them, they bring Christ to the cross in a secondary way, and that gladly, for a sum of money counted out (as is also recorded of Judas Iscariot), if they were allowed to remove the Gospel truth from the midst. But so much for the secondary ministers of Christ's death.

units.la: XIIII.
units.tr: XIIII.

units.la: SI ea est ratio sacerdotij Christi vt sit idē sacerdos qui victima: & Christus solus est victima illa semel pro nobis oblata: certè solus Christus est sacerdos.
units.tr: If the priesthood of Christ is of such a kind that the same person is both priest and victim, and Christ alone is that victim, offered once for us, then certainly Christ alone is priest.

units.la: Antecedens verum est.
units.tr: The antecedent is true.

units.la: Verum igitur est Consequens: & vi Consequentis sacrificium Missæ reiiciendum est.
units.tr: Therefore the consequent is true, and by force of the consequent the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexum hypotheticum patet ex prima illa cognitione Eiusdem & Diuersi; quæ ex primæ Philosophiæ fotibus hauriri solet.
units.tr: The hypothetical connection is plain from that first insight into the Same and the Different, which is usually drawn from the sources of first philosophy.

units.la: Assumptum omnes verè Christiani fatentur, neque id negant Pontificij: ac proinde, salvo pudore, vim superioris Consequentis negare non possunt.
units.tr: All true Christians confess the assumption, and the Papists do not deny it. Therefore, if they have any shame, they cannot deny the force of the preceding consequence.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: XV.
units.tr: XV.

units.la: {a}SI qui noui Testamenti sacerdos est, idem quoque Mediator est noui Testamenti, & solus Christus est noui Testamenti mediator: Certè, Christus solus est noui Testameti sacerdos.
units.tr: {a}If the one who is priest of the New Testament is also the Mediator of the New Testament, and Christ alone is the Mediator of the New Testament, then certainly Christ alone is priest of the New Testament.

units.la: Verum est Antecedens.
units.tr: The antecedent is true.

units.la: Verum igitur est Consequens: Et vi Consequentis Missæ sacrificium reiiciendum est.
units.tr: Therefore the consequent is true, and by force of the consequent the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexum hypotheticum perspicuum est ex ijs quæ in Connexo superiore proximo dicta sunt.
units.tr: The hypothetical connection is clear from what was said in the immediately preceding connection.

units.la: Assumptum habet duo membra: Prius est: Eum qui noui Testamenti sacerdos est, esse quoque noui Testamenti Mediatorem: quæ doctrina est Apostoli ita scribentis.
units.tr: The assumption has two parts. The first is that the one who is priest of the New Testament is also its Mediator. This is the teaching of the Apostle, who writes thus:

units.la: Christus excellentius ministerium sortitus est, quò præstantioris est Testamenti Mediator.
units.tr: Christ has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as he is the Mediator of a better covenant.

units.la: Itaque ob id noui Testamenti Mediator est, ut morte intercedente ad redemptionem earum prævaricationum quæ fuerant sub priore Testamento, vocati, promissionem accipiant æternæ hæreditatis: nam ubi Testamentum est, mors testatoris intercedat necesse est.
units.tr: And for this reason he is the Mediator of the New Testament, so that, death having intervened for the redemption of those transgressions which were under the former Testament, those who have been called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance. For where there is a testament, the death of the testator must necessarily intervene.

units.la: Accessistis ad noui Testamenti Mediatore Iesum & sanguinem aspersionis præstantiora loquentem quàm [loqueretur sanguis] Abel.
units.tr: You have come to Jesus, the Mediator of the New Testament, and to the sprinkling of blood that speaks better things than [does the blood of] Abel.

units.la: Mediator Dei & hominum homo Christus Iesus: qui semetipsum dedit redemptionis pretium pro quibus-vis, &c.
units.tr: The Mediator between God and men is the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as the price of redemption for all, etc.

units.la: Ex quibus perspicuum est, Christum officio Mediatoris & sacerdotis simul functum esse: atq; hæc duo ita in Scriptura coniungi, vt necesse sit eum qui sit noui Testamenti Sacerdos, esse quoque noui Testamenti Mediatorem.
units.tr: From these passages it is plain that Christ has discharged the office of Mediator and of priest at once, and that these two offices are so joined together in Scripture that the one who is priest of the New Testament must also be its Mediator.

units.la: Posterius membrum Assumpti est: Christum solum esse noui Testamenti Mediatorem: quod expressis verbis testatur Apostolus, inquiens: Vnus Deus, vnus etiam Mediator Dei hominum homo Christus Iesus. Firmum igitur manet Consequens nostri Connexi. Nec enim sacrificuli Pontificij possunt esse verè sacerdotes noui Testamenti, quin sint etiam (quod absit) Mediatores inter Deū & homines, ac proinde Redemptores Ecclesiæ. Loquor autem de nomine sacerdotis proprie sumpto: quemadmodum iam admonui in primo capite huiusce disputationis. Nam propter sacrificia Spiritualia, fideles omnes dicuntur sacerdotes in Scriptura. Et qui Euangelium annunciant, quatenus Spirituali gladio immolant & consecrant homines Deo, ea ratione per quandam similitudinem dici possunt sacerdotes (quanquam non memini nomen, ἱερεύς, vsquam illis tribui in Scriptis Apostolicis) nec dubium est quin eo respexerint veteres: qui Præfectos ac Pastores Ecclesiæ, sacerdotes appellarunt. Sed nos de veris sacerdotibus loquimur, verum, reale, externúmque sacrificium offerentibus: quales Pontificij suos sacrificulos nobis describunt.
units.tr: The second part of the assumption is that Christ alone is the Mediator of the New Testament. The Apostle testifies this in express words, saying: There is one God, and one Mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. The consequence of our connection therefore stands firm. For the Papist little priests cannot be true priests of the New Testament without also being (God forbid) Mediators between God and men, and so Redeemers of the Church. I am speaking, however, of the name priest taken in its proper sense, as I have already warned in the first chapter of this disputation. For on account of spiritual sacrifices all the faithful are called priests in Scripture. And those who proclaim the Gospel, inasmuch as they slay with the spiritual sword and consecrate men to God, may for that reason be called priests by a certain likeness (though I do not recall the word priest [ἱερεύς] being applied to them anywhere in the apostolic writings). And there is no doubt that the ancient writers had this in view when they called the presidents and pastors of the Church priests. But we are speaking of true priests, who offer a true, real and external sacrifice, such as the Papists describe for us in their little priests.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: SI Sacramentum Cœnæ Domini institutū est ut Christus nobis offeratur vera fide & summa cum reuerentia percipiendus: & repugnet, Christum nobis offerri à Deo,&,Christū à nobis offerri,vel, sacrificari Deo: certè Christus non offertur, vel, sacrificatur Deo,in Sacramento Cœnæ Domini: Quantò igitur minus in Missa?
units.tr: If the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper was instituted so that Christ might be offered to us, to be received with true faith and the greatest reverence, and if it is inconsistent for Christ to be offered to us by God and also offered or sacrificed to God by us, then certainly Christ is not offered or sacrificed to God in the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper. How much less, then, in the Mass?

units.la: Antecedens verum est.
units.tr: The antecedent is true.

units.la: Verum igitur Consequens: Et vi Consequentis Missæ sacrificium reiiciendum est.
units.tr: Therefore the consequent is true, and by virtue of the consequent the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexū hypotheticū satis patet ex eorū oppositorū natura, quæ simul esse nō possūt: Id enim habeamus necesse est, cp offerimus: &,aliquid nobis offertur, vt id habeamus.
units.tr: The hypothetical connection is sufficiently clear from the nature of those opposites which cannot exist together. For we must have that which we offer, and something must be offered to us in order that we may have it.

units.la: At enim,inquiunt,Deus dederat Israëlitis victimas quas ipsi Deo, offerebāt: & in Missa dicitur: Deus tuis donis offerimus. Ego verò Missa nihil moror,cōtradictionibus,nō minus quàm crucibus abundante. De victimis autē Israëlitarū exceptio plane est ἑτερογενὴς. Nos enim nō de donis externis hic agimus: sed de Christo nobis oblato in Cœna Domini, non à nobis offerendo.
units.tr: But, they say, God gave the Israelites victims which they themselves offered to God, and in the Mass it is said: "God, we offer to you your own gifts." But I make no account of the Mass, which abounds in contradictions no less than in crosses. The exception about the victims of the Israelites is plainly heterogeneous [ἑτερογενὴς]. For we are not here dealing with external gifts, but with Christ offered to us in the Lord's Supper, not to be offered by us.

units.la: Assumpti pars prior:nēpe,CœnæD. Sacramentū institutū esse, vt Christus nobis offeratur vera fide percipiēdus:probatur ex ipsa Christi Institutione, quam Euangelistæ commemorat: neque id in dubiū reuocari solet.
units.tr: The first part of our assumption, namely that the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper was instituted so that Christ might be offered to us to be received with true faith, is proved from Christ's own institution, which the evangelists record. Nor is this usually called into doubt.

units.la: Quod addimus in posteriori parte Assūpti nostri: si Christus nobis offertur, eū à nobis non offerri : Pontificij sibi videntur tollere hac responsione. In Coena Domini esse tum sacrificium, tu Sacramentum: ac proinde non repugnare, alio atque alio respectu, Christu, una eademque actione, offerri Deo & nobis: ac prof rut sacramenta legalia: vt Agni Paschalis ceremoniam quam illi dicut fuisse sacramentum, simul & sacrificiu: quadoquidem vocatur Courban Num. 9. Sed hec respoſio nihil est aliud quam principij petitio. Nos enim haec duo pernegamus: Coena D. esse sacrificiu, nempe externu & reale: itemque Missam habere aliquid cum Coena D. comune. Affirmamus aute Coenam D. esse Sacramentu, quo Christus nobis offertur: neque idPotificij negant: ia quod addunt, Sacramentu Coene D. esse simul sacrificiu reale & externu: hoc vero pernegamus. Suam illi sententiam, non modo no expressis, sed nullis Christi verbis confirmare possut: nos Christi verbis apertis expresfisq; nostram sententia confirmamus. Etenim Sacr. Coenę D. institutu esse, vt Christu nobis oblatu vera fide recipiamus, manifeste probat hęc Christi verba: Accipite, comedite, hoc est corpus meum: Ite, Bibite ex eo omnes: Ite, Probet seipsum homo, & ita de pane illo edat, et de poculo illo bibat: Ite, Poculu benedictionis cui benedicimus, none communio sanguinis Christi est? Panis que fragimus, none communio corporis Christi est? Quonia unus panis, unu corpus multi sumus, na omnes unius panis simus participes. Ecce tibi clarissima verba de manducādo Christi corpore: nulla verò extāt de sacrificādo. Nō eni, offerte, dixit: sed, accipite: nō dixit, sacri ficate: sed, manducate: nec Paulus dixit, panē quē frangimus esse sacrificiū: sed, cōmunio-ne corporis Christi. Denique nō ait Paulus, sacerdotes in Coena D. perimendo panis sub-stantiam, Christū sacrificare: sed, nos omnes vnius panis esse participes, affirmauit. Neque hūc accersenda fuit vetus cæremonia de Pa-schate ad probandū Coenæ D. sacrificiū. Nā in illo Sacramento legali (de quo infrà plu-ribus agendū erit) agnum fuisse immolan-dū, perspicuum est ex ipsa Institutione: & no-minatim vocatur, oblatio: licet nō fuerit sa-crificium proprie dictum, vt exponemus suo loco. Sed vt Christus ab Ecclesia Christiana immoletur vel offeratur: nulla vnquā lege, vel à Christo, vel ab Apostolis, sancitum est. Præterea nō valeret hoc ratiocinādi genus: Si Sacramenta quædam legalia fuerūt simul externa sacrificia: Ergo idem de Sacramen-tis Ecclesiæ Christianæ censendum est. Nam, vt in superioribus diximus, externa omnia sacrificia vnicū idémq; perfectissimū Chri-sti sacrificiū abrogauit: ne mihi dicendū sit, veterē illā cæremoniā non fuisse institutā, vt Agnū Deus afferret Israelitis, & simul Agnā ab Israelitis Deo offerretur: quod tamē Pō-tificij de Christo in illo suo sacrificio tradi-derunt. Mitto dicere, quàm absurdū sit, nos primùm offerre ChristūDeo in sacrificio, ac postea Christum nobis offerri in Sacramento. Quomodo enim Christum offerimus, si Chriftū non habemus? Hæc igitur dici præposterè (vt alia prętermittā) nemo nō videt: acproinde manet superior nostra Conclusio.
units.tr: What we add in the latter part of our assumption, that if Christ is offered to us he is not offered by us, the Papists seem to think they overturn by this reply: that in the Lord's Supper there is both a sacrifice and a sacrament, and so there is no inconsistency in Christ being offered to God and to us in one and the same action, in different respects. They compare the legal sacraments, such as the ceremony of the Passover lamb, which they say was at once a sacrament and a sacrifice, since it is called korban, Num. 9. But this reply is nothing other than begging the question. For we deny both of these points: that the Lord's Supper is a sacrifice, namely an external and real one, and likewise that the Mass has anything in common with the Lord's Supper. We affirm, however, that the Lord's Supper is a sacrament by which Christ is offered to us, and the Papists do not deny this. What they add, that the sacrament of the Lord's Supper is at the same time a real and external sacrifice, this we flatly deny. They cannot confirm their opinion not only by no express words, but by no words of Christ at all; we confirm ours by the clear and express words of Christ. For that the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper was instituted so that we might receive Christ offered to us with true faith is plainly proved by these words of Christ: "Take, eat, this is my body"; "Drink from it, all of you"; "Let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of that cup"; "The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? Because we, being many, are one bread and one body, for we all partake of the one bread." Behold, clear words about eating Christ's body; but none exist about sacrificing it. For he did not say "offer," but "take"; he did not say "sacrifice," but "eat." Nor did Paul say that the bread we break is a sacrifice, but "the communion of the body of Christ." Finally, Paul does not say that priests, by consuming the substance of the bread in the Lord's Supper, sacrifice Christ; he affirmed that we all are partakers of the one bread. Nor should the old ceremony of the Passover be brought in to prove a sacrifice in the Lord's Supper. For in that legal sacrament (which will have to be treated at greater length below) it is clear from the institution itself that a lamb was to be slain, and it is expressly called an offering, although it was not a sacrifice properly so called, as we shall explain in its place. But that Christ should be sacrificed or offered by the Christian Church was never decreed by any law, either by Christ or by the apostles. Moreover, this kind of reasoning would not hold: if certain legal sacraments were at the same time external sacrifices, therefore the same must be judged of the sacraments of the Christian Church. For, as we said above, Christ's one and most perfect sacrifice abrogated all external sacrifices. I need not say that the old ceremony was not instituted so that God should bring the lamb to the Israelites while at the same time the lamb was offered to God by the Israelites, which nevertheless the Papists have handed down about Christ in their sacrifice. I pass over saying how absurd it is that we first offer Christ to God in sacrifice and afterwards Christ is offered to us in the sacrament. For how do we offer Christ if we do not have Christ? That these things should be said in a topsy-turvy way (to pass over others) no one fails to see, and therefore our conclusion stands.

units.la: XVII.
units.tr: XVII.

units.la: SI in Cœna Domini Christus nobis offertur semel pro nobis sacrificatus: Ergo non a nobis in ipsa Cœna sacrificandus: Quanto igitur minus in Missa?
units.tr: If Christ is offered to us in the Lord's Supper as the one who was sacrificed once for us, then he is not to be sacrificed by us in the Supper itself. How much less, then, in the Mass?

units.la: Antecedens verum est, Verum & Consequens: Et vi Consequentis Missæ sacrificium reiiciendum est.
units.tr: The antecedent is true, and the consequent too; and by the force of the consequent the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexum hypotheticum negari nō potest: ne in ἀντίφασιν incurramus.
units.tr: The hypothetical connection cannot be denied, lest we fall into a contradiction [ἀντίφασιν].

units.la: Assumptum probant hæc Christi verba: Accipite, comedite: hoc est corpus meũ quod pro vobis datur. Hoc est corpus meũ quod pro vobis frangitur. Hoc est sanguis meus noui Testamenti qui pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum. Ex quibus intelligitur, in Cœnæ Domini Sacramento, nos totos ad Christi Passionē ac mortē reuocari, qua semel se pro nobis obtulit, vt nos cum Deo reconciliaret.
units.tr: The assumption is proved by these words of Christ: Take, eat; this is my body, which is given for you. This is my body, which is broken for you. This is my blood of the new Testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. From these words it is understood that in the sacrament of the Lord's Supper we are all led back to the passion and death of Christ, by which he once offered himself for us, that he might reconcile us to God.

units.la: Respondent, Christum seipsum in Cœna sacrificasse: atq; id volūt efficere ex verbis illis, Datur, frangitur, effunditur, in præsenti tempore vsurpatis. Sed miror istos homines sibi ipsis oculos vltro perstringere, ne videat apertissimā enallagen qua Christus de re iam instanti & mox futura, tanquā de præsenti, loquebatur: hoc autē loquēdi genus pasim occurrere, cūm ex multis aliis, tū ex his Scri pturæ locis manifestissimū est. Væ homini illi per quem Filius hominis proditur. Filius hominis traditur in manus peccatorū. Abeo & venio ad vos. Pro eis ego sanctifico meipsum. Pro onibus meis. Ire Paul° de suo martyrio iam iā instanti: Ego iā libor & tempus meæ resolutionis instat, & huiusmodi pleraq;. Hinc factū est, vt in Euang. Matth. hebraicè cōscripto, vsurpe tur futurū tempus. Quinetiā vetus Interpres (quē illi vulgò sequi solēt) verbū Græcū præ sētis temporis expresit per futurū: sic enim interpretatus est apud Matthæum & Lucam: Sanguis meus qui pro multis effundetur: & apud Paulum, Corpus meum quod pro vobis tradetur. Quid, quòd ne illiipsi suam Missa audiūt, quā statuūt ab omnibus audiendā esse? Sic enim extat in Canone Missę, adeoq; in ipsa Cōse- cratione, in qua siquid peccetur, actū est de ipsa Trāsfubstātiatione, quā tamē volūt esse sui sacrificij fūdamentū. Hic est enim calix sanguinis mei noui & æterni Testamenti. Mysterium fidei, qui pro vobis & pro multis effundetur in remissionem peccatorum. Imò, ne ipsi se audiūt quidē. Suprà enim in argumento 3. quū suis ipsi laqueis irretiti tenerētur, coacti fūt hæc verba suiCanonis, Hæc dona, hæc munera, quæ tibi offerimus, &c. exponere per enallagē de re mox futura (vt illi quidē aiebāt: quā bene suo loco diximus) idem autem in his Christi verbis faciendum esse non vident. Denique, exponunt vtroque modo, &, per futurum tempus, &, per praesens simul; nō solùm res ipsas, sed etiam vocabula & verborum tempora confundentes; quo nihil vnquam stultius, addo etiam, imprudentius, dici potuit. Fundetur sanguis (inquiunt) in cruce: funditur autem in ipsa Coenae actione, nempe incruente. O acutos homines, sed longè acutiores futuros, si semel nobis explicare potuerint, ecquanam ratione sanguis incruentè fundi posset! Sanguis enim aut verè dicitur fundi, aut per similitudinem. Si per similitudinem: non est verum & reale sacrificium in Missa. Si verè dicitur fundi; non igitur incruentè: nam incruentum excludit sanguinis fusionem; nisi forte isti homines sua omnia confundentes & contradictionibus inuoluentes, nouum aliquod rerum omnium chaos in mundum inuehant: quod profectò facerent, nisi lux Euangelica ipsorum tenebris obsisteret. Hoc igitur commentum, seu, portentum de immolatione Christi facta ab ipso Christo in sacra Coena: his rationibus procul à nobis eiicimus.
units.tr: They reply that Christ offered himself in the Supper, and they wish to establish this from those words, is given, is broken, is poured out, which are used in the present tense. But I marvel that these men blind their own eyes, so that they do not see the very plain enallage by which Christ spoke of a matter that was now at hand and soon to come, as if it were present; and that this manner of speaking occurs everywhere, as is plain both from many other passages and from these places of Scripture: Woe to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed. The Son of man is delivered into the hands of sinners. I go away and come to you. For them I sanctify myself. For all my own. Paul speaks of his martyrdom, now at hand: I am already being poured out, and the time of my departure is at hand, and very many similar examples. Hence it happens that in the Gospel of Matthew, written in Hebrew, the future tense is used. Indeed, the old translator (whom they are commonly accustomed to follow) rendered the Greek present tense by the future: so he translated it in Matthew and Luke, My blood which is shed for many shall be poured out, and in Paul, My body which is for you shall be given up. What of the fact that they do not even hear their own Mass, which they declare must be heard by all? For this stands in the Canon of the Mass, and so in the consecration itself, in which, if anything is mispronounced, the whole matter of transubstantiation is at stake, which nevertheless they want to be the foundation of their sacrifice: For this is the cup of my blood of the new and eternal Testament. The mystery of faith, which shall be poured out for you and for many for the remission of sins. Indeed, they do not even hear themselves. For above, in the third argument, when they were held fast entangled in their own snares, they were compelled to explain these words of their own Canon, These gifts, these offerings, which we offer to you, etc., by enallage, as referring to a matter soon to come (as they then said, which we rightly discussed in its place); yet they do not see that the same must be done with these words of Christ. Finally, they explain them in both ways, both by the future tense and by the present at once, confusing not only the things themselves but also the words and the tenses of the verbs; nothing more foolish, I add also more imprudent, could ever be said. The blood, they say, was to be shed on the cross; but it is poured out in the very action of the Supper, namely without blood. O clever men, who would be far more clever if they could once explain to us in what way blood could be shed without blood! For blood is said to be shed either truly or by way of likeness. If by way of likeness, then there is no true and real sacrifice in the Mass. If it is truly shed, then it is not without blood: for "without blood" excludes the shedding of blood; unless perhaps these men, confusing all things and entangling them in contradictions, are bringing into the world some new chaos of all things, which they would certainly do, were it not that the light of the Gospel resists their darkness. Therefore we cast out this invention, or rather monstrosity, of an immolation of Christ made by Christ himself in the holy Supper, on these grounds:

units.la: Prima ratio: quia rerum naturam euertit, & extinguit primariam illam lucem nostrae cognitionis: De quolibet veram esse affirmationem, aut negationē. Hinc enim sequitur, sanguinem non sanguinem, fundi, non fundi,praesens & futurum tempus idem esse.
units.tr: The first reason: because it overturns the nature of things and extinguishes that primary light of our knowledge, that of any thing an affirmation or a denial is true. For from this it follows that blood is and is not shed, and that the present and future tenses are the same.

units.la: Secunda ratio: quia nihil extat in institutione Coenae D. quo videri vnquam posset Christus se tunc Deo pro nobis obtulisse.
units.tr: The second reason: because there is nothing in the institution of the Lord's Supper by which it could ever be seen that Christ then offered himself to God for us.

units.la: Tertia ratio: quia refellitur hic error expressis Scripturae locis in quibus Christus dicitur semel passus: & eius oblatio, dicitur vnica oblatio.
units.tr: The third reason: because this error is refuted by express passages of Scripture in which Christ is said to have suffered once, and his offering is called a single offering.

units.la: Quarta: quia pugnat cum eo loquendi genere quod a Scriptura vsurpatur, quę nunquam dicit Christum se offerre nisi ratione verae & realis ipsius mortis (vt ante a nobis dictum est.)
units.tr: The fourth: because it conflicts with the manner of speaking that Scripture uses, which never says that Christ offered himself except by reason of his true and real death (as was said by us before).
