units.la: Quinta: quia si Christus sese pro nobis obtulit in Coena; haec oblatio aut fuit perfecta, aut imperfecta. Si dicas imperfectam: blasphemia est. Si perfectam: cur igitur postea Christus pro nobis mortuus est?
units.tr: The fifth: because if Christ offered himself for us in the Supper, that offering was either complete or incomplete. If you say incomplete, it is blasphemy. If complete, then why afterwards was Christ put to death for us?

units.la: Sexta: quia dicunt Missae sacrificiu offerri in memoriam Passionis, resurrectionis & ascensionis Christi: sic enim extat in eorum Missa: Vnde & memores nos eiusdem Christi filij tui Domini Dei nostri tam beatae passionis, nec non & ab inferis resurrectionis, sed & in caelos gloriosae ascensionis offerimus, &c. At quum Christus Coenam instituit, non potuit se tum offerre in memoriam suae mortis, resurrectionis & ascensionis. Memoria enim est rerum praeteritarum, non futurarum. Sed quid ego plura commemoro? haec enim sacrificulorum, no iam insci-tia, sed insania, etiam nobis tacentibus, satis se ipsa redarguit.
units.tr: The sixth: because they say the sacrifice of the Mass is offered in memory of the passion, resurrection and ascension of Christ; for this stands in their Mass: Wherefore, mindful of the blessed passion of the same Christ your Son our Lord God, and also of his resurrection from the dead, and of his glorious ascension into heaven, we offer, etc. But when Christ instituted the Supper, he could not then offer himself in memory of his death, resurrection and ascension. For memory is of things past, not of things to come. But why do I recount more? For this, not merely the ignorance but the madness of the sacrificing priests, already refutes itself sufficiently even without our speaking.

units.la: XVIII.
units.tr: XVIII.

units.la: SI Coena D. instituta est ut in ea fiat commemoratio sacrificij Christi: Certè, in Coena D. non fit ipsum Christi sacrificium: Quanto igitur minus in Missa?
units.tr: If the Lord's Supper was instituted so that a commemoration of Christ's sacrifice would be made in it, then certainly the sacrifice of Christ itself is not made in the Lord's Supper. How much less, then, in the Mass?

units.la: Antecedens verum est.
units.tr: The antecedent is true.

units.la: Verum igitur & consequens: Et vi consequentis, sacrificium Missæ reijciendum est.
units.tr: Therefore the consequent is also true, and by the force of the consequence, the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexum Hypotheticum patet: quia, rei commemoratio nō est res ipsa: quandoquidem commemoratio ἐξ ἀναγκης rem antegressam significat.
units.tr: The hypothetical connection is plain, because the commemoration of a thing is not the thing itself, since a commemoration necessarily signifies something that has gone before.

units.la: Assumpti veritas lucet expresis Christi verbis, Hoc facite in mei recordationem: & apud Paulum. Quotiescunque ederitis panem hunc & poculum hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annuntiatis vsque quo venerit.
units.tr: The truth of the assumption is clear from Christ's express words, "Do this in remembrance of me," and from Paul: "As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes."

units.la: Respondent Christum voluisse sacrificium suum repræsentari: non verbis tantum, sed etiam simili quadam actione. Sic enim, inquiut, Dominus liberationem primogenitorum commemorari voluit oblatione primogenitorum. Adde festos dies azymorum & Tabernaculorum in quibus res anteactæ rebus similibus in memoriam revocabantur. Atenim non negamus quin in sacra Coena mors Christi nobis quodammodo ante oculos ponatur, tum Euangelica prædicatione, idque imprimis (sic enim Paulus) Mortem Domini annuntiabitis, inquit, tum etiam Sacramento (hùc {huc enim spectat fractio panis teste eodem Apostolo, his verbis: Hoc meum est corpus quod pro vobis frangitur, inquit, summos Iesu Christi cruciatus ita significas) sed quid hoc ad mutas Missae caeremonias, aut ad ipsum Missae sacrificium quod proponunt? Ecquod enim est istud concludendi genus? Olim sub legis paedagogia Dominus certos ritus instituit, quibus maiores nostri beneficiorum a Deo acceptorum memoriam renouarent: ergo sacrificiu Christi ipsius Christi sacrificio repraesentandum est. Primum: non valet consequentia, a legis ceremoniis, ad tempora noui Testamenti: quin potius videmus eo Christi instituta respexisse, ut, quoad eius fieri posset, nos ab externis eiusmodi ritibus revocarent. Deinde: Prisicis illis temporibus ita faciendum esse nominatim & certa lege cantu erat: at de sacrificio externo in Coena Domini faciendo, nullum usquam verbum. Deniq; ista ratio no respondet eorum conclusioni: In veteribus enim caeremoniis fuisse rerum praeteritarum memoria perspicuu est. Sed isti volunt, Christi sacrificium, ipsius Christi sacrificio repraesentari; quod quidem no iam est similitudo, sed identitas. Perinde est enim ac si dicat: panes azymos quibus olim Israelitae quotannis certis ac solennibus diebus vescebatur, fuisse illos ipsos panes azymos qui olim in Ægypto cofecti fuerat. Idē dico de Taber. quàm sit ridiculū, nemo no videt, Quamobrem ex hac ipsorum ratione sequeretur: Coenam D. non esse Christi sacrificium, sed tantùm ipsius sacrificij similitudinem. Atque ita videmus quàm procul iam absint à sua sententia, ab ipsa disputationis aura prouecti. Atq; vt videant, quàm parum ipsi cum sua etiâ Missa consentiant (nedum cum verbo Dei velint consentire) expendât cum otio hæc Missæ verba; Suscipe sancta trinitas hanc oblationem quam tibi offerimus ob memoriam incarnationis, natiuitatis, circuncisionis, passionis, resurrectionis, & ascensionis Domini nostri Iesu Christi, &c. videant, inquam, num hæc possint cum illa commentitia sacrificij identitate conuenire.
units.tr: They reply that Christ wished his sacrifice to be represented not by words alone but also by some similar action. For, they say, the Lord wished the deliverance of the firstborn to be commemorated by the offering of the firstborn. Add the festivals of unleavened bread and of Tabernacles, in which past things were recalled to memory by similar things. But we do not deny that in the holy Supper the death of Christ is set, in some manner, before our eyes: first by the evangelical preaching, and this above all (for so Paul says, "You will proclaim the Lord's death"), and also by the sacrament (for to this the breaking of bread refers, as the same Apostle testifies in these words: This is my body which is broken for you, thus signifying the supreme sufferings of Jesus Christ). But what has this to do with the silent ceremonies of the Mass, or with the very sacrifice of the Mass which they propose? For what kind of inference is this? In former times, under the tutelage of the law, the Lord instituted certain rites by which our forebears renewed the memory of the benefits received from God; therefore the sacrifice of Christ is to be represented by the sacrifice of Christ himself. First, the consequence does not hold, from the ceremonies of the law to the times of the new Testament. Indeed we see that Christ's institutions aimed at this, that, as far as possible, they should draw us away from external rites of that kind. Second, in those ancient times it was indeed commanded by name and by a fixed law to do such things; but about performing an external sacrifice in the Lord's Supper there is no word anywhere. Finally, this reasoning does not match their conclusion. In the old ceremonies the memory of past things was plainly the purpose; but they want the sacrifice of Christ to be represented by the sacrifice of Christ himself, which is no longer a likeness but an identity. For it is just as if they said that the unleavened loaves on which the Israelites fed yearly on set solemn days were those very loaves which had once been baked in Egypt. I say the same of the Tabernacles: how ridiculous this is, no one fails to see. Therefore, from their own reasoning it would follow that the Lord's Supper is not Christ's sacrifice but only a likeness of the sacrifice. And so we see how far they now are from their own position, carried off by the very breeze of the debate. So that they may see how little they agree even with their own Mass (let alone how they wish to agree with the word of God), let them weigh at leisure these words of the Mass: Receive, holy Trinity, this oblation which we offer to you in memory of the incarnation, nativity, circumcision, passion, resurrection, and ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ, etc. Let them see, I say, whether these words can agree with that fictitious identity of sacrifice.

units.la: XIX.
units.tr: XIX.

units.la: Si Pontifici volunt Coenam Domini esse sacrificium εὐχαριστικόν; & sacrificium εὐχαριστικὸν non potest idem esse propitiatorium pro peccatis: certè, vel ex ipsorum Pontificiorum sententia, Coena non potest esse sacrificium pro peccatis: quanto minus Missa?
units.tr: If the Papists want the Lord's Supper to be a eucharistic sacrifice, and a eucharistic sacrifice cannot at the same time be propitiatory for sins, then certainly, even on the Papists' own opinion, the Supper cannot be a sacrifice for sins. How much less the Mass?

units.la: Antecedens verum est.
units.tr: The antecedent is true.

units.la: Verum igitur Consequens: Et vi consequentis sacrificium Missæ reijciendum est.
units.tr: Therefore the consequent is true, and by virtue of the consequence the sacrifice of the Mass must be rejected.

units.la: Connexum Hypotheticum non eget probatione.
units.tr: The hypothetical connection needs no proof.

units.la: Assumpti pars prior in promptu est, vel ex ipso vocabulo Eucharistiæ, quod in hac quæstione illi fere semper in ore habét: adde hæc expressa verba Missæ, Hostias tibi Domine laudis offerimus, &c.
units.tr: The first part of the minor premise is plain from the very word Eucharist, which they almost always have on their lips in this question. Add these express words of the Mass: We offer to you, Lord, the sacrifices of praise, etc.

units.la: Pars posterior confirmatur ex iis quæ copiosè à Mose traduntur de sacrificiis, tum Expiatoriis, tum Pacificis, sive, Eucharisticis, forma & ritib⁹ inter se distinctis. Huc adde vim naturámq; vtriusque sacrificij. Nam antecesisse beneficium oportet, pro quo gratiæ sint agendæ. Cùm autè imprimis gratias agamus Deo in sacra Cœna, quòd nobis Iesum Christum dederit, vt pro nobis oblatus, propitiatio pro peccatis nostris esset: necesse est, illud ipsum, pro quo gratias agimus, beneficium antecesserit: ac proinde in Cœna Domini non fiat sacrificium Christi pro peccatis propitiatorium.
units.tr: The second part is confirmed from what Moses hands down at length about sacrifices, both expiatory and peace (or eucharistic) offerings, which differ from one another in form and rites. Add to this the force and nature of each kind. For a benefit must have gone before, for which thanks are to be given. But since we above all give thanks to God in the holy Supper for giving us Jesus Christ, so that he might be offered for us as a propitiation for our sins, it is necessary that the very benefit for which we give thanks came first. Therefore no propitiatory sacrifice of Christ for sins is made in the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Respondent; vtrumque sacrificij genus posse concurrere: eò quòd fideles offerant quoq; Deo sacrificiu spirituale in Cœna Domini. Quòd si ita est, efficitur, sacrificiu illud, quatenus Eucharisticum, esse spirituale, non autem reale & externum. Qui fit igitur vt ipsam hostiam, quam volunt esse veram ac realem, & quam se dicunt offerre pro peccatis, vocent Eucharistiam? Certè, vel ex primis τρόπῳ παιδείας rudimentis didicerunt, hanc esse vim παρωνυμίας, vt si Eucharistia sit realis & externa; sacrificium Eucharisticum sit quoque externum & reale. Neque hoc vlla ratione stare potest: hostiâ esse reale & externam, ipsum autè sacrificiu esse internum &
units.tr: They reply that both kinds of sacrifice can coincide, because the faithful also offer to God a spiritual sacrifice in the Lord's Supper. If that is so, it follows that this sacrifice, insofar as it is eucharistic, is spiritual and not real and external. Why, then, do they call the very victim, which they want to be true and real, and which they say they offer for sins, the Eucharist? Surely from the first rudiments of their training they have learned the force of the paronymy [παρωνυμία]: if the Eucharist is real and external, then the eucharistic sacrifice is also external and real. This cannot stand in any way: that the victim is real and external, but the sacrifice itself is internal and spiritual.

units.la: F spirituale.Quinetiam, cùm res denominari soleat ex eo quod est potius: & illi sui sacrificij hostiam, Eucharistiam nominent: velintq; sacrificiu, quatenus Eucharisticum, esse spirituale : relinquitur,vt si quod est sacrificiu in Cœna Domini,illud sit spirituale ac propterea nō reale & externū. Quia verò quod negatur de Cœna D. id quoque de sua Missa negandum esse confitentur;Ecce, nobis redit nostra conclusio ἀναστευαςτικὴ quā in hoc cap.efficere statueram⁹:In Missa non fieri verum, reale & externū sacrificiū propitiatorū pro peccatis.Verum enimuero cùm Pontificij vt superiorū argumētorū vim effugiant, sese in vnius distinctionis latebram coniicere soleant:nempe,sacrificij cruenti & incruenti: quanquam ex iis quæ antè à nobis disputata sunt facilè ista distinctio tollitur: vt tamen res fiat dilucidior, pauca subiiciemus ad euertendam illam distinctionem.
units.tr: Moreover, since a thing is usually named from what is more important, and they name the victim of their sacrifice the Eucharist, and want the sacrifice, insofar as it is eucharistic, to be spiritual, it follows that whatever sacrifice there is in the Lord's Supper is spiritual, and therefore not real and external. But since they confess that what is denied of the Lord's Supper must also be denied of their own Mass, behold, our refutative [ἀναστευαστικὴ] conclusion returns to us, the one I had resolved to establish in this chapter: that in the Mass no true, real and external sacrifice, propitiatory for sins, is made. But since the Papists, to escape the force of the above arguments, are accustomed to hide in the shelter of a single distinction, namely that between bloody and unbloody sacrifice, and although that distinction is easily removed by what we have argued before, nevertheless, to make the matter clearer, we shall add a few points for overturning it.

units.la: XX.
units.tr: XX.

units.la: OMnis distinctio quæ non solum destituitur verbo Dei,sed ei aduersatur, sibíque ipsa contradicit: ridicula est,nedum Theologica: ac propterea à theologicis disputationibus reijcieda.
units.tr: Every distinction that is not only lacking in the Word of God but opposes it and contradicts itself is ridiculous, not to say theological, and therefore must be rejected from theological disputations.

units.la: Distinctio sacrificij cruenti & incruenti à Pontificiis in hac quæstione proposita, non solum destituitur verbo Dei,sed ei aduersatur sibíque ipsa contradicit. Quare distinctio sacrificij cruenti & incrueti à Potificiis in hac quæstione proposita, posita, ridicula est, nedum Theologica: ac propterea à Theologicis disputationibus reiicienda.
units.tr: The distinction between bloody and unbloody sacrifice, as the Papists propose it in this question, is not only lacking in the Word of God but opposes it and contradicts itself. Therefore the distinction between bloody and unbloody sacrifice, as the Papists propose it in this question, is ridiculous, not to say theological, and must be rejected from theological disputations.

units.la: Maior est extra controuersiam.
units.tr: The major premise is beyond controversy.

units.la: Minor tria continet quæ nos sigillatim probabimus.
units.tr: The minor premise contains three points, which we shall prove one by one.

units.la: Primum est; istam distinctionem Pontificiam destitui verbo Dei. Cùm enim agant de sacrificio noui Testamenti, affirmamus, noui Testameti temporibus vnicũ, reale, ex ternúmque sacrificiũ extitisse, quo legalium omniũ sacrificiorum vmbræ impletæ simul & abrogatæ sunt: nempe sanctissimũ illud sacrificiũ quod Christus semel in cruce pro nobis obtulit: ac proinde nulla Christianis sacrificia offerenda superesse, præter sacrificia spiritualia, de quibus egimus in primo cap. huius disputationis. Hæc quidem sacrificia quæ nobis ab Apostolis commendantur sunt incruenta, quia spiritualia: & siquidem eo sensu loquerentur Pontificij, longè abessent à suis erroribus. Verùm hoc sibi volunt: In nouo Testamento esse aliquod sacrificium reale & externũ idemque incruentũ: cuius rei nullum verbũ reperiri, nullum extare vestigium in scriptis Apostolicis affirmamus: quemadmodũ fusius à nobis confirmatũ est supra in argumento 2. Quòd si nobis fidem Pontificij non habeant, ferant igitur ἐνστασιν & proferant aliquem Scripturæ locum, ex quo doceant, eiusdẽ victimæ sacrificiũ externũ, esse posse tũ cruentũ, tũ incruentum. Secundum membrum minoris propositionis est: hanc Pontificiorum distinctionem aduersari verbo Dei: quod nos ita planum facimus. Si Christus non tantum sese obtulit cruento sacrificio, quū pro nobis semel mortuus est, sed etiā quotidie pro nobis offertur sacrificio incruento: ergo plura sunt & varia eiusdem Christi sacrificia: quod aduersatur his Scripturæ locis.
units.tr: The first is that this Papist distinction is lacking in the Word of God. For since they are dealing with the sacrifice of the New Testament, we affirm that in New Testament times there has existed one sacrifice, real and external, by which the shadows of all the legal sacrifices were at once fulfilled and abrogated: namely that most holy sacrifice which Christ once offered for us on the cross. Therefore no sacrifices remain for Christians to offer, except spiritual sacrifices, of which we treated in the first chapter of this disputation. Indeed, these sacrifices which the Apostles commend to us are unbloody, because they are spiritual; and if the Papists spoke in that sense, they would be far from their errors. But they mean this: that in the New Testament there is some real and external sacrifice that is at the same time unbloody. We affirm that no word for such a thing can be found, and no trace of it exists in the Apostolic writings, as we have confirmed more fully above in argument 2. But if the Papists do not trust us, let them bring forward an objection (ἔνστασιν) and produce some passage of Scripture from which they teach that the external sacrifice of the same victim can be both bloody and unbloody. The second part of the minor premise is that this Papist distinction is opposed to the Word of God, which we make plain as follows. If Christ not only offered himself in a bloody sacrifice when he died once for us, but is also offered for us every day in an unbloody sacrifice, then there are many and various sacrifices of the same Christ; and this is contrary to the following passages of Scripture.

units.la: Christus vna pro peccatis oblata victima in perpetuum sedet ad dextram Dei, &c. unica enim oblatione consecrauit in perpetuum eos qui sanctificantur.
units.tr: Christ, having been offered once as a victim for sins, sits for ever at the right hand of God, etc. For by one offering he has perfected for ever those who are sanctified.

units.la: Non vt saepe offerat semetipsum: sicut Pontifex quotannis ingreditur in sacrarium cum sanguine alieno: alioquin oportuisset eum saepe passum fuisse a condito mundo.
units.tr: Not that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters the sanctuary every year with blood not his own; otherwise he would have had to suffer often since the foundation of the world.

units.la: Sanctificati sumus per oblationem corporis Iesu Christi semel.
units.tr: We have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once.

units.la: Lex vmbram obtinens futurorum bonorum non expressam formam rerum, ijs hostiis quas singulis annis easdem assiduè offerunt nunquam poterit accedentes sanctificare: alioqui nonne desiissent offerri?
units.tr: The law, having a shadow of good things to come and not the very image of the things, can never make the comers thereto perfect by those sacrifices which they offer continually, year by year. Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered?

units.la: Sine sanguine non fit remissio.
units.tr: Without shedding of blood there is no remission.

units.la: Vbi est peccatorum remissio, non est amplius oblatio pro peccato, &c. & permulta in hanc sententiam quae proposuimus supra in Argum.4. Ex quibus intelligitur, oblationem Christi & vnicam, & semel factam, nō saepe faciendam esse. Quod si vera esset ista Pontifitificiorum distinctio: quis non videt iacere Apostoli Argumentum? Non vt sæpe se offerat, inquit, alioquin oportuisset eum sæpe passum fuisse. Imò (siquidem verum dicunt Pontifici) potest sæpe offerri Christus, nec tamè propterea pati: quia potest offerri sacrificio incruento. Atenim peregrinum istud & ἐτερόδοξον commentum precidit Apostolus, quū ait hæc duo esse consectaria ἐξ ἀνάγκης: Christum sæpe offerri; &, Christum sæpe pati. Rursus: Si lex potuisset sanctificare (inquit Apostolus) certè hostiæ desiissent offerri. Ex quibus concludo: posteaquam Christus qui potest sanctificare, exhibitus fuit & oblatus: eum non amplius esse offerendum: alioqui, Christus esset inferior legalibus victimis: quod absit. Atqui si incruente potest offerri Christus: quomodo stabit quod toties inculcat Apostolus, Christum semel oblatum esse, eúmque non esse sæpius offerendum? Præterea Apostolus affirmat, sine sanguine non fieri remissionem peccatorum. Contrà, Pontificij dicunt fieri remissionem peccatorum incruento sacrificio, hoc est, sine sanguine. Item: Apostolus negat vllam esse amplius oblationem pro peccato, posteaquam peccata per Christum remissa sunt. Contra, Pontificij affirmant, superesse quandam oblationem pro peccato, nempe incruentam. En, quàm bene Pontificiis cum Apostolo conueniat. Illis igitur oppono hoc Theorema Thelogicum,quod videant an labefactare posint. Quotiescunque extat in Scriptura Propositio vniuersalis: nulla est ei opponenda distinctio, nisi nitatur certis, dilucidis, expressisque ipsius Scripturæ verbis: ex quibus, sine controuersia, ἐvστασις ferri posit. Ratio est: quia nullum alioqui dogma in Theologia certum esset: semper enim exciperetur id quod esset in quæstione positum: quemadmodum Pontificij,non in hac tantum quæstione,sed in plerisque aliis faciunt.
units.tr: Where there is remission of sins, there is no longer an offering for sin, etc.; and very many things to this effect we set out above in Argument 4. From these it is understood that the offering of Christ is both unique and made once, and is not to be made often. But if that Papist distinction were true, who does not see how the Apostle's argument would collapse? "Not that he should offer himself often," he says, "otherwise he would have had to suffer often." Indeed, if the Papists speak the truth, Christ can be offered often and yet not suffer, because he can be offered in an unbloody sacrifice. But the Apostle cut off that foreign and heterodox fiction [ἐτερόδοξον] when he said that these two things follow of necessity [ἐξ ἀνάγκης]: that Christ is offered often, and that Christ suffers often. Again: "If the law could have sanctified," says the Apostle, "surely the sacrifices would have ceased to be offered." From these I conclude that since Christ, who can sanctify, has been presented and offered, he is no longer to be offered; otherwise Christ would be inferior to the legal victims, which God forbid. But if Christ can be offered unbloodily, how will it stand that the Apostle so often insists that Christ was offered once, and is not to be offered more often? Moreover, the Apostle affirms that without shedding of blood there is no remission of sins. On the contrary, the Papists say that remission of sins is effected by an unbloody sacrifice, that is, without blood. Likewise, the Apostle denies that there is any longer an offering for sin once sins have been remitted through Christ. On the contrary, the Papists affirm that some offering for sin still remains, namely an unbloody one. See how well the Papists agree with the Apostle! Therefore I set against them this theological theorem, and let them see whether they can overthrow it. Whenever there is a universal proposition in Scripture, no distinction is to be opposed to it unless it rests on certain, clear and express words of Scripture itself, by which it can be refuted beyond controversy. The reason is that otherwise no dogma in theology would be certain, for there would always be an exception made for whatever was in question, as the Papists do not only in this question but in most others.

units.la: Verùm,inquiunt,superiores illi loci sunt de cruento sacrificio intelligendi. Rectè sanè: nullum enim aliud Christi sacrificium Apostolus agnouit. Cùm igitur affirmans oblationem Christi vnicam esse, cruentum sacrificium intelligat: sequitur, cruentum Christi sacrificium esse vnicum ipsius sacrificium : ac proinde exibilandam esse distinctionem hanc de incruento Christi sacrificio. Isti autem perinde distinguunt cruentum ab incruento, ac si plane constaret aliquod esse Christi sacrificium incruentum,quod nos merum delirium esse & Apostolis incognitum, ex ipsorum Apostolorum scriptis confirmauimus. Omnes autem Theologicæ distinctiones debent esse eiusmodi,vt singulæ ipsarum partes manifestè luceant in Scriptura, quemadmodum diximus. Quòd si commentitias distinctiones proproponere liceat, quibus nihil aliud quàm principium petatur (id quod in hac quæ-stione Pötificiis vsuuenit) næ facillimum erit cuique Theologicè disputare.
units.tr: Their reply is that those earlier passages must be understood of a bloody sacrifice. Quite right: the Apostle recognised no other sacrifice of Christ. So when he affirms that Christ's offering is unique, he means the bloody sacrifice, and it follows that Christ's bloody sacrifice is his one sacrifice, and that this distinction concerning an unbloody sacrifice of Christ must be hissed off the stage. They distinguish the bloody from the unbloody as if it were plain that there is some unbloody sacrifice of Christ. We have shown from the writings of the Apostles themselves that this is sheer nonsense and unknown to the Apostles. All theological distinctions ought to be of such a kind that each of their parts shines clearly in Scripture, as we have said. But if it were permitted to put forward invented distinctions, which beg the question (as the Papists do in this controversy), then it would be very easy for anyone to dispute theologically.

units.la: Tertium membrum Minoris nostræ pro positionis fuit: Pontificiorum distinctio-nem sibi ipsi contradicere:quod ita fiet ma-nifestum, Sacrificium in quo victima sacri-ficatur Deo,non potest esse sine sanguinis fusione. Nam victima dicitur sacrificari, quum immolatur Deo.Quare qui dicit sa-crificium cuius victima Christus est, esse incruentum : ille dicit sacrificium non sa-crificium. Nam si incruentum est: non est igitur Christi sacrificium : quandoquidem fusio sanguinis est de ratione huius sacri-ficij,vt dictum est : nisi forte velint aliquid posse simul esse incruentum cum sanguinis fusione.
units.tr: The third part of our minor premise was that the distinction of the Papists contradicts itself. This will become clear as follows. A sacrifice in which a victim is slain to God cannot be without the shedding of blood. For a victim is said to be sacrificed when it is immolated to God. Therefore whoever says that a sacrifice whose victim is Christ is unbloody, says that a sacrifice is not a sacrifice. For if it is unbloody, it is not Christ's sacrifice, since the shedding of blood belongs to the essence of this sacrifice, as has been said, unless perhaps they want something to be able to be unbloody and at the same time involve the shedding of blood.

units.la: Respondent : fusionem sanguinis esse Sacramentalem. Ex quo efficio,quandoquidem incruenti vocabulum tollit verâ san-guinis fusionem : id dici Pontificiis Sacra-mentale, quod re vera non est , sed est rei veræ signum & figura. Vtrumque enim simul coniungunt , nempe incruentum & Sacramentale. Huc igitur post longos ac varios errores tandem redeunt: In Cœ-na non fieri ipsum Christi sacrificium ve-re, sed Sacramentaliter ,hoc est, sacram Domini Cœnam esse Sacramentum veri illius & vnici sacrificij, quod semel Christus fecit pro nobis, quum sese obtulit victimam Deo pro peccatis nostris. Nam si fusio sanguinis vera est: non est ergo incruentum sacrificium. Si Sacramentalis est fusio: ergo sacrificium non vere fit, sed Sacramentaliter: idque vi παραδωμένης. Quia vero non audent hac in parte plus tribuere suae Missae quam Coenae Domini: reliquum est, vt illi nobiscum affirment, falsum esse, in Missa fieri verum, reale & externum Christi sacrificium propitiatorium pro peccatis nostris: quod erat nobis refellendum.
units.tr: They reply that the shedding of blood is sacramental. From this I conclude that, since the word unbloody removes the true shedding of blood, the Papists are calling sacramental what in fact is not real but is only a sign and figure of the real thing. For they join the two together, namely unbloody and sacramental. So at last, after long and varied errors, they come back to this: in the Supper Christ's sacrifice is not truly made, but sacramentally; that is, the holy Supper of the Lord is a sacrament of that true and unique sacrifice which Christ made once for us, when he offered himself as a victim to God for our sins. For if the shedding of blood is real, then the sacrifice is not unbloody. If the shedding of blood is sacramental, then the sacrifice is not truly made but sacramentally, and that by the force of the handed-down tradition [παραδωμένης]. But since in this matter they do not dare to grant their Mass more than the Lord's Supper, what remains is that they agree with us that it is false that in the Mass there is made a true, real and external sacrifice of Christ propitiating for our sins. This was what we had to refute.

units.la: CAPVT IIII.
units.tr: Chapter IV

units.la: NON sine causa monent Philosophi cognoscendū esse falsum, vt maiorem veri cognitionem habeamus. Tunc enim manifeste patet necessariae demonstrationis veritas, quum ἀποδεικτικοί Syllogismi redarguuntur. Quare ex illa methodo quam nobis sequendam propositimus, posteaquam aduersariorum sententiam superiori disputatione ἀναιρετικῇ refutaimus: iam nobis subducenda sunt ea fundamenta, quae illi suis erroribus substernunt, & nostrae ad eorum argumenta responsiones, proferendae.
units.tr: The philosophers rightly warn that falsehood must be known if we are to have a greater knowledge of truth. For the truth of a necessary demonstration is then plainly evident, when demonstrative [ἀποδεικτικοί] syllogisms are refuted. Therefore, following the method which we proposed to follow, now that we have refuted the opponents' opinion by a refutative [ἀναιρετικῇ] disputation above, we must now lay bare the foundations on which they rest their errors, and bring forward our answers to their arguments.

units.la: Obiect.I.
units.tr: Objection I

units.la: Hoc facite in meam commemorationē, inquit, Christus: Ergo in Missa fieri debet sacrificium ex ipsa institutione Christi.
units.tr: "Do this in remembrance of me," says Christ. Therefore a sacrifice ought to be made in the Mass from the very institution of Christ.

units.la: Consequentia patet: quia FACERE significat sacrificare: si aliunde indicia suppetunt: vt, Hoc est quod facies in altari: Agnos anniculos duos per singulos dies iugiter. Item: Agnum unum faciesmanè, &c. Item. Scitis quia post biduum Pascha fiet, hoc est, immolabitur: interprete Marco: Vnde Poëta, Quum faciam vitulam pro frugibus ipse venito. Itaque hoc facite, id est, efficite vt vestro facto magis quàm voce mortem meam annuntietis. Quo fit vt actiones Christi, tum circa panem, tum circa calicem considerandæ sint. Cùm igitur Christus fieri iusserit id quod tu fecit: Christus autem seipsum in Coena sacrificauerit incruentè sub speciebus panis & vini: sequitur, in Missa sacrificium esse faciendum.
units.tr: The consequence is plain, because TO DO means to sacrifice, if other indications are at hand, as: "This is what you shall do on the altar: two yearling lambs daily continually." Likewise: "You shall make one lamb in the morning," etc. Likewise: "You know that after two days the Passover will be made," that is, will be slain, as Mark interprets it. Hence the poet: "When I shall make a heifer for the fruits, come yourself." So "Do this" means, make it so that by your deed rather than by your voice you proclaim my death. Hence the actions of Christ, both about the bread and about the cup, must be considered. Since therefore Christ has commanded that to be done which you did, and Christ sacrificed himself in the Supper unbloodily under the appearances of bread and wine, it follows that a sacrifice is to be made in the Mass.

units.la: Responsio.
units.tr: Answer

units.la: Pernego Consequens: Probatio verò plane inepta est. Primus error est παρὰ τὸ χῆμα τῆς λέξεως. Nec enim ea est significatio verbi ποιεῖν quo Paulus & Lucas vtuntur, vt perinde accipiendum sit, ac si dixisset: sacrificate. Verbum quidem hebræum Asa sæpe solet ad sacrificia referri: quia non tantum significat, facere: sed etiam, aptare & ritè aliquid componere: & propter hanc posteriorem significationem, sæpe infert ipsos ritus ex lege Dei in sacris adhiberi solitos: ita tamen, vt huius verbi, generalis sit significatio: neque sit ad vocabulum sacrificandi restringenda. Hoc autem perspicuum est ex illo ipso loco quem citant: Facies, inquit, vnum agnum mane & alterum vesperi: decimam partem similaginis mixtam oleo, &c. vbi repetendum est verbum Facies ἀπὸ τῆς κοινῆς. Atqui, agnus quidem sacrificabatur & mactabatur: sed id similagini minimè convenire, manifestum est. Illicigitur, Ἀσά significat, mactare: hic vero; simpliciter offerre. Quia vero Paulus & Lucas Hebraicè non scripserunt, sed Graecè: idcirco vis Graeci vocabuli spectanda fuit: nisi forte doceant, hic esse hebraismum: quod num satis firmis rationibus facturisint, expectabimus. Dum enim proferunt ex Matthaeo: Post biduum Pascha fiet: alias res agut: quippe cum ibi verbum ποιεῖν non vsurpetur (de cuius significatione disputamus) sed τὸ γίνεσθαι: quod in eo loco non fieri, sed esse significat: Hoc enim sibi vult Christus mox futurū Pascha, quemadmodū patet ex loco Marci quem etiam nobis opponūt. Erat, inquit, Pascha post biduum. Nec quod sequitur, apud Marcum (Quando Pascha mactabant) efficit vt verbum γίνεται à Matthaeo vsurpatum, significet sacrificare. Sic apud Ezechielem: Erit vobis Pascha: Est igitur disputiciendum, an, Pascha, significet agnum illum qui immolabatur: an verò, diem festum quo sancta haec caeremonia celebrabatur. In quo posteriore riore sensus vsurpatur à Matthęo in illo cap. ver.2. vt & multis aliis in locis. Prope erat Pascha Iudæorum, inquit Ioannes: Item. Quū esset Hierosolymis in Pascha die festo. Et Lucas, Festum azymorum quod dicitur Pascha. Et in hoc significato, facere Pascha, est festum illum diem agere, & caeremoniam illam celebrare ex praecepto legis, ex vsu loquedi Scripturae, vt No facţu est tale Pascha a diebus Iudicu, etc. Hic ergo peccat παρὰ τὸν ὁμωνυμίαν.
units.tr: I deny the consequence outright, and the proof is plainly absurd. The first error is from the figure of the expression [παρὰ τὸ σχῆμα τῆς λέξεως]. For this is not the meaning of the Greek verb poiein which Paul and Luke use, so that it is to be taken as if they had said "sacrifice." It is true that the Hebrew verb Asa [עשה] is often referred to sacrifices, because it does not only mean to make, but also to prepare and to put something together duly; and on account of this latter meaning it often introduces the very rites from the law of God that were customarily employed in sacred things. But the general meaning of this verb is still this, and it is not to be restricted to the word "to sacrifice." This is clear from the very passage they cite: "You shall make," he says, "one lamb in the morning and another in the evening, a tenth part of fine flour mixed with oil," etc., where the verb "you shall make" must be repeated from the common [ἀπὸ τῆς κοινῆς]. But the lamb was indeed sacrificed and slain, while it is plain that this does not suit the fine flour. Therefore there Asa means to slay, but here simply to offer. But since Paul and Luke did not write in Hebrew but in Greek, the force of the Greek word had to be considered, unless perhaps they teach that this is a Hebraism; we shall wait to see whether they will do this with sufficiently firm reasons. For when they bring forward from Matthew, "After two days the Passover will be made," they are doing something different, since the verb poiein is not used there (whose meaning we are disputing) but ginesthai, which in that place means not to be made but to be: for Christ means that the Passover is about to come in a little while, as is clear from the passage of Mark which they also set against us: "The Passover," he says, "was after two days." Nor does what follows in Mark, "when they slaughtered the Passover," make the verb ginetai used by Matthew mean to sacrifice. So in Ezekiel: "There shall be a Passover for you." It must therefore be discussed whether "Passover" means the lamb that was slain, or rather the festal day on which this holy ceremony was celebrated. In this latter sense it is used by Matthew in that chapter, verse 2, as in many other places also. "The Passover of the Jews was near," says John. Likewise: "When he was at Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover." And Luke: "The feast of unleavened bread, which is called the Passover." And in this sense, "to make the Passover" is to keep that festal day and to celebrate that ceremony by the command of the law, according to the usage of Scripture's speech, as in "No such Passover has been kept since the days of the judges," etc. Here then they err from the ambiguity of the word [παρὰ τὴν ὁμωνυμίαν].

units.la: Ad verbum Latinum quod attinet; non inde petenda est verbi Graeci significatio: quemadmodum de Hebraeo vocabulo diximus. Nam Graece scripserunt Apostoli: non Latine. Praeterea quum facere apud Latinos significat, sacrificare: tunc, conciso loquedi genere, facere dicitur simpliciter pro rem diuinam facere: ac proinde verbum illud iungitur cū sexto casu: dicunt enim facere hac vel illa victima: vt Poeta: Quum faciam vitula: nō autem, quum faciam vitulam: vt isti perperam recitant: atque id quàm alienum sit ab hoc propositio, miror eos non videre. Sed profecto errores isti, non iam Philosophorum praeceptis, sed Grammaticorum feruelis castigandi sunt.
units.tr: As far as the Latin word is concerned, the meaning of the Greek word is not to be taken from it, just as we said about the Hebrew word. For the Apostles wrote in Greek, not in Latin. Moreover, since among the Latins facere means to sacrifice, then, by a compressed manner of speaking, facere is used simply for to perform the divine rite; and so the verb is joined with the ablative case: they say facere hac vel illa victima, to make with this or that victim, as the poet: "When I shall make with a heifer," not "when I shall make a heifer," as these men wrongly quote it. How far this is from the present proposition I wonder that they do not see. But truly these errors are to be corrected not by the precepts of the philosophers, but by the rules of the grammarians.

units.la: Secundus error: παρὰ τὸ προς τι ἁπλῶς λεγόμενον. Dixit enim Christus, Hoc facite, nonaute simpliciter facite: & quemadmodū admonui in cap. superiori proximo, nusquā hoc complexum orationis significat ideē ac verbum, sacrificare. Item, Facere de Christo secundum legem apud Lucam (quemadmodū, nonnulli ex Pontificiis obiiciunt) significat quidem oblationem tum factam: nempe, nō vi verbi: sex ex loci circunstantia. Sic, qui circuncidebant, secundum legem faciebant, nec sacrificabant tamen.
units.tr: The second error is from what is said relatively but absolutely [παρὰ τὸ πρός τι ἁπλῶς λεγόμενον]. For Christ said, "Do this," not simply "make," and, as I pointed out in the immediately preceding chapter, this phrase nowhere means the same as the word "to sacrifice." Likewise, "to do concerning Christ according to the law" in Luke (as some of the Papists object) does indeed mean the offering then made, but not by the force of the word; it does so from the circumstance of the passage. Thus those who circumcised did so "according to the law," and yet they did not sacrifice.

units.la: Tertius error: ψευδοχρόφημα in Theologia: quum ita statuunt: verbum facere idem esse ac sacrificare, in hoc Christi praecepto, Hoc facite, si aliunde, inquiunt, indicia suppetant, quibus constet verbum illud in hoc significato vsurpari. Cùm potius ita dicendum fuerit: verbum Asa apud Hebraeos habere significationem offerendi & sacrificandi, quoties, non tantùm aliunde (vt isti volunt) sed ex illo ipso loco de quo agitur, nō indicia tantū (vt isti somniāt) sedfirmissima suppetunt argumenta. Quam nos regulam proposuimus & confirmauimus in posteriori nostra Responsione ad repetita F. Turriani Sophismata. Atque vt illis hunc laborem detraham, subiiciam certum argumentum, ex quo significatio illa verbi Asa colligi debeat. Nimirum: quādo res quae sacrificatur, vel, offerturDomino, componitur cum ipso verbo: vt, quum dicit Scriptura: facere, hoc est, sacrificare agnum, hoedum, similaginē, & reliqua huiusmodi: constructione Hebraica, non Latina.
units.tr: Third error: a false pretence [ψευδοχρόφημα] in theology, when they state that the verb facere means the same as sacrificare in this precept of Christ, Hoc facite, "if," they say, "other indications are available from elsewhere, by which it is clear that the verb is used in this sense." It should rather be said that the Hebrew verb Asa [עשה] has the meaning of offering and sacrificing whenever the thing that is sacrificed, or offered to the Lord, is joined with the verb itself. The argument is not based merely on indications from elsewhere (as they wish), which they dream up, but on the strongest arguments, which come from that very passage under discussion. We set out and confirmed this rule in our later Response to the repeated sophisms of F. Turrianus. And so that I may spare them this labour, I will add a certain argument from which that meaning of the verb Asa ought to be inferred: namely, when the thing that is sacrificed, or offered to the Lord, is construed with the verb itself, as when Scripture says facere, that is, to sacrifice a lamb, a kid, fine flour, and the like. This is a Hebrew construction, not a Latin one.

units.la: Quartus error: <bl>παρὰ τῶν ἀγνοιαν τῆς ἐλέγχε</bl>
units.tr: Fourth error: ignorance of the point at issue [παρὰ τῶν ἀγνοιαν τῆς ἐλέγχε].

units.la: Nam in vna eadémque ratione, diuersas fi-gnificationes vni verbo affingunt. Primùm enim cõtendunt facere in his Christi verbis, idem esse, ac sacrificare: deinde (quasi illos pœniteat) afferunt propriam illius verbi si-gnificationem: id est, inquiunt, efficite vt ve-stro sasto mortem meam annuntietis &c. ac nos reuocant ad ipsas Christi actiones. At enim debebant meminisse: Tum demum veram esse enunciationem, quum vnum dicitur: alioqui non erit enuntiare, sed ludere vocabulorum ἀμφιβολία: quemadmodum ex arte disserendi (quantum existimo) didicerunt.
units.tr: For within one and the same line of argument they attach different meanings to a single word. First they contend that facere in these words of Christ means the same as sacrificare; then, as if they regretted it, they bring forward the proper meaning of that verb, namely, "Make it so that by your doing you proclaim my death," and so they recall us to Christ's own actions. But they ought to have remembered that a statement is true only when one thing is meant; otherwise it is not a statement but a play on words, a amphibolia [ἀμφιβολία], as they have learned from the art of reasoning (as I think).

units.la: Quintus error: παρὰ τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ λαμβανόμενον. Et, vere vt dicam, non memini vsquam me legere stolidiorem principij petitionem. Vt enim probent, sacrificium esse in Cœna Domini faciendum: proferunt hæc verba. Hoc facite. Rursus, vt efficiant, ex his verbis sequi præceptum sacrificandi: aiunt Christum tunc temporis sacrificasse. Dum autem instamus, ne syllabam quidem extare in institutione Cœnæ D. quæ sacrificare significet: tum illi ad verbum facere, reuoluuntur, affirmántque idem esse, ac, sacrificare. Quod per inde est, ac si dicant: Christum sacrificasse: quia Christus sacrificauit. At nos affirma-mus, in sanctissimo hoc instituto nihil repe-riri quod vel leuissimam coniecturam ex-terni sacrificij afferre possit: Accipite, in-quit, comedite, bibite ex eo omnes, hoc facite qu. tiescunque biberitis ad mei recordationem, &c. Ecquid est, obsecro, in his verbis quod ad externi sacrificij significationem vel tantulum accedat? Mihi credite, Pontificij: hoc vestrum est, non disputantis argumentum, sed febricitantis insomnium.
units.tr: Fifth error: begging the question [παρὰ τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ λαμβανόμενον]. And, to speak truly, I do not remember ever reading a more foolish petitio principii anywhere. To prove that sacrifice is to be made in the Lord's Supper, they bring forward these words, Hoc facite. Again, to establish that a command to sacrifice follows from these words, they say that Christ sacrificed at that time. But when we press them that not even a syllable can be found in the institution of the Lord's Supper that signifies sacrificing, they fall back on the word facere, and affirm that it means the same as sacrificare. This is just as if they said: Christ sacrificed, because Christ sacrificed. But we affirm that in this most holy institution nothing can be found that could bring even the slightest conjecture of an external sacrifice. Accipite, he says, comedite, bibite ex eo omnes; hoc facite quotiescunque biberitis in mei recordationem, etc. Pray, what is there in these words that comes even slightly near the meaning of an external sacrifice? Believe me, Papists: this is not the argument of a disputant but the dream of a feverish man.

units.la: Sextus error in falso Consequenti. Verba enim Christi ad S. Coenae Sacramentum nō ad fictitium Missae sacrificium pertinent.
units.tr: Sixth error: a false consequent. For the words of Christ pertain to the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper, not to the fictitious sacrifice of the Mass.

units.la: Iam superius Pontificiorum argumentū incommodis vrgeamus.
units.tr: Now let us press the Papists' argument, already stated above, with its absurdities.

units.la: Si in Christi verbis FACITE significat, sacrificare: &, Hoc, ad actiones Christi referendum est, tum circa panem, tum etiam circa calicē (quemadmodū illi volunt) ergo id quod Christus fecit sacrificandū est, & ipsae actiones Christi sunt sacrificandae. Ἀδιωάτον, stultum, ridiculum.
units.tr: If in the words of Christ FACITE signifies sacrificare, and Hoc refers to the actions of Christ, both concerning the bread and also concerning the cup (as they wish), then what Christ did must be sacrificed, and Christ's own actions must be sacrificed. Absurd [ἀδύνατον], foolish, ridiculous.

units.la: Denique retorqueamus in Pontificios locum quem nobis obiiciunt.
units.tr: Finally, let us turn back upon the Papists the argument they throw at us.

units.la: Si Christus S. Coenae mysterium instituens iussit nos facere quod fecit: neque tum dicitur Christus vllum externum sacrificium fecisse: certè in S. Coenae mysterio nullum à nobis externum sacrificium faciendum est. Item.
units.tr: If Christ, instituting the mystery of the Lord's Supper, commanded us to do what he did, and at that time Christ is not said to have made any external sacrifice, then certainly in the mystery of the Lord's Supper no external sacrifice is to be made by us. Likewise.

units.la: Si facere, significat sacrificare (quod illi à nobis postulant.) Ergo nullu est sacrificiu in Missa. Consequentia patet. Sic enim Christus commemorante Paulo: Hoc facite, quotiescunque biberitis ad mei recordationem, Atqui in Missa nulla est communio, praesertim calicis à quo plebe arcet Eccles. Rom. sacrificuli: cū tamē fideles hoc facere iubeantur quotiescunque biberint, inquit, Paulus.
units.tr: If facere signifies sacrificare (which is what they demand of us), then there is no sacrifice in the Mass. The consequence is clear. For Christ, as Paul records, said: "Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of me." But in the Mass there is no communion, especially of the cup, from which the Roman sacrificers keep the people back; yet Paul says that the faithful are commanded to do this as often as they drink.

units.la: Nec vero audiendi sunt Pontificij qui hęc verba, Hoc facite, tradunt ad solos sacerdotes, vt vocant, pertinere. Nam aperte refelluntur ex hoc loco Pauli verba Christi ad vniuersam Corinthiorum Ecclesiam accomodantis. Nec tamen negamus in hoc mysterio habendā esse vocationis vniuscuiusque ratione: quandoquidem nō licet cuiuis sacra symbola ministrare. Sed dū Pastores docēt, hortantur & Sacramenta ipsa administrant: populus autem attentē audit, & cum debita reuerentia Sacramenta recipit: tota Ecclesia rectē dicitur præstare quod Christus iusserit his verbis, Hoc facite. Nisi forte velint S. Cœnam ad solos Pastores restringere, eō quod soli Apostoli cum Christo discubuerint, quum sacrum hoc mysterium fuit institutum. Item.
units.tr: Nor indeed are the Papists to be heard, who maintain that these words, Hoc facite, pertain only to the priests, as they call them. For the words of Christ, which Paul applies to the whole congregation of the Corinthians, clearly refute them. Nor do we deny that in this mystery account must be taken of each person's calling, since it is not lawful for anyone to administer the holy symbols. But while the ministers teach, exhort and administer the sacraments themselves, and the people listen attentively and receive the sacraments with due reverence, the whole Church is rightly said to perform what Christ commanded in these words, "Do this." Unless perhaps they wish to restrict the Lord's Supper to the ministers alone, because only the apostles reclined with Christ when this holy mystery was instituted. Likewise.

units.la: Si facere, significat sacrificare (quæ Pontificiorū est sententia) falsum est igitur quod illi ipsi dicunt sacrificiū fieri in Transsubstantiatione. Consequētia patet. Hoc facite, inquit, quotiescunque biberitis. Atqui, si illis credimus, Transsubstantiatio longē antecedit sumptione sacrameti (ne nūc vrgeamus quod solus sacrificulus in Missa comedit & bibit.) Ex quo fit vt sumptio Sacramenti, sit ipsum sacrificium externum (quod illi nolunt, & reclamat Canon Missæ, in quo oblatio sacrificij antecedit ipsam manducationem) aut, facere, non significet sacrificare: quod tamen illi propo-nunt.
units.tr: If facere signifies sacrificare (which is the opinion of the Papists), then what they themselves say is false, that a sacrifice takes place in Transubstantiation. The consequence is clear. Hoc facite, he says, quotiescunque biberitis. But, if we believe them, Transubstantiation comes long before the reception of the sacrament (not to press now that the little sacrificer alone eats and drinks in the Mass). It follows that either the reception of the Sacrament is itself the external sacrifice (which they do not want, and the Canon of the Mass protests, in which the offering of the sacrifice precedes the eating itself), or facere does not signify sacrificare, which nevertheless they propose.

units.la: Hunc igitur Pontificiorum errorem ita corrigamus.
units.tr: Let us therefore correct this error of the Papists as follows.

units.la: Quandoquidem, vt Cœnæ D. mysterium rite celebretur, ad ipsum Christi institutum deueniendum est, ex Apostoli doctrina: & Christus S. Cœnam instituens nominatim dixit: H o c FACITE: quibus verbis iussit nos huic sanctissimo instituto planè adhære-re, ab eoque ita pendere, vt nullis homini-bus, quicunque tandem ij sint, miscere liceat sua commenta, quibus illius puritas vllo modo corrumpatur: Idcirco Missam Pontificiam, quæ nihil habet cum hoc Christi instituto commune: quippe quæ potius humanis additamentis mysterium Cœnæ Domini penitus corrupit, & in nouum & Scripturæ incognitum sacrificandi genus conuertit: optimo iure, vera Dei Ecclesia ex Euangelicis præceptis reformata damnat atq; reiicit.
units.tr: Since, for the mystery of the Lord's Supper to be celebrated rightly, we must come to the very institution of Christ, according to the doctrine of the Apostle; and since Christ, instituting the Holy Supper, expressly said: THIS DO. By these words he commanded us to adhere plainly to this most holy institution and to depend upon it in such a way that it is not lawful for any men, whoever they may be, to mix in their own inventions, by which its purity is corrupted in any way. Therefore the Papal Mass, which has nothing in common with this institution of Christ, since it rather, by human additions, has utterly corrupted the mystery of the Lord's Supper and turned it into a new kind of sacrificing unknown to Scripture, is condemned and rejected by the true Church of God, reformed according to the evangelical precepts, with the best right.

units.la: Ex hac nostra Responsione facile tollitur sequens Pontificiorum obiectio, quæ à superiore manauit.
units.tr: From this our Response the following objection of the Papists, which flowed from the previous one, is easily removed.

units.la: Obiectio 2.
units.tr: Objection 2.

units.la: Si quod fieri iussit Christus his verbis: H o c FACITE in meam commemorationem, id fieri imperauit ad oblationem in cruce factam commemo-randam ipsius facti similitudine, & hoc fieri non potest nisi per solam oblationem: Ergo Christus imperauit imperauit vt sacrificium externum offerremus.
units.tr: If Christ commanded that this be done, by the words, DO THIS in remembrance of me, he commanded it to be done to commemorate the oblation made on the cross, by a likeness of the act itself, and this cannot be done except through the oblation alone. Therefore Christ commanded us to offer an external sacrifice.

units.la: Verum est Antecedens.
units.tr: The antecedent is true.

units.la: Verum igitur Consequens.
units.tr: Therefore the consequent is true.

units.la: Assumptum patet ex loco Pauli, Mortem Domini annuntiabitis, inquit, donec veniat.
units.tr: The minor premise is plain from the words of Paul: You shall proclaim the Lord's death, he says, until he comes.

units.la: Responsio.
units.tr: Answer.

units.la: Assumptum est salsissimum: ut perspicuum est ex illo ipso loco Pauli, quem tamen ipsi suffulciunt suo argumento. Sic enim Paulus: annuntiabitis, inquit. At, aliquid exprimere similitudine facti, non est, annuntiare. Nam καταγγέλλειν ad praedicationem verbi Dei pertinet, non ad gesticulationes theatricas. Vrgeda est enim particula causalis, ὅτι, apud Apostolum. Sic enim illi: Hoc facite ad meam recordationem: quotiescunque enim ederitis panem hunc, & poculum hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annuntiabitis donec veniat. En tibi quo pacto fiat commemoratio mortis Christi: nempe, annuntiando: hoc est, praedicando. Quare primus hic error est, παρὰ τὸ ἡῆμα τῆς λέξεως.
units.tr: The premise is most ridiculous, as is plain from the very passage of Paul which they themselves use to support their argument. For Paul says: you shall proclaim. But to express something by a likeness of the deed is not to proclaim. For to proclaim [καταγγέλλειν] belongs to the preaching of God's Word, not to theatrical gestures. Moreover, the causal particle [ὅτι] should be insisted upon in the Apostle. For he says: Do this in remembrance of me; for as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you shall proclaim the death of the Lord until he comes. See how the remembrance of Christ's death is made: namely, by proclaiming, that is, by preaching. So this is the first error, a fallacy of the expression [παρὰ τὸ ἡῆμα τῆς λέξεως].

units.la: Secundus error: falsa & absurda interpretatio verborum Christi: quis enim hanc expositionem ferat? Hoc facite, id est, repraesentate oblationem in cruce factam ipsius facti similitudine. Ergo si bonos istos Grammaticos audiamus: facere, significabit repraesentare ipsius facti similitudine: &, Hoc, significabit oblationem in crucem factam. At enim in argumento superiore nobis exponebant pronomen demonstratiuum, Hoc, de actionibus Christi, tum circa panem, tum circa calicem. Obsecro: Num illæ Christi actiones fuerunt oblatio in cruce facta? Sic Pontificij disputatores, quod vna manu ponunt, altera tollunt. Nec mirum: cum ea sit mendacij natura vt seipsum destruat. Quinetiam si istis credamus: moriendum esset, vt mortem Christi repræsentaremus: nullam enim maiorem facti similitudinem video.
units.tr: The second error is the false and absurd interpretation of Christ's words. For who could bear this explanation? Do this, that is, represent the offering made on the cross by a likeness of the deed. So if we listen to these good grammarians: to do will mean to represent by a likeness of the deed, and this will mean the offering made on the cross. Yet in the argument above they were explaining the demonstrative pronoun this as referring to Christ's actions, both over the bread and over the cup. I beg you: were those actions of Christ the offering made on the cross? So the Papist disputants, what they set down with one hand, they take away with the other. No wonder, since it is the nature of a lie to destroy itself. Indeed, if we believed them, we would have to die in order to represent Christ's death, for I see no greater likeness of the deed.

units.la: Tertius error: παρὰ τὸ ἐπόμενον. Nec enim sequitur, si Christus voluit mortem suam nobis aliqua similitudine in memoriam revocari: idcirco similem oblationem esse faciendam. Nam, ecce, In Baptismo mortem Christi nobis in memoriam revocari testatur Apostolus: nec propterea in Baptismo fit vlla similis oblatio: nec ipsi dicunt Baptismum esse externum aliquod sacrificium. Cum autem in Cœna Domini ipsa signa, videlicet, panis & vinum atque imprimis ipsius panis fractio, nobis in memoriam revocet mortem & passionem Iesu Christi: externis hisce rebus, ab ipso Christo institutis contenti esse debemus: non autem temere & arbitratu nostro facta quædam externa comminisci, quæ tanti mysterij naturam & vsum penitus euertant.
units.tr: The third error is a fallacy of what follows [παρὰ τὸ ἐπόμενον]. It does not follow that, because Christ wished his death to be brought to our memory by some likeness, a similar offering must therefore be made. For, look, the Apostle testifies that Christ's death is brought to our memory in Baptism, and yet no similar offering is made in Baptism for that reason; nor do they themselves say that Baptism is some external sacrifice. But since in the Lord's Supper the signs themselves, namely the bread and wine, and above all the breaking of the bread, bring to our memory the death and passion of Jesus Christ, we ought to be content with these external things instituted by Christ himself, and not rashly and at our own pleasure devise certain external acts which utterly overturn the nature and use of so great a mystery.

units.la: Nunc Pontificios ad incommodum & ἀδύνατον adigamus.
units.tr: Now let us drive the Papists to an absurdity [ἀδύνατον].

units.la: Si simile sacrificium & similem oblationem fieri necesse est, ut sacrificium Christi & oblatio in cruce facta significetur: ergo nullum aliud signum est, quàm sacrificium. Absurdum: cùm etiā in Theologia signum latiùs pateat quàm sacrificium. Isti autem negant mortem Christi posse aliter significari quàm sacrificio.
units.tr: If a similar sacrifice and a similar offering must be made, so that the sacrifice of Christ and the offering made on the cross may be signified, then there is no sign other than the sacrifice. This is absurd, since in theology a sign has a wider range than a sacrifice. Yet they deny that the death of Christ can be signified in any way other than by a sacrifice.

units.la: Retorqueamus argumentum: Si Christus præcepit ut oblatione quam ipse fecit in cruce pro nobis, facti similitudine in memoriam renovemus: Ergo Missa non est ex præcepto Christi instituta: quandoquidem nihil est in Missa quod vllā habeat cum passione Christi similitudinem.
units.tr: Let us turn the argument back: If Christ commanded that we renew in memory, by a likeness of the deed, the offering which he himself made for us on the cross, then the Mass was not instituted by Christ's command, since there is nothing in the Mass that has any likeness to the passion of Christ.

units.la: Consequentia patet. Nam in Missa ad voluptatem comparata sunt omnia: tantùm abest vt horribiles mortis Christi cruciatus vllo modo significentur. Illic omnia lucent auro & gemmis: odores suauissimi incenduntur: aures musicis cantibus demulcetur: altare ipsum mollissimè stratum est. Quid plura? Si voluptas non habet doloris similitudinem: certè quæ fiunt in Missa, morti & passioni Christi similia esse non possunt. Item.
units.tr: The consequence is plain. For in the Mass everything is arranged for pleasure; so far is it from the case that the dreadful torments of Christ's death are signified in any way. There everything gleams with gold and jewels; the most sweet perfumes are burned; the ears are soothed with musical chants; the altar itself is spread with the softest coverings. What more? If pleasure has no likeness to pain, then certainly the things done in the Mass cannot be like the death and passion of Christ. Likewise.

units.la: Si in Missa fit oblatio similis oblationi Christi: (vti dicunt) Ergo non est illa ipsa oblatio: quod tamen affirmant quoties vrgentur Apostoli verbis, quibus docet vnica Christi oblatione fideles esse consummatos: quà de re à nobis ante disputatum est.
units.tr: If in the Mass an offering is made that is similar to the offering of Christ (as they say), then it is not that very offering; yet they affirm this whenever the Apostles are pressed with the words by which he teaches that the faithful are made perfect by the one offering of Christ, a matter which we have already disputed above.

units.la: Quamobrem error ille ita corrigatur, vt dicamus: Christum instituisse S. Coenæ Sacramentum ad mortis suæ memoriam celebrandam: quippe cui nostra, tum obliuio, tū ingratitudo satis perspecta sit. Porrò ipsum noluisse, vt nudis tantùm signis sensus nostri afficeretur: sed imprimis (Paulo interprete) adhibendam esse synceram & perspicuam Euangelij prędicationem, quæ morte Christi & eius beneficia nobis inculcet & nos simul doceat, quæ sit vera signorum, quæ nobis in S. Cœna proponuntur, significatio: & quis sit legitimus ipsius Sacramenti vsus.
units.tr: Therefore that error should be corrected so that we say: Christ instituted the sacrament of the Holy Supper to celebrate the memory of his death, since both our forgetfulness and our ingratitude are sufficiently well known. Moreover, he did not wish our senses to be affected only by bare signs; but above all (as Paul interprets it) there must be employed the sincere and clear preaching of the Gospel, which impresses upon us the death of Christ and its benefits, and at the same time teaches us what is the true meaning of the signs set before us in the Holy Supper, and what is the lawful use of the Sacrament itself.

units.la: Obiect. 3.
units.tr: Objection 3.

units.la: Sacrificium externum proprie dictum est, quū res aliqua peculiari modo immutatur & conficitur in eum finem, vt per ipsam commutationem concilietur Deo gloria.
units.tr: A sacrifice is properly called external when some thing is specially changed and produced for the purpose that, through that very change, glory is brought to God.

units.la: Missa est eiusmodi.
units.tr: The Mass is of this kind.

units.la: Quare Missa est sacrificium externum proprie dictum.
units.tr: Therefore the Mass is properly called an external sacrifice.

units.la: Minor patet: quia in Transsubstantiatione separatim conficitur corpus & separatim sanguis: atque id speciem & similitudinem quandam mortis habet.
units.tr: The minor premise is plain, because in Transubstantiation the body is produced separately and the blood separately, and this has a certain appearance and likeness of death.

units.la: Respons.
units.tr: Answer.

units.la: Maioris propositionis primus error est: quòd, cùm, ex præceptis τρόπῳ παιδείας, priùs definiri debeat, An sit, quàm, Quid sit (quoties illud in dubium reuocatur) nòsque pernegemus, post vnicum Christi sacrificium vllum externum sacrificium in Ecclesia Christiana superesse: frustra laborent in afsignanasignanda sacrificij externi definitione. Nam quod illi concludunt: etiam sublatis legalibus sacrificiis, superesse nihilominus externa sacrificia: quemadmodum, sublatis legali bus Sacramentis, supersunt noui Testaméti Sacramenta: perinique faciunt. Vt enim ea sunt noui Testamenti Sacramenta, quae Christus verbis expressis instituit: ita nobis ea supersunt sacrificia, quae in sacris literis commendantur: nimirum spiritualia, non autem externa & realia, vt Pontificij existimant.
units.tr: The first error in the major premise is this. According to the method of teaching [τρόπῳ παιδείας], one must first define whether a thing exists before one defines what it is, whenever that existence is called into doubt. We deny outright that any external sacrifice remains in the Christian Church after the one sacrifice of Christ. So they labour in vain to assign a definition of external sacrifice. As for their conclusion that external sacrifices remain even when the legal sacrifices have been abolished, just as New Testament sacraments remain when the legal sacraments have been abolished, they do no good by it. For just as those are the sacraments of the New Testament which Christ instituted in express words, so those sacrifices remain for us which are commended in the sacred writings, namely spiritual sacrifices, and not external and real ones, as the Papists suppose.

units.la: Secundus error: quod ea definitio quam proponunt, imperfecta fit: omissum enim est praecipuum membrum ipsius definitionis: nempe, institutum Dei: quod si absit, verum sacrificium esse non potest. Itaque, quum dicunt, Peculiari modo res immutatur: addendum fuit: Et offertur Deo ex ipsius instituto. Alioqui non video cur Ethnicorum sacrificia, vera sacrificia non fuerint. Sed de vocabulo sacrificij & de eius definitione iam ante a nobis disputatum est.
units.tr: The second error is that the definition they propose is imperfect, for the chief element of the definition is left out, namely the institution of God. Without this there can be no true sacrifice. So when they say, a thing is specially changed, it ought to have been added: and is offered to God by his own institution. Otherwise I do not see why the sacrifices of the heathen were not true sacrifices. But we have already discussed the word sacrifice and its definition earlier.

units.la: Tertius error: quum dicunt, rem aliquam immutari & confici: quae verba satis-ne recte explicari possint, ipsi viderint. Cum autem ideo instituta sit definitio, vt facilius doceat: & haec Pontificiorum definitio fit, non tantum imperfecta, sed etiam obscura, secum pugnans, & inexplicabilis, nedum possit rem ipsam nobis explicare: relinquitur, vt sit inepta definitio, & quæ definitio dici non debeat.
units.tr: The third error is this. When they say, a thing is changed and produced, let them see for themselves whether these words can be properly explained. A definition is devised so that it may teach more easily, and this Papist definition is not only imperfect but also obscure, self-contradictory and unintelligible, so far from being able to explain the thing to us. It follows that it is a useless definition, and should not be called a definition at all.

units.la: 1. Vrgeamus incomodo. Si illud demum verum est externum sacrificium proprie dictum, in quo res quæ offertur non tantum immutari debeat, sed etiam confici siue fieri, vt dicunt. Ergo nullum vnquam sacrificium legale veteris Testamenti fuit verum sacrificium proprie dictum ἀδιώλατον.
units.tr: 1. Let us press the inconvenience. If that alone is truly an external sacrifice properly so called, in which the thing offered must not only be changed but also produced or made, as they say, then no legal sacrifice of the Old Testament was ever a true sacrifice properly so called [ἀδιώλατον: an utter absurdity].

units.la: Consequentia patet: quia in legalibus sacrificiis, res quæ offerebatur, non fiebat: sed potius immolabatur & exurebatur pro ratione sacrificij: nec vllus vnquam sine risu cogitare posset, ex hac mirifica definitione consequi: In legalibus sacrificiis repente agnos, hædos & vitulos fuisse factos, qui Deo offerrentur: aut, cineres, in quos holocausta conuertebantur, fuisse Deo in legalibus sacrificiis oblatos. Item.
units.tr: The consequence is plain, because in the legal sacrifices the thing offered was not made. Rather it was slain and burnt, according to the nature of the sacrifice. And no one could think without laughing that this wonderful definition implies that in the legal sacrifices lambs, kids and calves were suddenly made and then offered to God, or that the ashes into which the burnt offerings were turned were offered to God in the legal sacrifices. And so on.

units.la: 2. Si in Missa res immutatur & conficitur, & hoc Pontificij ad suam Transsubstantiationem referunt: Ergo res vna eademque est substantia panis, & substantia corporis Christi (absit dicto blasphemia.) Consequentia patet: Nam de vna eademque re dicuntur hæc duo, immutari, & confici, siue, fieri. At id quod immutatur (vt isti volunt) est substantia panis & vini: quod vero fit, siue, conficitur: est corpus & sanguis Christi (ex eorum sententia) Quorsum igitur res hæc euadat, facile est videre.
units.tr: 2. If in the Mass the thing is changed and produced, and the Papists refer this to their Transubstantiation, then one and the same thing is the substance of bread and the substance of the body of Christ (God forbid such blasphemy). The consequence is plain. For these two things, to be changed and to be produced or made, are said of one and the same thing. But what is changed (as they want) is the substance of bread and wine, and what is produced or made is the body and blood of Christ (on their own view). It is easy to see where this leads.

units.la: Iam argumentum retorqueamus hoc modo: Si ea est natura sacrificij Missæ, vt res offerenda, siue, victima immutetur (vt Pontificij definiunt) & vi Transsubstantiationis, substantia panis immutatur, nō autē corpus Christi (vt illi ipsi volunt) Ergo in Missa substantia panis offertur Deo, non autem corpus Christi. Aut, si corpus Christi offertur. Ergo Christi corpus immutatur, ἀδιωάτως. Item.
units.tr: Now let us turn the argument back in this way. If the nature of the sacrifice of the Mass is such that the thing offered, or the victim, is changed (as the Papists define it) and by the power of Transubstantiation the substance of bread is changed, and not the body of Christ (as they themselves wish), then in the Mass the substance of bread is offered to God, and not the body of Christ. Or, if the body of Christ is offered, then the body of Christ is changed, [ἀδυνάτως: impossibly]. And so on.

units.la: Si separatim corpus & sanguis conficiuntur vi Transsubstantiationis: aut hæc separatio fit vere, aut non vere. Si vere: Ergo Christus vere occiditur (quod absit) Nam eiusmodi separatio sine morte fieri non potest. Si non vere: non fit igitur vere Transsubstantiatio. Item.
units.tr: If the body and blood are produced separately by the power of Transubstantiation, then this separation either happens truly or does not happen truly. If truly, then Christ is truly slain (God forbid), for such a separation cannot happen without death. If not truly, then Transubstantiation does not truly happen. And so on.

units.la: Si separatim corpus & sanguinem conficivi Transsubstantiationis, efficit, vt sacrificium sit in Missa, quoniam illud habet quandam mortis similitudinem: ergo in Missa non est verū sacrificiū, sed tantum species & imago sacrificij. Item.
units.tr: If by the power of Transubstantiation the body and blood are produced separately, this makes the sacrifice in the Mass have a certain likeness of death. Therefore in the Mass there is no true sacrifice, but only the appearance and image of a sacrifice. And so on.

units.la: Si propter concomitantiam sanguis a corpore Christi separari non potest, nec vicissim corpus a sanguine (vt Pontificij tradunt) falsum est igitur quicquid illi suprà dixerunt de corpore separatim confecto, itemque de sanguine: ac propterea falsum est etiam quod proponunt de mortis similitudine, qua tamen volunt suum Missæ sacrificium niti.
units.tr: If, because of concomitance, the blood cannot be separated from the body of Christ, nor conversely the body from the blood (as the Papists teach), then whatever they said above about the body being produced separately is false, and likewise about the blood. Therefore what they propose about the likeness of death is also false, though they want their sacrifice of the Mass to rest on it.

units.la: Quamobrem Syllogismi Pontificiorum errores ita corrigamus. Sacrificium externum proprie dictum, est, sacra cæremonia a Deo instituta, qua pios maiores vti voluit an te aduentum Christi: vt ea ratione, tū ad poenitentiam, tum ad fidem ipsius Christi venitur (cuius externum sacrificium typus erat) excitati, cultum Deo gratum acceptúmque exhiberent. Cùm autem Christus aduentu suo, atque imprimis eo sacrificio quod semel in cruce pro nobis obtulit, omnes typos & figuras veteris Testamenti abrogauerit: nullum externum sacrificium proprie dictū in Ecclesia Christiana relictum est. Ac proinde dogma Pontificiorum de Missæ sacrificio, humanum est commentum: quo luci & veritati Euangelicæ, & ipsius Christi exhibitioni, perfectisimóque eius sacrificio, quoad eius fieri potest, derogatur.
units.tr: Therefore let us correct the Papists' syllogisms in this way. An external sacrifice properly so called is a sacred ceremony instituted by God, which he willed the godly of old to use before the coming of Christ. By it they were roused to repentance and to faith in Christ himself (of whom the external sacrifice was a type), so that they might offer worship pleasing and acceptable to God. But since Christ, by his coming, and above all by that sacrifice which he offered once for all on the cross for us, has abrogated all the types and figures of the Old Testament, no external sacrifice properly so called has been left in the Christian Church. Accordingly the Papists' doctrine of the sacrifice of the Mass is a human invention, by which the light and truth of the Gospel, the very presentation of Christ, and his most perfect sacrifice are, so far as it can be, detracted from.

units.la: Obiect. 4.
units.tr: Objection 4.

units.la: Omnis Pontifex siue sacerdos ex hominibus assumptus pro hominibus constituitur in iis quæ sunt ad Deum vt offerat dona & sacrificia pro peccatis, inquit Apostolus, Ergo, etiā temporibus noui Testamenti, sunt sacerdotes constituti qui offerant dona & sacrificia pro peccatis.
units.tr: Every high priest taken from among men is appointed for men in the things pertaining to God, that he may offer gifts and sacrifices for sins, says the Apostle. Therefore, even in the times of the New Testament, there are priests appointed who offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.

units.la: Consequentia patet: Quia tempus præsens vsurpatur ab Apostolo: Constituitur, inquit, & Propositio est vniuersalis.
units.tr: The consequence is plain, because the Apostle uses the present tense: is appointed, he says, and the proposition is universal.

units.la: Responsio.
units.tr: Response.

units.la: Falsum est Consequens. Error est falsa expositio loci Apostoli. Perspicuum est enim Apostolu illic agere de Pontificibus veteris Testamenti, vt eos cum Christo comparet: idque, fdque,non vt solam similitudinem inter eos esse doceat: sed potius, vt Christum Pontificibus veteris Testamenti, infinitis partibus,anteponat.Sed praestat singulos errores falsę illius interpretationis, saltem crasiores redarguere.
units.tr: The consequence is false. The error lies in a false exposition of the Apostle's passage. For it is clear that the Apostle there is speaking of the high priests of the Old Testament, in order to compare them with Christ. He does this not merely to teach that there is some likeness between them, but rather to set Christ infinitely above the high priests of the Old Testament. But it is worth refuting the individual errors of that false interpretation, at least the grosser ones.

units.la: Primus error: dum ita legunt apud Apostolum: Omnis Pontifex siue sacerdos. Nam si de summo sacerdote intelligunt (quo sensu nos Christum dicimus esse noui Testamenti sacerdotem) bene habet. Sed non video quî sacrificulos innumerabiles iuuare possit hæc sententia: quandoquidem de eo sacerdote loquitur Apostolus, quę vnum, & solum (quandiu vixerit) esse oporteat. Quòd si nomen sacerdotis latè exponunt pro omnibus sacrificij faciendi Ministris, procul ab Apostolo recedunt. Sic enim ille πᾶς ἀρχιερεὺς, inquit, hoc est, summus sacerdos.
units.tr: The first error is that they read in the Apostle, Every high priest or priest. If they understand this of the chief priest, in the sense in which we call Christ the priest of the New Testament, then it is well and good. But I do not see how this sentence can help countless petty sacrificers, since the Apostle is speaking of that priest who ought to be one and only, as long as he lives. But if they stretch the name of priest broadly to cover all ministers of sacrifice, they depart far from the Apostle. For he says, every chief priest [πᾶς ἀρχιερεύς], that is, the chief priest.

units.la: Secundus error : quòd vniuersalem sententiam Apostoli non ad legales Pontifices restringant: Cùm tamē aperte subiiciat Apostolus: Sicut & Aaron, inquit: vt iam dubitari non possit, quin ibi sermonem instituerit de veteris Testamenti Pontificibus. Porrò constat, Christum comparari cum omnibus illis Pōtificibus, de quibus loquitur Apostolus, vt perspicuum est ex his verbis quæ paulò post sequuntur: Ita & Christus, inquit, &c. quæ omnia miror ab istis non animaduersa. Nec illis fauet præsens tempus illic vsur-patum ab Apostolo. Quum enim de rebus præteritis differimus, solemus præsens tem-pus vsurpare, vt ita res ipsas ante oculos pro-ponere videamur. Sic idem Apostolus: Et ij quidem qui sunt ex filiis Leui sacerdotio fun-gentes, præceptum habent decimarum accipien-darum a populo, secundum legem. Item. Hic quidem homines qui moriuntur decimas accipiunt. Item. Lex homines constituit Pontifices infirmos. Item. In primum quidem tabernaculum quouis tempore ingrediuntur sacerdotes qui ritus obeunt: In secundum autem semel quotannis solus Pontifex non sine sanguine quem offert pro seipso & pro populi erratis. Item. Omnia secundum legem sanguine purificantur. Item. Lex vmbram obtinens futurorum ijs hostiis quas singulis annis easdem offerunt: nunquam potest accedentes sanctificare. Item. Nunc autem meliorem expetunt: & fexcenta eiusmodi, quæ siquis velit ad noui Testamenti tempora accommodare, propter verba præsentis temporis in his omnibus locis vsurpata: ille profecto in errore crassissimo versabitur. Quamobrem Apostolus ea quæ olim fieri solita sunt, per verbum præsentis temporis expressit, loquendi genere passim vsitato.
