units.tr: The second error is that they do not confine the Apostle's universal statement to the legal priests, although the Apostle openly adds, as also Aaron, so that there can be no doubt that he is discussing the priests of the Old Testament. Moreover, it is established that Christ is compared with all the priests of whom the Apostle speaks, as is clear from the words that follow shortly: So also Christ, and so on. I am surprised that these people have not noticed all this. Nor does the present tense used there by the Apostle favour them. When we discuss past things, we are accustomed to use the present tense, so that we seem to set the things themselves before our eyes. So the same Apostle: And those indeed who are of the sons of Levi, who discharge the priesthood, have a command to take tithes from the people according to the law. Likewise: Here indeed men who die receive tithes. Likewise: The law appoints men as high priests who are weak. Likewise: Into the first tabernacle the priests who perform the rites enter at all times; but into the second only the high priest, once a year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the errors of the people. Likewise: All things according to the law are purified with blood. Likewise: The law, having a shadow of the good things to come, can never make those who approach perfect, by those sacrifices which they offer year by year. Likewise: But now they desire a better country, and countless others of this kind. If anyone wished to apply these to the times of the New Testament, because of the present-tense verbs used in all these passages, he would surely be in the grossest error. Therefore the Apostle expressed what was formerly customarily done by the present tense, in a manner of speaking commonly used everywhere.

units.la: Hocigitur incommodo Pontificios vr-geamus. Si propositio Apostoli esset plane vniuersalis: ergo Christum etiam comprehende-ret. ret: At hoc falsum esse perspicuum est ex iis quæ sequuntur apud Apostolum. Quod & ipse circumdatus sit infirmitate, & propter hanc debeat, sicut pro populo, ita & pro seipso offerre pro peccatis, ἀδύνατον & blasphemum. Sic enim idem Apostolus, Cui non sit quotidie necesse sicut illis Pontificibus prius pro peccatis propriis victimas offerre, &c.
units.tr: Let us therefore press this difficulty upon the Papists. If the Apostle's proposition were plainly universal, it would include Christ too. But that this is false is clear from what the Apostle goes on to say: that he himself is beset with infirmity, and that because of this he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins, which is impossible [ἀδύνατον] and blasphemous. For the same Apostle says, who does not need every day, as those priests did, first to offer victims for their own sins, and so on.

units.la: Retorqueamus locum Apostoli in Pontificios hoc modo: Si Apostolus in cap. 5. Epist. ad Heb. ad cap. 7. tota illa epistola ita tractat de sacerdotibus omnibus externa sacrificia offerentibus, ut solos legales sacerdotes commemoret & Christum æternum sacerdotem legalibus illis sacerdotibus adumbratum: nec vllos proferat mortales homines qui in Ecclesia Christiana sacerdotes dici debeant: Certè si cum Apostolo loqui & sentire velimus, nullos agnoscemus mortales sacerdotes Ecclesiæ Christianæ.
units.tr: Let us turn the Apostle's passage back against the Papists in this way. If the Apostle, in chapter 5 of the Epistle to the Hebrews, and in chapter 7 and throughout that whole epistle, so treats of all priests offering external sacrifices that he mentions only the legal priests, and Christ the eternal priest foreshadowed by those legal priests, and brings forward no mortal men who ought to be called priests in the Christian Church, then certainly, if we wish to speak and think with the Apostle, we shall acknowledge no mortal priests of the Christian Church.

units.la: Sic igitur falsa Pontificiorum interpretatio videtur esse corrigenda. Omnis Pontifex ex hominibus assumptus pro hominibus constituitur in iis quæ apud Deum [agenda sunt] ut offerat donaria & victimas pro peccatis, inquit Apostolus: hoc est: Ea fuit ratio Pontificum veteris Testamenti, ut quisquis esset legitimus Pontifex, is, ex præscripto legis, ex hominibus assumeretur, & constitueretur ad eos ritus erga Deum obeundos, qui continebantur in lege, atque imprimis, ut offerret donaria, & victimas pro peccatis, &c.
units.tr: Thus the false interpretation of the Papists seems to be corrected. Every high priest taken from among men is appointed for men in the things to be done before God, that he may offer gifts and victims for sins, says the Apostle. That is: such was the manner of the priests of the Old Testament, that whoever was a lawful priest was, by the prescription of the law, taken from among men and appointed to perform before God those rites which were contained in the law, and especially to offer gifts and victims for sins, and so on.

units.la: Correctio sive obiectionis & falsæ interpretationis.
units.tr: Correction of the objection and of the false interpretation.

units.la: Obiectio 5.
units.tr: Objection 5.

units.la: Omnis Pontifex ad offerendum munera & hostias constituitur. Vnde necesse est hunc (nempe Christum) habere aliquid quod offerat, inquit Apostolus. Ergo Christus se quotidie offert in coelis pro nobis. Consequentia patet ex verbis illis Habere, & offerat: quae non rem praeteritam sed praesentem significant. Adde quae aliquanto post sequuntur. Non in manufactA Sancta Iesus introiuit, exemplaria verorum, sed in ipsum coelum vt appareat nunc vultui Dei pro nobis.
units.tr: Every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices. Hence it is necessary that this one (namely Christ) have something to offer, says the Apostle. Therefore Christ offers himself every day in heaven for us. The consequence is plain from the words "to have" and "to offer," which signify not a past act but a present one. Add what follows a little later: "Jesus did not enter into the holy places made with hands, the copies of the true ones, but into heaven itself, to appear now before the face of God for us."

units.la: Responsio.
units.tr: Answer.

units.la: Nego Consequens. Error est: falsa expositio loci citati. Sic enim locus ille interpretandus est: Necesse fuit hunc quoque habere aliquid quod offerret: vel, quod offerre debuerit. Et sic interpretatur qui inter scholasticos Doctores Pontificios habetur doctissimus, vt Thomas. Haec enim vis est verbi προσφέρειν, quo vtitur Apostolus: quod quidem non significat tempus praesens, vt illi existimant: Doctoribus Grammaticis poenas propterea daturi. Hoc igitur sibi vult Apostolus; Christum noui Testamenti Pontificem naturam humanam habuisse, vt eam semel pro nobis offerret, tum quum semel pro nobis in cruce mortuus est: ipsumque Christum verum Deum ac verum hominem, peracto illo vnico sacrificio, ad dextram Dei Patris consedisse, vbi pro nobis interpellat.
units.tr: I deny the consequence. It is an error: a false exposition of the passage cited. For that passage must be interpreted thus: it was necessary that this one also have something to offer [προσφέρειν], or, that he ought to have offered. This is how the most learned of the Papist scholastic teachers, such as Thomas, interpret it. For this is the force of the verb "to offer" [προσφέρειν] which the Apostle uses, and it does not signify the present tense, as they suppose, and so they will pay the penalty before the grammarians. So this is what the Apostle means: Christ, the High Priest of the New Testament, had a human nature, so that he might offer it once for us, when he died once for us on the cross; and that Christ himself, true God and true man, having completed that one sacrifice, sat down at the right hand of God the Father, where he intercedes for us.

units.la: Nec enim Christus fuit terrenus & legalis sacerdos, qui ex præscripto legis sacrificium offerret: sed nouo & perfectissimo sacerdotio defunctus, quum seipsum in cruce obtulit, finem imposuit legali sacerdotio: quo stante, Christi sacerdotium stare nō poslet: quia figura cum veritatis exhibitione simul esse non potest.
units.tr: For Christ was not an earthly and legal priest, who offered a sacrifice according to the prescription of the law. Rather, having discharged a new and most perfect priesthood, when he offered himself on the cross, he put an end to the legal priesthood. While that stood, the priesthood of Christ could not stand, because a type cannot exist at the same time as the reality it prefigures.

units.la: Alter error in alio loco quem subiiciût, non minus corrupto, falsa ipsorum expositione. Nam, apparere vultui Dei pro nobis, non est seipsum offerre & sacrificare: quandoquidem illud est huius effectum: quod facile fuit colligere ex ipsa serie contextus: Ingressus est, inquit, in ipsum cœlu[videlicet posteaquam factus est victima pro peccatis nostris] ut appareat in conspectu Dei pro nobis. Sic Paulus, Christus qui mortuus est, inquit, imo vero qui etiam excitatus est, qui etiam est ad dextram Dei, qui etiam postulat pro nobis, & alibi. Vnus est mediator Dei & hominum homo Christus Iesus qui semetipsum dedit redemptionis pretium &c. Adde quæ paulò post sequûntur apud nostrum Apostolum: Vna, inquit, pro peccatis oblata victima, in perpetuum sedet ad dextram Dei: Προσενέγκας, hoc est, posteaquam obtulit: non autem, assiduè oblaturus vt isti somniant. Cæterum vt omnes videat quàm syncerè ex Scripturæ locis argumententur, audiamus ea quæ continuò subiicit Apostolus, Neque, inquit, vt sæpe offerat semetipsum, &c. Quid autem Pontificij? Vt saepe offerat seipsum, inquiunt. Et hoc est, scilicet, ex Apostoli loco argumentari. Quamobrem satis erit hoc uno incommodo longè grauissimo superiorem obiectionem obruere.
units.tr: Their other error, in another passage which they bring forward, is no less corrupt, owing to their false exposition. For to appear before the face of God for us is not to offer and sacrifice oneself, since that appearing is the effect of the offering, as was easy to gather from the very sequence of the context: "He entered, it says, into heaven itself [namely, after he had been made the victim for our sins], so that he might appear in the sight of God for us." So Paul: "Christ who died, he says, nay rather who was also raised, who is also at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession for us," and elsewhere: "There is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom," and so on. Add what follows a little later in our Apostle: "One sacrifice for sins, he says, he offered, and sits for ever at the right hand of God." "Having offered" [Προσενέγκας], that is, after he had offered; not, as those dreamers suppose, one who is going to keep offering again and again. Moreover, so that everyone may see how sincerely they argue from the passages of Scripture, let us hear what the Apostle goes on to add: "Nor, he says, that he should offer himself often," and so on. But what do the Papists say? "That he should offer himself often," they say. And this, of course, is what they call arguing from the Apostle's passage. Therefore it will be enough to overturn the earlier objection with this one, by far the most serious, defect.

units.la: Si sacrificium Missæ ex eo fit quod Christus appareat nunc in conspectu Dei pro nobis (quod Pontificij audent affirmare) & Christus assiduè pro nobis apparet in conspectu Dei, quanuis Missa non assiduè celebretur (quod Pontificij non audent negare:) Sequitur: sacrificium Missæ sine Missæ sacrificio esse posse. Ita facilè redarguitur superior obiectio, adhibito instrumento artis differendi, ἐξ ἀνλιικεμένων: quod est verum ac proprium flagellum earum obiectionum quas Pontificij nobis opponunt.
units.tr: "If the sacrifice of the Mass comes about because Christ now appears before the face of God for us (which the Papists dare to affirm), and Christ constantly appears before the face of God for us, although the Mass is not constantly celebrated (which the Papists do not dare to deny), it follows that the sacrifice of the Mass can exist without the sacrifice of the Mass." In this way the earlier objection is easily refuted, by applying the tool of the art of disputing, [ἐξ ... ], which is the true and proper scourge of those objections which the Papists oppose to us.

units.la: Obiectio 6.
units.tr: Objection 6.

units.la: Necesse est exemplaria quidem cœlestium his mundari: ipsa autem cœlestia melioribus hostiis quàm istis, inquit Apostolus, hoc est, pluribus Missarum oblationibus. Ergo in Missa fit verum & externum sacrificium. Consequentia patet, quia nomine cœlestium intelligit Ecclesiam & loquitur de hostiis, plurali numero.
units.tr: "It is necessary indeed that the heavenly things themselves be cleansed by these, but the heavenly things themselves by better sacrifices than these," says the Apostle, that is, "by many oblations of the Masses." Therefore in the Mass there is a true and external sacrifice. The consequence is plain, because by the name "heavenly things" he understands the Church, and he speaks of sacrifices in the plural.

units.la: Responsio.
units.tr: Answer.

units.la: Falsum est Consequens. Error idem qui supra.
units.tr: The consequence is false. The error is the same as above.

units.la: Errores superioris obiectionis. supra; nempe, falsa loci Apostolici expo-sitio. Primùm enim, vocabulum, θυσίας ab Apostolo vsurpatum, perperam illi exponunt de Missarum oblationibus: quia vocabulum illud significat victimam: oblationem autem significare Apostolus solet vocabulo προσφορά: Atque illa duo distinguenda sunt, vt patet ex eodem Apostolo: Sanctificati sumus, inquit, per oblationem corporis Iesu Christi semel: vbi vides, corpus Christi esse victimam, cuius semel oblatio facta est. Quare nomen hostiae in hoc loco retinendum fuit: quod agnouit etiam vetus Interpres. Quia verò locus hic tum à veteribus tum à recentioribus, adeóque ab ipsis Scholasticis Doctoribus variè fuit expositus (quorum tamen nullus, qui modò Doctoris nomen mereatur, vocabulum θυσίας de Missarum oblationibus intellexit) neque patitur instituti nostri ratio, vt varias interpretationes, vel proferamus, vel excutiamus: nobis satis erit, nouam hanc, falsam & ἑτεροδόξον interpretationem, incommodis laceratam, ex huius disputationis theatro explodere.
units.tr: The errors of the earlier objection, namely the false exposition of the Apostolic passage. For first, they wrongly explain the word "sacrifices" [θυσίας], used by the Apostle, as referring to the oblations of the Masses, because that word signifies a victim; the Apostle usually signifies an oblation by the word "offering" [προσφορά]. And these two must be distinguished, as is clear from the same Apostle: "We have been sanctified, he says, through the offering [προσφορά] of the body of Jesus Christ once for all," where you see that the body of Christ is the victim, whose offering was made once. Therefore the name "victim" [θυσία] had to be retained in this passage, as the ancient translator also recognised. Since this passage has been variously expounded both by the ancients and by more recent writers, and indeed by the scholastic teachers themselves (none of whom, however, who deserves the name of teacher, understood the word "sacrifices" [θυσίας] to refer to the oblations of the Masses), and since the plan of our work does not allow us either to set forth or to examine the various interpretations, it will be enough for us to drive out this new, false and heterodox interpretation, battered by its defects, from the stage of this disputation.

units.la: Cùm per cœlestì Pontificij intelligant Ecclesiam post aliquot interpretes: aut Ecclesiam veteris Testamenti simul cum Ecclesia Christiana comprehendunt: aut, non: Si non comprehendunt: nos sic ratiocinamur.
units.tr: Since the Papists, following some interpreters, understand the "heavenly things" to be the Church, they either include the Church of the Old Testament together with the Christian Church, or they do not. If they do not include it, we reason thus:

units.la: 1 Quæcunque non mundata sunt melioribus illis hostiis de quibus Apostolus locutus est: ea nullū habuerūt accessum ad cœleste hæreditate.
units.tr: 1. "Whatever things were not cleansed by those better sacrifices of which the Apostle spoke, these had no access to the heavenly inheritance."

units.la: Ecclesia veteris Testamenti nō mundata est meliorib9 illis hostiis, & c.(inquiūt illi.)
units.tr: The Church of the Old Testament was not cleansed by those better sacrifices, and so on (they say).

units.la: Ecclesia igitur veteris Testamenti nullū habuit accessum ad cœleste hæreditate, ἀδύνατον & perabsurdum.
units.tr: "Therefore the Church of the Old Testament had no access to the heavenly inheritance," which is impossible and utterly absurd.

units.la: Maior est perspicua ex his Apostoli verbis: Lex vmbram obtinens futurorum, ijs hostiis quas singulis annis easdem assiduè offerunt, nunquam potest accedentes sanctificare: Item.
units.tr: The major premise is clear from these words of the Apostle: "The law, having a shadow of the good things to come, can never, by those sacrifices which they offer continually year by year, make perfect those who approach." Likewise:

units.la: Nihil sanctificauit Lex, & alibi. Dona sacrificiaque offeruntur quæ non possunt conscientia sanctificare cultorem, &c.
units.tr: "The law made nothing perfect," and elsewhere: "Gifts and sacrifices are offered which cannot make the worshipper perfect in conscience," and so on.

units.la: Si malint veterem etiam Ecclesiam vnâ cum Ecclesia Christiana comprehendere: nos rursus sic agemus.
units.tr: If they would rather include the ancient Church as well, together with the Christian Church, we shall again proceed thus:

units.la: 2 Si Israelitica Ecclesia mundata etiam fuit melioribus illis hostiis de quibus Apostolus locutus est: nec tamen fuit mundata Missarū oblationibus: certè meliores illæ hostiæ de quibus locutus est Apostolus, non sunt Missarum oblationes. Item.
units.tr: 2. "If the Israelite Church was indeed cleansed by those better sacrifices of which the Apostle spoke, yet was not cleansed by the oblations of the Masses, then certainly those better sacrifices of which the Apostle spoke are not the oblations of the Masses."

units.la: 3 Siverum est quod Pontificij dicunt, in Missa non plures esse hostias, sed vnam tantum: & locum hunc Apostoli exponunt de pluribus hostiis: certè perperam hunc locum ad suam Missam accommodant. Discant enim ex Prima Philosophiæ præceptis, quænam sit inter vnum & plura contrarietas, Item. Si locus Apostoli de pluribus hostiis esset intelligendus: ipse sibi contradiceret (quod absit.) Consequentia patet, Quia statim subiicit in illo ipso loco: Neque, inquit, vt saepe offerat semetipsum, &c. Ex quo efficitur, & Christū esse vnicam victimam: &, vnicae illius victimae vnicam quoque fuisse oblationem: vt & alibi. Vna pro peccatis oblata victima, in perpetuum sedet ad dexteram Dei, &c.
units.tr: 3. "If it is true, as the Papists say, that in the Mass there are not many sacrifices but only one, and they apply this passage of the Apostle to many sacrifices, then certainly they wrongly fit this passage to their Mass. Let them learn from the first principles of philosophy what the opposition is between one and many." Likewise: "If the Apostle's passage were to be understood of many sacrifices, he would contradict himself" (God forbid). The consequence is plain, because he immediately adds in that very passage: "Nor, he says, that he should offer himself often," and so on. From which it follows both that Christ is the one victim, and that this one victim had also one offering only; so also elsewhere: "One victim offered for sins, sits for ever at the right hand of God," and so on.

units.la: Aut Apostolus in hoc loco oblationem Christi in cruce pro nobis factam intellexit: aut non. Si non intellexit: Ecclesia igitur non est mundata morte Christi (quod absit) ne mihi vrgenda sint quae sequuntur apud Apostolum. Ex quibus manifestè colligitur ibi agi de vnico Christi sacrificio. Si intellexit: quorsum igitur plures Missae oblationes?
units.tr: "Either the Apostle in this passage understood the offering of Christ made for us on the cross, or he did not. If he did not understand it, then the Church has not been cleansed by the death of Christ" (God forbid), "and the things that follow in the Apostle must not be pressed on me. From them it is clearly gathered that there he is speaking of the one sacrifice of Christ. If he did understand it, why then are there many oblations of the Mass?"

units.la: Quamobrem ita corrigamus errorem istius obiectionis.
units.tr: Therefore let us correct the error of this objection thus:

units.la: Apostolus pluralem numerum in hoc loco pro singulari vsurpauit: eò quòd in comparatione legalium victimarum versabatur. Hinc factum est, vt numerum multitudinis in vno comparationis membro vsurpatum, in altero retinuerit. Caeterum, pluralem numerum saepe pro singulari vsurpari in Scriptura, manifestum est: de qua enallage Doctores, praesertim Hebraei consulendi sunt.
units.tr: The Apostle used the plural number in this passage for the singular, because he was dealing with a comparison with the legal victims. Hence it came about that, having used the plural of multitude in one member of the comparison, he kept it in the other. Moreover, that the plural is often used for the singular in Scripture is evident; on this figure of speech the teachers, especially the Hebrews, should be consulted.

units.la: Sed quia fortasis aegrè ferunt a nobis corrigi: saltem suorum magistrorum vocem audiant. Sic enim Thomas, locum hunc Apostoli enarras: Dicit, Hostiis, in plurali, inquit. Contra: Quia tantum est una hostia Christi: infra: Una enim oblatione consummauit in perpetuum sanctificatos. cap. 10. Respondeo: licet una sit in se: tamen pluribus hostiis veteris legis figurabatur. Hæc Thomas, posteriorum monachorum imperitiam pro nobis redarguës.
units.tr: But since they may take it badly that we correct them, let them at least hear the voice of their own masters. Thus Thomas expounds this passage of the Apostle: He says, "Sacrifices," in the plural. Against this: because there is only one sacrifice of Christ; below: "For by one offering he has perfected for ever those who are sanctified," chap. 10. I answer: although it is one in itself, yet it was prefigured by many sacrifices of the old law. So Thomas, refuting by our side the ignorance of the later monks.

units.la: Obiectio 7.
units.tr: Objection 7.

units.la: Translato sacerdotio necesse est ut legis translatio fiat, inquit Apostol. Nulla igitur lex Dei sine sacerdotio esse potest. Et vi Consequentis: lex Euangelica non potest esse sine sacrificio. Hoc autem sacrificium, est sacrificium Missæ.
units.tr: When the priesthood is transferred, the law must of necessity be transferred as well, says the Apostle. Therefore no law of God can exist without a priesthood. And by the force of the consequence: the Gospel law cannot exist without sacrifice. But this sacrifice is the sacrifice of the Mass.

units.la: Consequentia patet propter relationem sacerdotij & sacrificij.
units.tr: The consequence is evident, because of the relation between priesthood and sacrifice.

units.la: Responsio.
units.tr: Answer.

units.la: Nolo ad viuum resecare istud concludendi genus: quandoquidem (quod ad rem ipsa attinet) nemo nostrum hactenus negauit sacerdotium noui Testamenti. Sed vim ista Consequentis plane repudio. Error est duplex, nempe παρὰ τὸ ἐπόμενον & Petitio principij. Nec enim sequitur: si aliquod est noui Testamenti sacerdotium: idcirco in Missa fieri verū & externum sacrificium. Atque id est de quo inter nos quæritur, & quod hic proponitur non probatum, sed tanquam postulatum. Nos vero affirmamus, Christū esse vnicum æternúmque sacerdotem noui Testa-menti: eiúsque sacrificium in cruce peractu, esse vnicum, verum & reale ac proprie dictu noui Testamenti sacrificiu, ad Christi æternu sacerdotium relate dictum. Atque ita vno verbo vana hæc obiectionis Pontificiæ bul-la in ventos abiit: quam nos etiam subiectis aliquot incommodis redarguamus.
units.tr: I do not wish to cut this kind of argument to the quick, since (as far as the matter itself goes) none of us has so far denied the priesthood of the New Testament. But I wholly reject the force of this consequence. It is a double error, namely the fallacy of the consequent [παρὰ τὸ ἐπόμενον] and begging the question. For it does not follow that, if there is some priesthood of the New Testament, therefore a true and external sacrifice is performed in the Mass. That is precisely what is in dispute between us, and what is here proposed not as proved but as if granted. We, on the other hand, affirm that Christ is the only and eternal priest of the New Testament, and that his sacrifice accomplished on the cross is the one, true and real sacrifice of the New Testament, properly so called, and related to Christ's eternal priesthood. And so this empty bubble of the Papists' objection vanishes into the air with a single word; yet we will also refute it by pointing out several inconveniences.

units.la: Si verum esset & necessarium sacerdotes Pon-tificios esse veros sacerdotes, & in Missa fieri ve-rum & externum sacrificium, quia nouum Testa-mentum non potest esse sine Sacerdotio & sacri-ficio: Sequeretur, solos Pontificios sacerdotes esse veros sacerdotes noui Testamenti & Missæ sa-crificium esse solum noui Testamenti sacrificium, nec vllum aliud posse reperiri. Quod si recipia-tur (absit dicto blasphemia) nec Christus esset sacerdos, nec eius sacrificium in cruce factum, es-set sacrificium noui Testamenti. Ἀδυσᾶτον, blasphe-mum, impium. Item.
units.tr: If it were true and necessary that the Papist priests are true priests, and that a true and external sacrifice is made in the Mass, because the New Testament cannot exist without priesthood and sacrifice, it would follow that only the Papist priests are the true priests of the New Testament, and that the sacrifice of the Mass is the only sacrifice of the New Testament, and that no other can be found. But if this were accepted (let me not speak blasphemy), neither would Christ be a priest, nor his sacrifice made on the cross be the sacrifice of the New Testament. [ἀδύνατον]: impossible, blasphemous, impious. Likewise:

units.la: Si verum sit: non posse esse sacerdotium quin simul fiant externa sacrificia (quod isti volût.) Certè stare non poterit hoc argumentum Aposto-li: Si lex plane accedentes sanctificassest, nonne, (inquit) hostiæ desiissent offerri? Hoc etiam sta-re non poterit quod ait idem Apostolus: Vbi est remissio, non esse amplius oblationem pro peccato. Item, Vnica oblatione consummatos fuisse eos qui sanctificantur. Item, Non ut sæpe offerat semetipsum, inquit, & pleraque si-milia.
units.tr: If it is true that there cannot be a priesthood without external sacrifices being offered at the same time (which they want), then certainly this argument of the Apostle cannot stand: "If the law had perfected those who draw near, would not," he says, "the sacrifices have ceased to be offered?" Nor can what the same Apostle says stand: "Where there is remission, there is no longer an offering for sin." Likewise, "that those who are sanctified had been perfected by one offering." Likewise, "not that he should offer himself often," and many similar things.

units.la: Heb.10. Ibid. Ibid. Heb.9.
units.tr: Heb. 10. Ibid. Ibid. Heb. 9.

units.la: Retorqueamus locum Apostoli in ipsos Pontificios, hoc modo:
units.tr: Let us turn the Apostle's passage back upon the Papists themselves, in this way:

units.la: 1 Si Christus æternus sacerdos secundum ordine Melchisedec suo tempore nobis exhibitus mutauit, tum legem, tum sacerdotium legis, quod quidem externum erat & sacrificiis externis vnicu & perfectum Christi sacrificium repræsentabat: Certe ferendi non sunt qui externum hodie sacerdotium & externorum sacrificiorum vsum in Ecclesiam volunt renocare. Item.
units.tr: 1 If Christ, the eternal priest according to the order of Melchizedek, who was shown to us in his time, has changed both the law and the priesthood of the law, which indeed was external and, through external sacrifices, represented the one and perfect sacrifice of Christ, then surely those who want to recall today an external priesthood and the use of external sacrifices into the Church are not to be tolerated. Likewise:

units.la: 2 Si vetus sacerdotium translatum est, non in sacrificulos Pontificios, sed in Christum vnicum Ecclesiæ Christianæ Pontificem: & sacrificia legalia, in vnicum ipsius Christi sacrificium: vt in hoc loco Apostolus copiose confirmaut: certe locus hic Apostoli ad euertendum, non ad stabiliendum: Missæ sacrificium accommodandum est. Quamobrem huius loci à Pontificiis detorti corruptique nos ita verum sensum restituamus.
units.tr: 2 If the old priesthood has been transferred, not to Papist little priests, but to Christ alone, the High Priest of the Christian Church, and the legal sacrifices to the one sacrifice of Christ himself, as the Apostle abundantly confirms in this place, then certainly this passage of the Apostle is to be applied to overthrowing the sacrifice of the Mass, not to establishing it. Wherefore, having seen that this passage has been twisted and corrupted by the Papists, we thus restore its true sense.

units.la: Posteaquam Christus sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedec nobis fuit exhibitus: vnico illo sacrificio quod in cruce pro peccatis nostris obtulit, vetus sacerdotium & legalia omnia sacrificia abrogauit: eorum omnium substantia in ipso Christo remanente. Vt igitur legale sacerdotium suam rationem, modum, ritus denique suos habuit: ita noui Testamenti sacerdotium suam habet rationem, longe legalibus omnibus figuris præstantiorem. Nam in veteris Testamenti sacerdotio plures fuere sacerdotes, tes,iidémque mortales, & plura sacrificia: at sacerdotij noui Testamenti hæc est ratio & natura, vt vnus sit sacerdos, idemque æternus, nempe Christus: & vnicum sit, nempe Christi sacrificium, quo semetipsum in cruce pro nobis obtulit, factus sacerdos simul & victima: cuius quidem sacrificij semel facti & nunquam iterandi perpetua est efficacitas.
units.tr: After Christ was shown to us as priest for ever according to the order of Melchizedek, he abrogated the old priesthood and all the legal sacrifices by that one sacrifice which he offered on the cross for our sins, the substance of all of them remaining in Christ himself. Just as the legal priesthood had its own reason, manner and, finally, its own rites, so the priesthood of the New Testament has its own reason, far more excellent than all the legal figures. For in the priesthood of the Old Testament there were many priests, and these mortal, and many sacrifices; but the reason and nature of the priesthood of the New Testament is this: that there is one priest, and he eternal, namely Christ; and there is one sacrifice, namely the sacrifice of Christ, by which he offered himself for us on the cross, made priest and victim at once; and of this sacrifice, once made and never to be repeated, the efficacy is perpetual.

units.la: Obiectio 8.
units.tr: Objection 8.

units.la: Agnus Paschalis fuit figura mysterij Eucharistiæ: & Agnus ille sacrificandus erat & offerendus. Ergo in mysterio Eucharistia Christus est sacrificandus & offerendus.
units.tr: The Paschal lamb was a figure of the mystery of the Eucharist, and that lamb was to be sacrificed and offered. Therefore, in the mystery of the Eucharist, Christ is to be sacrificed and offered.

units.la: Consequentia patet: quia oportet inter figuram & veritatem esse similitudinem. Assumptum confirmat Paulus 1. Cor. 5. Pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus.
units.tr: The consequence is plain, because there must be a likeness between figure and truth. Paul confirms the assumption in 1 Cor. 5: "Our Passover, Christ, has been sacrificed."

units.la: Responsio.
units.tr: Answer.

units.la: Falsum est Consequens: tum propter sua, tum propter Antecedentis vitia. Quod vt magis fiat perspicuum, age, excutiamus Antecedens.
units.tr: The consequence is false, both on account of its own faults and on account of the faults of the antecedent. So that this may become clearer, come, let us examine the antecedent.

units.la: Duo proponuntur in Antecedente: vnum, agnum Paschalem fuisse figuram mysterij Eucharistiæ: Alterum, Agnum Paschalem sacrificandū & offerendum fuisse. De vtroque sigillatim nobis agendum est. Agnum Paschalem fuisse typum & figuram Christi, cuius sanguis semel pro nobis effusus nos ab æterno exitio liberauit, agnoscimus. Rursus agnoscimus, Christum nobis offerri in sacro Cœnæ Dominicæ mysterio: sed non video quinam inde colligi possit, Agnum illum fuisse figuram mysterij Eucharistiæ: siquidem proprie loquimur, vti decet, quoties de rebus Theologicis accuratæ disputationes instituuntur: licet non ignoremus aliquot ex veteribus ita locutos fuisse: qua de re suo loco nobis agendum erit. Iam expresi sunt loci, ex quibus facile intelligi potest, Agnum Paschalem Christum ipsum repræsentasse: adeo vt ab aperta Scripturæ sententia nobis recedere non liceat. Pascha nostrum (inquit Paulus) pro nobis sacrificatum est, nempe, Christus (id quod non sua sed nostra causa citarunt Pontifici) &, Non confringetur vllum os ipsius, inquit Moses de Agno Paschali quod in Christo impletum fuisse docet Ioannes. Quare ita statuendum est ex Theologicis principiis: sacramenta veteris Testamenti figurasse, non nostra sacramenta, proprie: sed Christum ipsum: quem etiam ipsa novi Testamenti sacramenta nobis proponunt. Sit igitur hic Pontificiorum error: ψευδολογία in Theologia: aut certè, quacunque tandem id interpretatione leniatur, ἀκυρολογία.
units.tr: Two things are put forward in the antecedent: first, that the Paschal lamb was a figure of the mystery of the Eucharist; second, that the Paschal lamb was to be sacrificed and offered. We must deal with each separately. We acknowledge that the Paschal lamb was a type and figure of Christ, whose blood, once poured out for us, has freed us from eternal destruction. Again we acknowledge that Christ is offered to us in the holy mystery of the Lord's Supper; but I do not see what can be inferred from this, that the lamb was a figure of the mystery of the Eucharist, since we speak properly, as is fitting whenever accurate disputations about theological matters are carried on, although we do not ignore that some of the ancients spoke in this way; we shall have to deal with that matter in its own place. Now, passages have been cited from which it can easily be understood that the Paschal lamb represented Christ himself, so that we may not depart from the plain sense of Scripture. "Our Passover," says Paul, "has been sacrificed for us, namely Christ" (a text which the Papists have cited, not for their own purpose but for ours). And "not a bone of him shall be broken," says Moses of the Paschal lamb, which John teaches was fulfilled in Christ. Therefore this must be affirmed from theological principles: the sacraments of the Old Testament figured not our sacraments, strictly speaking, but Christ himself, whom the sacraments of the New Testament also set before us. So let this be the error of the Papists: a false speaking in theology, or at least, however it may be softened by some interpretation, an improper speaking.

units.la: Addunt, Agnum Paschalem fuisse sacrificandum & offerendum: quod quatenus verum sit, dispiciendum est. Agnum illū fuisse mactanmactandum, pasim legimus: sacrificandum vero sacrificio proprie dicto, nusquam videas. Vocatur, inquis, Courban. Certe: sed hoc nomen generale est, quo legales omnes oblationes significabantur, vt videre licet Leuit. cap. 1. ver. 3. 10. 14. & cap. 2. ver. 1, 4. 5. 7. 14. & sexcenta similia. Unde Marcus: Corban, quod est donum, inquit. Amplius dico: ipsum etiam nomen, Zeuach (cuius vsus est frequentissimus in sacrificiis proprie dictis) aliquando vsurpari in caeremonia Agni Paschalis, idque propter mactationem: Sed non propterea vetus illa caeremonia fuit vnquam numerata inter sacrificia externa & legalia, quae quidem proprie sacrificia dicta sunt.
units.tr: They add that the Paschal lamb was to be sacrificed and offered; how far this is true must be examined. We read everywhere that the lamb was to be slain; but nowhere will you see that it was to be sacrificed in the proper sense. You say it is called "korban." Certainly, but this is a general name by which all the legal offerings were signified, as may be seen in Leviticus chapter 1 verses 3, 10, 14, and chapter 2 verses 1, 4, 5, 7, 14, and countless similar passages. Hence Mark: "Corban, which is a gift," he says. I say more: the word itself, zebach (whose use is most frequent in sacrifices properly so called), is sometimes employed in the ceremony of the Paschal lamb, and that on account of the slaying; but that old ceremony was never for that reason counted among the external and legal sacrifices, which are indeed what are properly called sacrifices.

units.la: Cum igitur Zeuach non tantum significet sacrificium proprie dictum, sed etiam aliquoties ita late sumatur, vt etiam spiritualia sacrificia significet (vt: Sacrificans confessio-nem. Item, Sacrificia Deo grata Spiritus con-fractus, &c. in quibus locis vocabulum illud vsurpatur) non recte colligitur: Agnum Paschalem fuisse sacrificium proprie dictum, eo quod aliquando vocatur vel oblatio, vel sacrificium: Et hic error est παρὰ τὸ ὁμωνυμίαν. Quid ergo? nimirum vt diiudicemus, quaenam sint sacrificia proprie dicta, adeoque pro peccatis oblata (de quibus agunt Pontificij, quando volunt suam Missa esse verum & externum sacrificium proprie dictum & propitiatorium pro peccatis)non ex solo vocabulo ratiocinandum est: sed ex ipsa sacrificiorum proprie dictorum institutione.Ex quo fit vt dicamus,Agnum Paschalem non fuisse sacrificium proprie dictum: quandoquidem nec a solis sacerdotibus,nec ad altare mactabatur, nec aliquid obserua-batur eorum quæ Dominus facienda præce-perat in sacrificiis offerendis.Ipsi autem Pō-tificij,quum sacrificium proprie dictum definiunt, nominatim hæc addunt: Quum a de-lecto Ministro offertur: adeo vt se ipsi refel-lant & pro nobis ad suam hanc obiectionem respondeant.Et certè,quanquam omnis cul-tus Deo, ex ipsius præscripto, exhibitus,suo modo, oblatio, donum & sacrificium spi-rituale dici poterit: tamen diligenter consi-derandum est, quidnam fuerit in legalibus cæremoniis præcipuum ac primarium,vt in-de dispicere liceat, quænam fuerint vera sa-crificia in ipsa Dei lege instituta. In Agno Paschali, mactatio quidem videbatur ad ve-ra sacrificia accedere , in quibus victimæ mactabantur: sed nemo non videt agnum fuisse mactandum,non vt Deo offerretur,& sacrificaretur (nulla enim ne minima quidē particula:Deo consecrabatur,quod in victi-mis legalibus solitū erat) sed vt ex eo Israe-litæ vescerentur: vt perspicuum est ex ipsa institutione Exod. 12. & Num.9.Celebrabit, inquit,Pascha cum azymis & herbis amaris comedent illud, &c. Quinetiam (quod à Pontificiis, vel non animaduersum, vel neglectum fuisse miror) quum Pharao permitteret Israelitis sacrificium Deo facere, dummodo in AEgypto sacrificarent: negauit Moses id rectum esse, & aperte negauit Israelitas in AEgypto esse sacrificaturos. Atenim Israelitæ Pascha in AEgypto celebrarunt, vt testatur sacra historia. Quid igitur dubitationis superesse potest, quin ceremonia agni Paschalis fuerit à sacrificiis distinguenda? Sed de Antecedente huiusce obiectionis, nimis iam multa.
units.tr: Therefore, since zebach signifies not only a sacrifice properly so called but is also sometimes taken so broadly that it signifies even spiritual sacrifices (as: "Sacrificing confession"; likewise, "The sacrifices pleasing to God are a broken spirit," etc., in which places that word is used), it is not rightly concluded that the Paschal lamb was a sacrifice properly so called, because it is sometimes called either an offering or a sacrifice. And this error is a parà to homonymia, a fallacy of ambiguity. What then? Assuredly, in order to judge what sacrifices are properly so called, and therefore offered for sins (about which the Papists argue when they wish their Mass to be a true and external sacrifice properly so called and propitiatory for sins), we must reason not from the word alone but from the very institution of sacrifices properly so called. From this it follows that we say the Paschal lamb was not a sacrifice properly so called, since it was slain neither by priests alone nor at the altar, and no part was observed of those things which the Lord had commanded to be done in offering sacrifices. But the Papists themselves, when they define a sacrifice properly so called, expressly add this: "when it is offered by a lawful minister"; so that they refute themselves and answer this objection of theirs on our behalf. And indeed, although every worship exhibited to God according to his prescription may in its own way be called an offering, a gift and a spiritual sacrifice, nevertheless we must consider carefully what was principal and primary in the legal ceremonies, so that from this it may be possible to discern which were the true sacrifices instituted in God's own law. In the Paschal lamb, the slaying indeed seemed to approach the true sacrifices, in which victims were slain; but everyone sees that the lamb was slain not in order to be offered and sacrificed to God (for not even the smallest portion of it was consecrated to God, as was customary with legal victims), but so that the Israelites might eat of it; as is plain from the institution itself, Exodus 12 and Numbers 9. "They shall keep the Passover," it says, "and eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs," etc. Moreover (which I wonder the Papists either did not notice or neglected), when Pharaoh allowed the Israelites to sacrifice to God, provided they sacrificed in Egypt, Moses denied that this was right, and plainly denied that the Israelites would sacrifice in Egypt. Yet the Israelites celebrated the Passover in Egypt, as sacred history attests. What doubt, then, can remain that the ceremony of the Paschal lamb must be distinguished from sacrifices? But enough, indeed too much, has been said about the antecedent of this objection.

units.la: Consequês igitur recte negauimus: quod quidem peculiarem etiamnum errorem habet παρὰ τὸν ἀγνοίαν τῆς ἐλέγχῳ. Peccatur enim in ratione temporis. Ecquænam est enim hæc consecutio? Agnus Paschalis erat olim immolandus: ergo, Christus hodie immolandus est: propterea quòd Agnus ille fuit figura iampridem exhibiti Christi. Imò verò (nisi ad Iudæos Pontificij transeunt) ita concludendum est potius: Christum fuisse quidem olim pro nobis immolandum: nunc verò immolatum fuisse: quemadmodum exponit Paulus, optimus veterum & legalium cæremoniarum interpres. Pascha nostrum pro nobis sacrificatum est (nempe) Christus. Non dixit, sacrificandum est, vel, immolandum, vel, offerendum: sed, sacrificatum est, inquit. Tum addit, Itaque festiu agitemus, non fermento veteri, nec fermento malitiæ & nequitiæ, sed non fermentatis panibus syncëritatis & veritatis. hæc ille: quibus nos præclarè docet, quinam fructus veteris illius cæremoniæ in Ecclesia Christiana remanserit. Nō enim, sacrificemus Christum, dixit, sed, festum agitemus, eo, videlicet, modo, quem subiicit, synceritate & veritate: vbi nihil externum, nihil crassum, sed omnia spiritualia nobis proponit.
units.tr: Therefore we have rightly denied the consequence, which moreover has a peculiar further error, a para tEn agnoian tes elenchou, an ignorance of the refutation. For the error lies in the matter of time. For what sort of sequence is this? The Paschal lamb was once to be slain; therefore Christ is to be slain today, because that lamb was a figure of Christ already long since exhibited. Rather (unless the Papists are going over to the Jews) the conclusion should instead be this: that Christ indeed was once to be sacrificed for us, but now has been sacrificed, as Paul, the best interpreter of the ancient and legal ceremonies, explains: "Our Passover has been sacrificed for us, namely Christ." He did not say "is to be sacrificed," or "to be slain," or "to be offered," but "has been sacrificed," he says. Then he adds, "Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth." These are his words, by which he teaches us excellently what fruit of that ancient ceremony has remained in the Christian Church. For he did not say, "let us sacrifice Christ," but "let us keep the feast," that is, in that manner which he adds, sincerity and truth; where he sets before us nothing external, nothing gross, but everything spiritual.

units.la: Sentiant igitur Pötificij incommoda suę istius Conclusionis.
units.tr: Let the Papists, then, feel the disadvantages of this their conclusion.

units.la: Si consectarium est: Christum esse immolandum, eo quod Agnus (qui figura Christi fuit) olim immolari solitus est: Ergo re vera Christo etiamnum hodie moriendum est: & eius sanguis verè fundendus. Quia mactatio agni veram & realem Christi mactationem & mortem significauit: quemadmodum ex Apostolo audiuimus, ἀδωάλον. Item.
units.tr: "If it follows that Christ is to be slain, because the lamb (which was a figure of Christ) was once customarily slain, then in truth Christ must still today be put to death, and his blood truly shed; because the slaying of the lamb signified the true and real slaying and death of Christ, as we have heard from the Apostle: absurd." Likewise:

units.la: Si verum est Christum esse immolandum hodie & offerendum, vt veritas figuræ agni Pa-schalis respondeat: Ergo Christus sua morte non impleuit legales typos & figuras, ἀδωάλον, blasphemum, impium. Item.
units.tr: "If it is true that Christ is to be slain and offered today, so that the truth may correspond to the figure of the Paschal lamb, then Christ did not fulfil the legal types and figures by his death: absurd, blasphemous, impious." Likewise:

units.la: Ergo stare nō possunt hæc Christi verba (quod abest) de ipso agno Paschali differentis: Dico vobis me non amplius comesturum ex eo: donec completum fuerit in regno Dei. Quibus verbis declarauit, veterem illam figuram morte sua implendam fuisse: adeo vt qui adhuc implenimplendam illam vrgeat,is mortem Christi neget,quatum in ipso est. Qui quidem vnus est ex praecipuis Missae fructibus.
units.tr: "Therefore these words of Christ cannot stand (which God forbid), spoken concerning the Paschal lamb itself: 'I tell you that I will no longer eat of it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.' By these words he declared that the old figure was to be fulfilled by his death; so that whoever still urges that it is yet to be fulfilled denies the death of Christ, as far as in him lies. And this is indeed one of the principal fruits of the Mass."

units.la: Sed iam Pontificiorum obiectione hoc modo in ipsos retorqueamus.
units.tr: But now let us turn the Papists' objection back against them in this way.

units.la: Si ex instituto Dei nihil reseruandum erat ex agno Paschali: & Pontifici hostias in ipsorum Missa consecratas & pixide inclusas diligentissime seruant: Ergo Agnus Paschalis non fuit figura sacrificii Missae. Item.
units.tr: If by God's appointment nothing was to be kept back from the Paschal lamb, yet the Papists keep the hosts consecrated in their Mass with the greatest care and enclosed in a pyx, then the Paschal lamb was not a figure of the sacrifice of the Mass. Likewise.

units.la: Si Agnus Paschalis erat figura Christi, vt docet Apostolus: (quem citant Pontifici:) & Agnus ille sacrificabatur (id quod isti vehementer vrgent) & Christus morte sua legales omnes figuras impleuit (quod omnes verè Christiani agnoscunt:) Ergo Christus non est amplius sacrificandus: & vi consequentis ruit Missae sacrificium.
units.tr: If the Paschal lamb was a figure of Christ, as the Apostle teaches (whom the Papists cite), and that lamb was sacrificed (which they press vehemently), and Christ by his death fulfilled all the legal figures (which all true Christians acknowledge), then Christ is no longer to be sacrificed; and by force of this consequence the sacrifice of the Mass falls.

units.la: Superest vt corrigamus Pontificiorum argumentum, in hunc modum.
units.tr: It remains to correct the Papists' argument in this way.

units.la: Agni Paschalis caeremonia (vt & reliqua veteris Testamenti sacramenta) ad Christum spectabat: ac propterea in vno Christo desiit: qui sua morte ac resurrectione veteribus & legalibus caeremoniis finem impo-suit: ipsarum caeremoniarum substantia in ipso Christo remanente. Vetus autem illud Sacramentum, praeter rei praesentis circumstantias, significabat etiam aliquando futurum, vt Christi sanguis pro nobis effunderetur, cuius ea est efficacitas, vt nos a Satana & ab inferorum potestate sartos tectos conseruet. Præterea in AgniPaschalis celebratione adumbrabatur piorum hominum sanctimonia & integritas & ea quæ ad pœnitentiam carnisque mortificatione pertinent, quemadmodum Apostolus nobis exposuit. Sacramentū autem Cœnæ D.ipsum quidem Christū nobis proponit: sed non immolandū : imò potius semel pro nobis sacrificatū & oblatū Deo: vt eum vera fide ac pœnitentia, recipientes, à tenebrarum potestate liberemur.
units.tr: The ceremony of the Paschal lamb, like the other sacraments of the Old Testament, looked to Christ, and therefore it ceased in Christ alone, who by his death and resurrection put an end to the old and legal ceremonies, while the substance of those ceremonies remains in Christ himself. That old sacrament, however, besides the circumstances of the present thing, also signified that at some time Christ's blood would be poured out for us, and its efficacy is that it keeps us safe and sheltered from Satan and the power of the underworld. Moreover, the celebration of the Paschal lamb foreshadowed the holiness and integrity of godly people, and those things that pertain to repentance and the mortification of the flesh, as the Apostle has set out for us. But the sacrament of the Lord's Supper sets before us Christ himself, not to be sacrificed, but rather once offered for us as a sacrifice and offered to God; so that by receiving him with true faith and repentance we may be freed from the power of darkness.

units.la: Obiectio 9.
units.tr: Objection 9.

units.la: Omnia sacrificia à Prophetis prædicta, sunt legitima.
units.tr: All sacrifices foretold by the prophets are lawful.

units.la: Sacrificium Missæ fuit à Prophetis prædi-ctum.
units.tr: The sacrifice of the Mass was foretold by the prophets.

units.la: Quare sacrificium Missæ est legitimum.
units.tr: Therefore the sacrifice of the Mass is lawful.

units.la: Maior est perspicua. Minorem probant loci sequentes.
units.tr: The major premise is clear. The minor is proved by the following passages.

units.la: Tu es sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedec, inquit Dauid de Christo prophetans. Ergo necesse est aliquod sacrificium in Ecclesia Christiana remanserit. Consequentia patet, quia sacerdos infert sacrificiū. Christi autem sacerdotium est perpetuum. Rursus: nisi se Christus sacrificauerit in Cœna incruentè sub speciebus panis & vini: certè Christus nusquam funĕtus est sacerdotio secundùm ordinem Melchisedec. Nam Melchisedec obtulit Deo panem & vinum ita commemorante Mose, nec vnquam fit mentio mentio vllius sacrificij cruenti quod Melchise-dec Deo obtulerit.
units.tr: "You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek," says David, prophesying of Christ. Therefore it is necessary that some sacrifice has remained in the Christian Church. The consequence is plain, because a priest implies a sacrifice. But Christ's priesthood is perpetual. Again: unless Christ offered himself unbloodily in the Supper under the species of bread and wine, Christ has certainly never exercised the priesthood after the order of Melchizedek. For Melchizedek offered bread and wine to God, as Moses recounts, and nowhere is there mention of any bloody sacrifice that Melchizedek offered to God.

units.la: Responsio.
units.tr: Answer.

units.la: Iam nos Pontificij adoriuntur Propheta-rum testimoniis. Sed cùm perspicuum sit ex superioribus, adeóque ex locis Apostolicis quos illi nobis obiecerunt, nusquam istud Missae sacrificium fuisse institutum: sequens Pontificiorum disputatio vna conclusione tolli potest, quam nos ita paucis comprehendemus.
units.tr: Now the Papists attack us with the testimonies of the prophets. But since it is clear from what was said above, and so from the apostolic passages which they have objected to us, that this sacrifice of the Mass was nowhere instituted, the following Papist disputation can be overthrown with one conclusion, which we shall briefly set out thus.

units.la: Quaecunque Prophetae prædixerunt ad fidem & salutem Ecclesiæ, & ad tempora noui Testamenti pertinentia; ea Apostoli suis scriptis non tantùm proposuerunt, sed etiam copiosè explicarunt.
units.tr: Whatever the prophets foretold concerning the faith and salvation of the Church, and concerning the times of the New Testament, the apostles not only set forth in their writings but also explained at length.

units.la: Sacrificium Missae Apostoli suis scriptis non proposuerunt, nedum illud copiosè explicarint.
units.tr: The apostles did not set forth the sacrifice of the Mass in their writings, much less explain it at length.

units.la: Quare sacrificium Missae Prophetae non prædixerunt: quippe quod nec ad fidem & salutem Ecclesiæ, nec ad tempora noui Testamenti pertineat.
units.tr: Therefore the prophets did not foretell the sacrifice of the Mass, since it pertains neither to the faith and salvation of the Church nor to the times of the New Testament.

units.la: Nunc singulos locos expendamus quibus freti Pontificij nobis Prophetas, scilicet, opponunt; ac primùm de Melchisedeco nobis agendum est.
units.tr: Now let us weigh the individual passages on which the Papists, relying on them, set the prophets against us; and first we must deal with Melchizedek.

units.la: Vnum in Ecclesia Christiana esse sacrificium, nempe quod Christus æternus sacerdos secundùm ordinè Melchisedec pro nobis semel obtulit, & cuius sacrificij semel peracti perpetua est virtus & efficacia: nós agnoscimus. Sed negamus inde efficí,Christum esse saepius,idque in Missa, sacrificandum: neque hanc suam consequentiam isti probant.Si sacerdos est, inquiunt, est igitur sacrificium. Certè: sed quemadmodum sacerdos aeternus est;ita huius aeterni sacerdotis sacrificiū non est metiendum ex sacrificiis in veteri lege & ante legē scriptam vsurpatis: id quod saepe antea confirmauimus ex Apostolo ad Hebraeos scribente.Haec est igitur natura sacrificij Christi,vt semel tantum fieri debuerit: & semel factum,vim nihilominus habeat perpetuam. Atenim, inquiunt, si Christus est sacerdos secundum ordinem Melchisedec: Christus igitur sese sacrificauit incruentè in Coena. Qui tandem, obsecro? Quandoquidem simile quoddam sacrificium Melchisedec obtulit: inquiunt. Hoc igitur quam vim habeat,iam nobis considerandum est. Primum cum hunc locum Dauidicum Apostolus copiosissimè persecutus fuerit, & comparationem Christi cum Melchisedeco accuratissimè nobis explicarit, neque tamen vllam fecerit mentionem: certè pudorem in Pontificiis desideramus, quos non pudet summum aliquod mysterium Apostolo incognitum obtrudere, vt, scilicet, suppleant quod ab ipso Apostolo praetermissum est. Quid enim? nónne id
units.tr: We acknowledge that there is one sacrifice in the Christian Church, namely the one which Christ, the eternal priest after the order of Melchizedek, offered once for us, and whose sacrifice, once completed, has a perpetual virtue and efficacy. But we deny that it follows from this that Christ is to be sacrificed more often, and that in the Mass; nor do they prove their consequence. "If he is a priest," they say, "then there is a sacrifice." Certainly; but just as he is an eternal priest, so the sacrifice of this eternal priest is not to be measured by the sacrifices used under the old law and before the written law, as we have often confirmed from the Apostle writing to the Hebrews. This, then, is the nature of Christ's sacrifice: that it had to be made only once, and once made it nevertheless has perpetual force. But, they say, if Christ is a priest after the order of Melchizedek, then Christ sacrificed himself unbloodily at the Supper. Who, I beg you, says so? Since, they say, Melchizedek offered a similar sacrifice. What force this has we must now consider. First, since the Apostle pursued this Davidic passage most fully, and set out the comparison of Christ with Melchizedek most exactly, and yet made no mention of it at all, we certainly miss the shame in the Papists, who are not ashamed to foist upon us some supreme mystery unknown to the Apostle, in order, namely, to supply what the Apostle himself passed over. For what? Did that not pertain to the Apostle's purpose?

units.la: Facilius Melchisedeci ad Missae sacrificium trahi non potest. id ad Apostoli propofitū pertinebat? Imò, fi Pontificiis credas, hoc fuit caput illius comparationis quam Apostolus proposuit. At infirmi tum adhuc erant Hebræi, inquis, ac propterea nondum tanti mysterij capaces. Sic enim Apostolus, De quo nobis multa sunt dicenda, eaque difficilia explicatu: quandoquidem segnes facti estis auribus. Ve-rumenimuero cum Apostolus illa difficilia intellectu paulò post in medium afferat, eáque copiosa oratione nobis explicet; quid te iuuabit tua ifthæc obiectio? Quis autem ferat mirificam hanc interpretatio-nem? De quo nobis multum est sermo, & difficilis explicatu (inquit Apostolus) hoc est (inquiunt Pontificij) de quo propter difficultatem tacere volumus. Imò vero, quò res est difficilior, eò fe longiorem & accuratiorem sermonem instituere velle profitetur: ac propterea Hebræorum attentionem eiusmodi præfatiuncula conciliat. Sed, inquis, non valet Consequentia : Si nihil ibi dixit Apostolus de sacrificio Missæ, quum de Melchifedeco ageret: Ergo factum Melchifedeci ad sacrificium Missæ non pertinet. Atenim affirmo ego con-sequentiam valere: & propono hoc theorema Theologicum, quod Pontificij nunquam labefactabunt. Ex typis & figuris veteris Testamenti eatenus dogma aliquod statui posse, quatenus typos illos & figu-
units.tr: The case of Melchizedek cannot more easily be dragged to the sacrifice of the Mass. Indeed, if you believe the Papists, this was the very head of that comparison which the Apostle proposed. But, you say, the Hebrews were then still weak, and therefore not yet capable of so great a mystery. For thus the Apostle: "Of whom we have much to say, and it is hard to explain, since you have become dull of hearing." But truly, since the Apostle afterwards brings forward those hard matters for understanding and explains them to us in a lengthy discourse, how will this objection of yours help you? And who could bear this marvellous interpretation? "Of whom we have much speech, and it is hard to explain" (says the Apostle); that is (say the Papists), "of whom we wish to be silent because of the difficulty." Nay rather, the more difficult the matter, the more he professes that he wishes to conduct a longer and more exact discourse; and therefore such a short preface wins the attention of the Hebrews. But, you say, the inference does not hold: if the Apostle said nothing there about the sacrifice of the Mass when he was treating of Melchizedek, then the deed of Melchizedek does not pertain to the sacrifice of the Mass. Indeed I affirm that the inference holds, and I propose this theological principle, which the Papists will never overturn: some doctrine can be established from the types and figures of the Old Testament only so far as the Apostle has explained those types and figures.

units.la: Obiectio Pontificiorum. ras Apostoli claris exprefsissque verbis explicarunt. Qua de re nos alibi plura diximus. Quamobrem si ex historia Melchisedeci velis ἀποδεικτικῶς & Theologicè differere: profer igitur Apostolicam expositionem; alioqui tua disputatio tantum erit allegorica, non autè Theologica: quam doquidem si allegoriis ludere liceat; nusquam pedem figas: sed semper incertus per hominum commenta ac placita vagaberis. Atq; id Academicis & Pyrrhonianis relinquimus; quippe à Theologica πληροφορία prorsus alienum.
units.tr: The objection of the Papists: ...the Apostle has explained those types and figures in clear and express words. We have said more on this matter elsewhere. Therefore, if you wish to argue from the history of Melchizedek apodeictically [ἀποδεικτικῶς] and theologically, bring forward the apostolic exposition; otherwise your disputation will be merely allegorical, not theological. For if it is permitted to play with allegories, you will never plant your foot anywhere, but will always wander uncertain through the inventions and opinions of men. And this we leave to the Academics and the Pyrrhonists, since it is wholly foreign to theological full assurance [πληροφορία].

units.la: Secundò: Melchisedecum obtulisse Deo panem & vinum pernegamus: quod tamen Pontificij affirmant. Error istorum est: ψευδογραφημα in Theologia. Nihil enim tale extat apud Mosen. Sic enim Moses: Melchisedec rex Salem protulit panem & vinū. Et ipse erat sacerdos Dei Excelsi. Et benedixit ei, & dixit: Benedictus Abrā, &c. Sic enim legendum & distinguendum est ex Hebraico cotextu: & retinenda propria significatio copulæ; quasi dicat, regem Melchisedecum, fuisse quoque sacerdotem: vt perspicuum est ex argumento Apostoli ad Hebr. Hic igitur de oblatione & sacrificio verbū nullum. Proferre enim non est, sacrificare: neq; verbum Hebraicū, Hotsi, sacrificare & offerre significat: quod & satis intellexit vetus interpres, cui tantopere isti sunt addicti. Sic enim ille, Melchisedec rex Salem proferens panem & vinum, inquit. Rursus ecce alter error in vocabulo panis, quo Hebraei non panem tantum sed cibos cuiusque modi, instructam que mensam solent significare: quemadmodum norunt ij qui vel tantulum in ea lingua exercitati sunt. Protulit igitur Melchisedec panem & vinum ipsius Abrahami causa, cuius voluit ita gratulari de parta victoria. Itaque Graecus interpres dixit ἄρτος, numero plurali. At, inquis, dicuntur serui Abrahami comedisse de spoliis hostium. Quid tum? num propterea Melchisedici munificentia locum habere non debuit? Affirmat Moses, inquis, Melchisedecum fuisse sacerdotem Dei Excelsi. Ita sit sane: sed quis hanc conclusionem patienter audiat? Dicitur fuisse sacerdos: Ergo panem & vinum sacrificauit. Vide potius quae sequuntur: nempe Melchisedecum benedixisse Abrahamo, & ab eo decumam ex omnibus accepisse (quae diligenter expendit Apostolus) & facile iudicabis quamobrem Melchisedecus sacerdos fuisse dicatur. Itaq; illius munificentia, regem decuit: benedicere autem & decimas accipere, decuit sacerdotem.
units.tr: Second, we deny that Melchizedek offered bread and wine to God, although the Papists affirm it. This is their error, a fabrication [ψευδογραφημα] in theology. For nothing of the kind is found in Moses. Thus Moses: "Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine. And he was priest of God Most High. And he blessed him, and said: Blessed be Abram," etc. For the passage must be read and punctuated in this way from the Hebrew context, retaining the proper meaning of the copula, as if to say that King Melchizedek was also a priest, as is plain from the Apostle's argument in Hebrews. Here, therefore, there is not a word about offering or sacrifice. For to bring forth is not to sacrifice; nor does the Hebrew word hotsi mean to sacrifice and to offer. The old translator understood this well enough, and these men are so attached to him. For he says: "Melchizedek king of Salem bringing forth bread and wine." Again, there is another error in the word "bread," since the Hebrews commonly use it to signify not bread alone but food of every kind, and a furnished table, as those know who have practised even a little in that language. Melchizedek therefore brought forth bread and wine for Abraham's own sake, whom he wished to congratulate on the victory won. Hence the Greek translator used "bread" in the plural. But, you say, Abraham's servants are said to have eaten of the enemies' spoils. What then? Was Melchizedek's generosity therefore out of place? Moses affirms, you say, that Melchizedek was priest of God Most High. So be it; but who would patiently hear this conclusion? "He is said to have been a priest; therefore he sacrificed bread and wine." Rather, look at what follows: that Melchizedek blessed Abraham and received a tenth of everything from him (which the Apostle weighs carefully), and you will easily judge why Melchizedek is said to have been a priest. Thus his generosity befitted a king, but to bless and to receive tithes befitted a priest.

units.la: Tertiò: si daremus Melchisedecum panem & vinum obtulisse Deo (absit autem a nobis tam procul ab historiae veritate recedere) nihil inde tamen efficerent. Error est μέγιστον ἐτερογενὲς & plane absurdum. Nec enim ista consectaria sunt: Melchisedecus fuit figura Christi, &, panem ac vinum Deo obtulit. Ergo Christus in sacra Cœna sese incruente obtulit Deo pro nobis: quod fit etiam hodie in Missæ sacrificio. Obsecro te, ubinam Gentium Medium aliquod reperias quo isti termini tam longè disiti copulari & coniungi posfsint? Facilius, mihi crede, polum Arctici (vt hoc mihi per Astrologos liceat) cum Antarctico coniunxeris. Quis enim te imprimis docuit Melchisedecum fuisse figurà Christi? nonne Apostolus? At is comparat utriusque personam, non autè sacrificium: sic enim ille. Sine patre, sine matre, sine genere, nec initium dierum, neque vitæ finem habens: sed assimilatus filio Dei, manet sacerdos in perpetuū, & paulò post. Qui non ex lege cuius mandatū sit carnale factus est [sacerdos] sed ex vi indissolubilis vitæ. En igitur in quo constituendus sit ille ordo de quo Psaltes ab Apostolo citatus: Tu es sacerdos in æternum secundùm ordinem Melchisedec. Nempe quòd Melchisedecus, fuerit Rex simul & sacerdos, & tanquam æternus nobis in Scriptura propositus sit, adeóque præstantior Abrahamo & eius posteris, vt ita figuram gereret Christi æterni regis simul & sacerdotis & præstantioris Leuiticis omnibus sacerdotibus. Alioquin & alij plerique fuere sacerdotes: & ab ipsis Leuiticis sacerdotibus panis & vinum aliquando offerebantur. Ex quo fit vt
units.tr: Thirdly: even if we granted that Melchisedec offered bread and wine to God (though far be it from us to depart so far from the truth of the history), they would gain nothing from it. The inference is a very great error of a different kind [μέγιστον ἑτερογενές] and plainly absurd. These are not valid consequences: Melchisedec was a figure of Christ, and he offered bread and wine to God; therefore Christ offered himself to God for us in the Lord's Supper without bloodshed, which is also done today in the sacrifice of the Mass. Tell me, where in the world could you find some middle term that could join and couple such distant extremes? You would more easily, believe me, join the Arctic pole to the Antarctic (if I may use the astrologers' language). For who first taught you that Melchisedec was a figure of Christ? Was it not the Apostle? Yet he compares the persons of the two, not their sacrifices. For this is what he says: Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God, he abideth a priest continually, and a little later: Who is made a priest not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life. Here, then, is the point in which that order is to be established, of which the Psalmist, cited by the Apostle, speaks: Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec. Namely, that Melchisedec was at once king and priest, and is set before us in Scripture as one who is, as it were, eternal; and so he is superior to Abraham and his posterity, and thus bore the figure of Christ, the eternal king and priest at once, and superior to all the Levitical priests. Otherwise, many others too were priests, and bread and wine were sometimes offered by the very Levitical priests. From this it follows that

units.la: in re alia quàm in sacrificiis & oblationibus ordo ille Melchisedeci constituendus sit. Nam si oblationes & sacrificia spectes, non dubium est quin legalia & Aaronica sacrificia longè præstantissimè Christi sacrificium repræsentarint ac præsertim holocausta: vt docet Apostolus ad Hebr. nec sanè vlla panis oblatio tam expressè futurum Christi sacrificium repræsentare potuisset. Nam pati, mori, sanguinem fundere & mactari, panis non conueniunt.
units.tr: that order of Melchisedec is to be established in something other than sacrifices and oblations. For if you look at oblations and sacrifices, there is no doubt that the legal and Aaronic sacrifices represented Christ's sacrifice far more excellently, and especially the burnt offerings, as the Apostle teaches in the Epistle to the Hebrews. Indeed, no offering of bread could have represented Christ's future sacrifice so clearly. For bread does not fit with suffering, dying, shedding blood and being slain.

units.la: Vt ergo Pontificios pudeat suæ absurditatis ita dicamus.
units.tr: So, to shame the Papists for their absurdity, let us put it this way.

units.la: 1 Si quia Melchisedec panem & vinũ offeres fuit figura Christi (vt Pontificy existimant) sequitur Christum esse offerendum sub speciebus panis & vini: vt illi ipsi concludunt: Ergo simili ratione Christus esset offerendus sub earum omnium rerum speciebus quæ veteris Testamenti temporibus offerebantur Deo, vt Christum repræsentarent. A'δωάτων & horrendum. Item.
units.tr: 1. If, because Melchisedec offering bread and wine was a figure of Christ (as the Papists think), it follows that Christ is to be offered under the species of bread and wine, as they themselves conclude; then by a similar reasoning Christ would have to be offered under the species of all those things which were offered to God in the times of the Old Testament, to represent Christ. Impossible [ἀδώρατον] and horrible. Likewise:

units.la: 2 Si verum est quod isti dicunt: sequitur antiquorum sacrificiorum externam speciem in Ecclesia Christiana remansisse. Falsũ & ἑτερόδοξον: sic enim potius Scriptura docet, veterum sacrificiorum substantiam nobis in vno Christo remansisse, sublata exteriori specie.
units.tr: 2. If what they say is true, it follows that the external appearance of the ancient sacrifices has remained in the Christian Church. False and heterodox [ἑτερόδοξον]. For Scripture teaches rather that the substance of the ancient sacrifices has remained for us in Christ alone, with their outward appearance removed.

units.la: 3 Si sacerdotium Leuiticum stetit vsq; ad mortem Christi (vt docet Apostolus) Et, stante illo sacerdotio, sola legalia sacrificia erant legitima (vt omnes pij agnoscunt.) Et Christus sacerdos secundum ordinem Melchisedec ante mortem in sacra Cœna sacrificauit (vt Pontificij volunt.) Ergo sacrificium istud in Cœna factum, aut legale fuit, aut non legitimum. Vtrumque absurdissimum. Item.
units.tr: 3. If the Levitical priesthood stood until the death of Christ (as the Apostle teaches), and while that priesthood stood, only the legal sacrifices were lawful (as all the godly acknowledge), and Christ, a priest according to the order of Melchisedec, sacrificed before his death in the Lord's Supper (as the Papists want), then that sacrifice made at the Supper was either legal or not lawful. Both alternatives are most absurd. Likewise:

units.la: Si oblatio & sacrificium Melchisedeci fuit figura Christi (vt Pontificij existimant,) Ergo hanc figuram aut Christus impleuit, aut non. Si impleuit: ruit igitur Missæ sacrificium: quod enim semel impletum fuit, quotidie implendum non est. Non impleuisse autem, quis vnquam Christianus audit dicere? Hoc tamen sequitur ex Pontificiorum argumento. Item.
units.tr: If the oblation and sacrifice of Melchisedec was a figure of Christ (as the Papists think), then either Christ fulfilled this figure or he did not. If he fulfilled it, then the sacrifice of the Mass falls; for what has been fulfilled once need not be fulfilled daily. But that he did not fulfil it, what Christian has ever heard anyone say? Yet this follows from the Papists' argument. Likewise:

units.la: Si aduentu Christi exhibita fuit ea veritas cuius Melchisedec erat figura (ipsis Pontificiis assentientibus, aut certè, verbo negare non audentibus) & nihilominus remanserunt species oblationis Melchisedeci, nempe species panis & vini (quod isti Transsubstantiatores volunt,) ergo figura & veritas simul stare possunt. Ἀδιώλτον & ἀντιφατικόν.
units.tr: If the truth of which Melchisedec was the figure has been displayed by the coming of Christ (the Papists themselves agreeing, or at least not daring to deny it in words), and nevertheless the species of Melchisedec's oblation remain, namely the species of bread and wine (which these Transubstantiators want), then figure and truth can stand together at the same time. Indissoluble [ἀδιάλυτον] and contradictory [ἀντιφατικόν].

units.la: Retorqueamus igitur in Pontificios argumentum ex Melchisedeco petitum.
units.tr: Let us therefore turn back upon the Papists the argument drawn from Melchisedec.

units.la: Si Melchisedecus offerens panem & vinum Deo fuit figura Christi (vt affirmant) & Christus vnica oblatione in cruce facta veteres omnes figuras eò spectantes abrogauit (vt docet Apostolus) certè similitudo Melchisedeciad Missæ confirmatione trahi non potest. Hæc enim figura vnà cum aliis abrogata fuit. Item.
units.tr: If Melchisedec, offering bread and wine to God, was a figure of Christ (as they affirm), and Christ, by the single oblation made on the cross, abrogated all the ancient figures pointing to it (as the Apostle teaches), then certainly the likeness of Melchisedec cannot be drawn in to confirm the Mass. For this figure was abrogated together with the others. Likewise:

units.la: Si oblatio Melchisedeci figura fuit Eucharistiæ. ristia (vt isti autumant) certè Eucharistia à sa- cerdotibus Pontificiis offerri non potest. Conse- quentia patet: Nam debet manere relatio inter offerentem & rem oblatam: itémque, inter figuram & figuratum. At solus Chri- stus fuit figuratus in Melchisedeco. A nullo igitur alio,preter Christum,Eucharistia of- ferri posset. Nec est cur proferant suos illos secundarios sacerdotes: semper enim Mel- chisedecum vrgebimus,quem vllos eiusmo- di secundarios sacerdotes habuisse, ne ipsi quidem Pontificij audent somniare.Vis au- tem huiusce nostræ Conclusionis pendet ex his Apostoli verbis: Illi quidem citra iusiuran- dum sacerdotes factî sunt,hic verò cum iureiurâ- do per eum qui dixit ei: Iuravit Dominus & non pœnitebit eum:Tu es sacerdos in æternum secun- dùm ordinem Melchisedec. Et aliquantò post.
units.tr: If the oblation of Melchisedec was a figure of the Eucharist (as these men assert), then certainly the Eucharist cannot be offered by the Papist priests. The consequence is clear: for a relation must remain between the one offering and the thing offered, and likewise between the figure and the thing figured. But Christ alone was figured in Melchisedec. Therefore the Eucharist could be offered by no one other than Christ. Nor is there any reason for them to bring forward their secondary priests; for we shall always press Melchisedec, whom not even the Papists themselves dare to dream had any such secondary priests. The force of this our conclusion, moreover, depends on these words of the Apostle: Those indeed were made priests without an oath, but he with an oath by him that said unto him: The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec. And a little later.

units.la: Lex enim homines constituit infirmos: at ser- mo iurisiurandi post legem concepti filium consti- tuit qui in æternum est sanctificatus. Hæc Apo- stolus. Solus igitur Christus est sacerdos se- cundùm ordinem Melchisedec: ac propter- ea,solius Christi fuit, id offerre quod obla- tione Melchisedeci adumbratum fuit.Item.
units.tr: For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore. So says the Apostle. Christ alone, therefore, is a priest after the order of Melchisedec; and for that reason it belonged to Christ alone to offer what was foreshadowed by the oblation of Melchisedec. Likewise:

units.la: Si oblatione Melchisedeci nititur Missæ sa- crificium: actum est igitur de Transsubstantia- tione. Nam Melchisedecus dicitur protulisse non inane aliquod spectrum, vanáque panis & vini accidentia: sed panem & vinum. At Transsubstantiatio(quam volunt esse animâ sacrificij Missæ) tollit panis & vini substantiam. Iam si periit Transsubstantiatio: Missæ igitur sacrificium animam exhalauit.
units.tr: If the sacrifice of the Mass rests on the oblation of Melchisedec, then transubstantiation is done for. For Melchisedec is said to have brought forth not some empty phantom and vain accidents of bread and wine, but bread and wine. But transubstantiation (which they want to be the soul of the sacrifice of the Mass) removes the substance of bread and wine. Now if transubstantiation has perished, then the sacrifice of the Mass has breathed its last.

units.la: Huc spectant hæc verba Canonis Missæ, Hostiam puram, hostiam sanctam, hostiam immaculatam, panem sanctum vitæ æternæ & calicem salutis perpetuæ supra quæ propitio ac sereno vultu respicere digneris & accepta habere, sicut accepta dignatus es munera pueri tui iusti Abel, & sacrificium Patriarchæ nostri Abrahæ & quod tibi obtulit summus sacerdos tuus Melchisedec sanctum sacrificium, immaculatam hostiam. Si offertur ipsum Christi corpus, quor sum igitur ista comparatio? Nonne veritas est dignior sua figura? Quare, ex ipso Canone Missæ consequitur: id quod isti in sua Missa offerunt, non esse præstantius panem & vino quæ ipsi volunt à Melchisedeco fuisse oblata. Item.
units.tr: To this bear these words of the Canon of the Mass: Look upon these offerings with a kindly and serene countenance, and deign to accept them, as thou didst deign to accept the gifts of thy righteous servant Abel, and the sacrifice of our patriarch Abraham, and that holy sacrifice, the spotless victim, which thy high priest Melchisedec offered to thee. If the very body of Christ is offered, why then this comparison? Is not the truth more worthy than its figure? Therefore it follows from the Canon of the Mass itself that what these men offer in their Mass is not more excellent than the bread and wine which they themselves say were offered by Melchisedec. Likewise:

units.la: Si ea quæ Melchisedecus obtulit (ut isti dicunt) non fuerunt tecta alienaforma & alienis accidentibus: & in Missa sacrificio (si Pontificis habeatur fides) Christus offertur tectus alienaforma & alienis accidentibus: quomodo oblatio Melchisedeci ad Missæ sacrificium pertinebit? Nam si ea quæ videntur, offeruntur in Missa: certè panis & vinum in Missa offeruntur: Si aliud videtur & aliud offertur in Missa: ergo procul recedis à Melchisedeco. Etenim premo ego verbum Protulit, quo vtitur Moses, quum narrat Melchisedecum panè vinúmq; protuprotulisse. Aliud est autem, palàm aliquid proferre,quàm, id ipsum velare & tegere ne oculis pateat. Item.
