Quod pro nobis ad tempus humilitatem sustinuit gaudens prædicabo, quia talibus hostiis delectatur. Hostia iubilationis, est hostia prædicationis. Idem. Vetera sacrificia vacuanda esse declarat: ideoque in moribus bonis sacrificium requirit. Immola Deo sacrificium laudis, inquit, hoc est, sacrificium acceptabile, hoc est holocaustum pingue ut laudetur Deus ab homine quem creauit, quem redemit, cui regnum cœlesle promisit. Idem. Audiant Iudæi sacrificia
units.tr: JEROME. Shall I eat the flesh of bulls? Psalm 49. Having taken up again the ceremonies of the old law, he passes on to Gospel purity and shows what he desires in their place. Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, he says. Idem. Referring the story of Jonah to Christ and to the calling of the Gentiles: before the Lord's Passion, the sailors, fearing, cried out to their gods. After his Passion they fear, reverence and worship the Lord, and they offered sacrifices which they certainly did not have, in the midst of the waves, according to the letter; but a sacrifice to God is a contrite spirit, and so on. Jonah, a fugitive at sea, shipwrecked and dead, saves the tossing little ship and saves the Gentiles, who had been driven about by the error of the world into various opinions. From this it is shown that the shipwreck could not be calmed except by the death of the fugitive. Idem. And I will offer in his tabernacle a sacrifice of joy, Psalm 26. Because he bore humility for a time on our behalf, I will rejoice and proclaim it, since he delights in such sacrifices. A sacrifice of joy is a sacrifice of proclamation. Idem. He declares that the old sacrifices are to be set aside, and therefore he requires a sacrifice in good conduct. Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, he says, that is, an acceptable sacrifice, that is, a rich burnt offering, so that God may be praised by the man whom he created, whom he redeemed, and to whom he promised the heavenly kingdom. Idem. Let the Jews hear that their sacrifices

units.la: In Psal.26.
units.tr: On Psalm 26.

units.la: In Psal.49. sua cessasse. Quid ergo tu homo offeres? audi quid subiecit: sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus, &c.
units.tr: On Psalm 49. have ceased. What then will you, a man, offer? Hear what he added: a sacrifice to God is a contrite spirit, and so on.

units.la: AMBROSIVS. In Christo semel oblata est hostia potens ad salutem sempiternam. Idem. Iussit Dominus Angelo ut parceret plebi, sacrificium autem Dauid offerret 2. Reg. 12. Erant enim tunc sacrificia pro delictis, haec nunc sunt sacrificia poenitentiae. Idem. Apud veteres ideo oblata occidebatur hostia, ut homines peccati causa morti subiectos significaret. Nunc autem quia per donum Dei purificati sunt homines & a morte secunda liberati, viuam hostiam debent offerre ut signum sit vitae aeternae. Non enim sicut tunc corpora pro corporibus immolantur: nunc vero non corpora, sed vitia corporis perimenda sunt. Idem. Nonne altare est caeleste, fides nostra in quo offerimus quotidie orationes nostras? Idem. Accedamus, inquit, cum vero corde & plenitudine fidei, & c. Heb. 10. Accedamus sciliicet fide & spirituali cultura in veraci corde, quia nihil est visibile horum, neque sacerdos, neque sacrificium, neque altare, &c. quia spiritu spiritualia percipimus, &c.
units.tr: AMBROSE. In Christ the victim, offered once, is powerful to salvation everlasting. Idem. The Lord commanded the angel to spare the people, but David was to offer a sacrifice, 2 Sam. 12. For then there were sacrifices for sins; these now are sacrifices of repentance. Idem. Among the ancients the victim offered was slain, to signify that men, subject to death on account of sin, [were so]. But now, since men have been purified by the gift of God and freed from the second death, they ought to offer a living victim, so that it may be a sign of eternal life. For bodies are not now sacrificed for bodies as they were then; rather it is not bodies but the vices of the body that must be destroyed. Idem. Is not our faith the heavenly altar, on which we offer our prayers daily? Idem. Let us draw near, he says, with a true heart and fullness of faith, and so on, Heb. 10. Let us draw near, that is, by faith and spiritual worship, in a sincere heart, for none of these things is visible, neither priest, nor sacrifice, nor altar, and so on, because we perceive spiritual things by the spirit, and so on.

units.la: Idem.
units.tr: Idem.

units.la: AVGVSTINVS. Ipse verus Deus & Pontifex qui pro nobis non in sanguine taurorum & hircorum, sed in sanguine suo semel introiuit in sancta: quod tunc Pontifex ille significabat, qui cum sanguine in sancta sanctorum per annos singulos introibat: Ipse igitur est qui in se uno totum exhibuit, quod esse necessarium ad redemptionis ptionis nostra sciebat effectum: idem scilicet sacerdos & sacrificiu: idem Deus & templum. Sacerdos per quē sumus reconciliati: sacrificium quo reconciliati: templu in quo reconciliati: Deus, cui reconciliati: solus tamen sacerdos, sacrificium & templum: & hæc omnia Deus secundum formam serui. Idem. Christus morte sua, quippe, vno vero sacrificio pro nobis oblato, quicquid culparum erat, vnde nos principatus & potestates ad luenda supplicia iure detinebant: purgauit, aboleuit, extinxit: & sua resurrectione in nouam vitam nos prædestinatos vocauit: vocatos iustificauit: iustificatos glorificauit. Idem. Vt, quoniam quatuor considerantur in omni sacrificio: Cui offeratur: a quo offeratur: quid offeratur: pro quibus offeratur: idem ipse vnus verúsque mediator per sacrificium pacis reconcilians nos Deo: vnum cum illo maneret, cui offerebat: vnum in se ficeret, pro quibus offerebat: vnus ipse esset, qui offerebat & quod offerebat. Idem: Quod Dauid obtulit vt populo parceret, vmbra erat futuri: qua significatum est, quod per vnum sacrificium, cuius illa figura erant, saluti populi spiritualiter parcitur: ipse est enim Christus Iesus qui traditus est propter delicta nostra & resurrexit propter iustificationem nostram: propter quod etiam dicit: Pascha nostrum immolatus est Christus. Idem, Immola Deo sacrificium laudis, &c. Psal. 49. Hinc sacrificiorum veterum aperta mutatio est: illa enim Deus accepturum se non fuisse prædixit: cultoribus suis sacrificium laudis
units.tr: AUGUSTINE. The true God himself and High Priest, who entered once into the holy places for us, not with the blood of bulls and goats, but with his own blood, which that high priest foreshadowed, who used to enter the holy of holies with blood every year. He, therefore, is the one who in himself alone exhibited the whole of what he knew to be necessary for the effecting of redemption: the same priest and sacrifice, the same God and temple. Priest, through whom we are reconciled; sacrifice, by which we are reconciled; temple, in which we are reconciled; God, to whom we are reconciled; yet he alone is priest, sacrifice and temple, and all these things, God according to the form of a servant. Idem. Christ, by his death, namely by the one true sacrifice offered for us, cleansed, abolished and extinguished whatever guilt there was, by which the principalities and powers rightly held us bound to pay the penalties; and by his resurrection he called us, predestined, into a new life; those called he justified; those justified he glorified. Idem. Since four things are considered in every sacrifice: to whom it is offered, by whom it is offered, what is offered, and for whom it is offered, the same one and only mediator, reconciling us to God through the sacrifice of peace, remained one with him to whom he offered; he made himself one with those for whom he offered; he himself was the one who offered and what was offered. Idem. What David offered so that the people might be spared was a shadow of what was to come, by which it was signified that through the one sacrifice, of which those were figures, the people are spiritually spared for salvation. For it is Christ Jesus who was delivered up for our sins and rose again for our justification; on account of which he also says: Christ our Passover has been sacrificed. Idem. Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, etc., Psalm 49. Hence there is a plain change of the old sacrifices: for he foretold that he would not accept those sacrifices, and he appointed for his worshippers a sacrifice of praise.

units.la: N In Psal.94. indixit. Idem, Imponimus in ara sacrificium quando Deum laudamus. At vero sacerdotem sirequiras, super coelos est: interpellat pro te, qui in terra mortuus est pro te.
units.tr: On Psalm 94. We place a sacrifice on the altar when we praise God. But if you seek the priest, he is above the heavens; he intercedes for you, he who died on earth for you.

units.la: THOMAS autem (ne Scholasticos plane cotemnamus) Christum (inquit) non obtulit pro peccatis suis, sed tantum pro nostris: Esa.53. Vulneratus est propter iniquitates nostras. Item: nec frequenter pro nobis sed tantum semel 1. Petr. 3. Christus semel pro peccatis nostris mortuus est, unica enim eius oblatio sufficit ad exhaurienda peccata totius generis humani. Ac, ne sim longior aliis testimoniis recitandis, desinam in hac praeclara Hieronymi precatione: Nos famuli tui supplices deprecamur, Domine Iesu Christe, ut magnis facinoribus nostris immensam misericordiam largiaris, nosque per contritionem cordis humiliatos, mactando vitia, iugulando delicta, dignum tibi acceptabileque praeparés holocaustum.
units.tr: THOMAS, however (so that we do not wholly despise the Schoolmen), says: Christ offered not for his own sins but only for ours, Isa. 53: He was wounded for our iniquities. Likewise: nor frequently for us but only once, 1 Pet. 3: Christ died once for our sins, for his one offering suffices to exhaust the sins of the whole human race. And, lest I be longer in reciting other testimonies, I will end with this excellent prayer of Jerome: We, your suppliant servants, beseech you, Lord Jesus Christ, that you would grant us immense mercy for our great crimes, and that, humbled by contrition of heart, by putting to death our vices and slaying our sins, you would prepare a holocaust worthy and acceptable to you.

units.la: Ex his igitur veterum Doctorum testimoniis & plerisque aliis consimilibus, quorum pleni sunt eorum libri, perspicuum esse potest, ipsorum veterum hanc fuisse sententiam: Christum unico sacrificio pro nobis in cruce facto, propitiatorio pro peccatis, legalia omnia sacrificia abrogasse: cuius qui dem sacrificij semel facti perpetua est efficacitas: nec vlla iam alia Ecclesiae Christianae sacrificia, praeter spiritualia, superesse: quae nobis in scriptis Apostolorum commendantur. dantur. Quam nos sententiam (vt ad illud Augustinianum reuertamur) diuinarū Scripturarum authoritati congruentem, cum ipsorum Veterum laude accipimus: & siquæ occurrant minus dilucidè ab illis ipsis proposita, de sacrificiis noui Testamenti:ea nos ex aliis eorundem accuratioribus testimoniis,explicamus: adeò vt facilè ab omnibus intelligi posit: Veteres nobis in hac quæstione & in hoc Theologicè & ἀποδεικτικῶς disserendi genere,perperam fuisse obiectos. Quia verò monent Philosophi, in disputatione ἀναστευαστικῇ, quoad eius fieri potest, inuestigandum esse προτον ψευδος, & erroris primarios fontes aperiendos, vt ipsa refutatio melius perspecta sit: pauca subiiciemus de iis quæ potissimum videntur Pontificios in hunc errorem, quem refutauimus, induxisse.
units.tr: From these testimonies of the ancient teachers, and from many others of the same kind, with which their books are full, it may be clear that this was the opinion of the ancients themselves: that Christ, by the single sacrifice made once for us on the cross, a propitiation for sins, abrogated all the legal sacrifices; and that the efficacy of that sacrifice, once made, is perpetual; and that no other sacrifices of the Christian Church remain, besides spiritual ones, which are commended to us in the writings of the Apostles. We accept this opinion (to return to that saying of Augustine) with praise for the ancients themselves, as agreeing with the authority of the divine Scriptures; and if any passages on the sacrifices of the New Testament, set forth by those same men less clearly, occur, we explain them from other, more precise testimonies of the same writers, so that they may easily be understood by all: that the ancients were wrongly put forward to us in this question, and in this manner of arguing, both theologically and [demonstratively, ἀποδεικτικῶς]. But since philosophers advise that, in a refutative [ἀναστευαστικῇ] disputation, as far as it can be done, the first falsehood [προτον ψευδος] is to be sought out and the primary sources of error are to be uncovered, so that the refutation itself may be better perceived, we shall add a few remarks on those things which chiefly seem to have led the Papists into this error, which we have refuted.

units.la: Pontificij, omissa prima illa quæstione: An vlla sint externa & realia sacrificia in Ecclesia Christiana: prosiliunt ad Sacrificij definitionem: & quærunt: Quid sit, cùm nondum planum fecerint: An sit. Quare, si vera esset eorum sentētia: primum omnium efficiendum esset ex planis ac dilucidis Scripturæ locis, & ex ipsa Christi institutione: sacrificia externa & realia esse à Christianis offerenda: atque inde facilè depromerent veram ac propriam sacrificij à Christianis offerendi definitionem.
units.tr: The Papists, passing over that first question, whether there are any external and real sacrifices in the Christian Church, rush to the definition of sacrifice and ask: what it is, before they have made clear whether it is at all. Wherefore, if their opinion were true, it would first have to be shown from the plain and clear passages of Scripture, and from Christ's own institution, that external and real sacrifices are to be offered by Christians; and from that they would readily draw out the true and proper definition of the sacrifice to be offered by Christians.

units.la: Secundò: Quum externum sacrificium definiunt: omittunt ea quæ sunt ὑπαωδήν, & sine quibus sacrificium esse non potest: videlicet, ipsum Dei institutum: quod cum illos deficiat, nihil mirum si dubij incertíque per humana somnia vagentur.
units.tr: Secondly: when they define external sacrifice, they omit those things which are ὑπαωδήν (underlying), and without which a sacrifice cannot exist, namely God's own institution. Since this is lacking to them, it is no wonder that they wander about in doubt and uncertainty, following human dreams.

units.la: Tertiò: Non distinguunt inter sacrificium crucis, &, ipsius sacrificij tum commemorationem, tum applicationem.
units.tr: Thirdly: they do not distinguish between the sacrifice of the cross and the commemoration of that sacrifice, and its application.

units.la: Quartò: confundunt sacramentum cum sacrificio externo: cum tamen Sacramentum in genere latius pateat quàm sacrificiū: & vt quidem ab Ecclesiæ Christianæ Doctoribus vsurpatur, quædam sit inter Sacramentum & sacrificium oppositio: quandoquidem ea est sacrificij natura, vt à nobis aliquid offeratur Deo: at in Sacramentis noui Testamenti, summa Dei beneficia nobis offeruntur.
units.tr: Fourthly: they confuse the sacrament with an external sacrifice, although a sacrament in general has a wider range than a sacrifice. And, as the teachers of the Christian Church use the term, there is a certain opposition between sacrament and sacrifice: for it is the nature of a sacrifice that something is offered by us to God, whereas in the sacraments of the New Testament the greatest benefits of God are offered to us.

units.la: Quintò: non satis recte tenent vim ac naturam sacrificij spiritualis: adeò vt identidem externum cum interiori sacrificio confundant.
units.tr: Fifthly: they do not hold rightly enough to the force and nature of a spiritual sacrifice, so that again and again they confuse the external with the inward sacrifice.

units.la: Sextò: quæ Veteres minùs dilucidè & figuratè dixerunt de sacrificio, vt Cœnæ Dominicæ mysterium nobis commendarent: ea Pontificij arripiunt ad sui erroris confirmationem: non spectato Veterum ipsorum propósito: cùm deberent potius scripta Veterum ad amussim verbi diuini exigere, & ea Veterum testimonia præferre, quæ cum Prophetarū & Apostolorum scriptis conueniunt.
units.tr: Sixthly: what the ancients said about sacrifice less clearly and in figurative terms, in order to commend to us the mystery of the Lord's Supper, the Papists seize upon to confirm their own error, without regard to the purpose of the ancients themselves. Yet they ought rather to measure the writings of the ancients by the rule of the divine Word, and to prefer those testimonies of the Fathers which agree with the writings of the Prophets and Apostles.

units.la: Quæ cùm ita sint: cùm in disputatione καταςκευαςικὴ sententia nostram planis ex- presisque Scripturæ locis cófirmauerimus: Pontificiorum autem errores ἀνασκευαστικῇ disputatione refutauerimus, atque etiā absurdis & incommodis oppresserimus, denique ad eorum obiectiones,tum ex Scriptura,tum exVeteribus propositas,respondGerimus: ita discussa erroris caligine:nobis redit ea lux veritatis, quam initiò proposuimus, in Orthodoxæ & ex verbo Dei Reformatæ ac verè Catholicæ Ecclesiæ sententia conspiciendam: nempe: Christum esse solum Pontificem ac verè sacerdotem noui Testamenti: & eius sacrificium semel in cruce peractum, esse unicum, reale & externum sacrificium in Ecclesia Christiana: idemque unicum propitiatorium pro peccatis nostris.
units.tr: These things being so: since in the constructive part of our disputation we have confirmed our view by plain and express passages of Scripture, and in the refutative part of our disputation we have overturned the errors of the Papists and pressed them with absurdities and inconveniences, and finally have answered their objections, both those drawn from Scripture and those drawn from the ancients: the mist of error having thus been dispelled, there returns to us that light of truth which we set forth at the beginning, to be beheld in the judgment of the Orthodox Church, which is Reformed from the Word of God and truly Catholic, namely: that Christ is the only High Priest and truly the priest of the New Testament; and that his sacrifice, once accomplished on the cross, is the one, real and external sacrifice in the Christian Church, and the same is the one propitiation for our sins.

units.tr: FINIS.
